title: Three Japanese Visited At The Shanghai Telegraph Office At The Corner Of Foochow A Szechuan Roads

page_data.en:
FORM NO. 3
G. 500-11-37

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
File No.
CENTRAL STATION
No. D. 88/3/4
Date 22 - 12 - 1937

Subject (in full). Three Japanese visited at the Shanghai Telegraph Office
at the corner of Foochow & Szechuen Roads.
Made by... J.P.S.53... R.Okawa Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

Upon receiving instruction of Inspt.Brownrigg,
at about 11.15 a.m. to-day, I conducted enquiry re the heading
where no Japanese could be found.

One of the above Office staff states that three
Japanese visited the Office at about 11 a.m. to-day, and asked to
see some of cable maps which were shown him. Then they
left without any trouble. He also states that he did not
know anything about them as they were all in plainclothes,
and no explanation given.

J.F.C.165 taken by me. Yours obedient servant,

R. Okawa
J.P.S.53.R. Okawa

事由（全称）：三名日本人访问位于福州路与四川路拐角处的上海电报局。
制作人…… J.P.S.53…… R.Okawa（大川） 转呈人 [签名]

先生，

接到布朗里格（Brownrigg）巡官的指示后，
于今日上午约11时15分，我就上述标题事项进行了调查，
但未发现任何日本人。

该电报局的一名职员称，今日上午约11时，三名
日本人访问了该局，并要求查看一些电缆地图，地图已展示给他们看。随后他们
离开，未发生任何纠纷。他还表示，由于这些人皆身着便衣，
且未作任何解释，因此他对他们一无所知。

J.F.C.165 由我记录。 您顺从的仆人，

R. Okawa
J.P.S.53. R. Okawa

2.

Re Radio Broadcasting Station, Chinese
Government Radio Administration Sassoon
House, and Chinese Government Telegraph
Administration, 7C Foochow Road and
Central News Agency Telegraph.

Further to the previous report it was revealed that
at 11.30a.m. 27-11-37 a party of Japanese Consular
Officials and Japanese Imperial Telegraph Co. consisting
of five persons paid a visit to the Radio Broadcasting
Station escorted by the Shanghai Municipal Police and
took over control. In the afternoon negotiations
proceeded between the manager and Japanese Officials in
the Japanese Consulate General with a view to arriving
at a satisfactory settlement for the purpose of operation
and administration.

It was not ascertained whether the Japanese
Authorities had taken over other establishments to be
controlled or not.

Chengtu Road Station,

Date Nov. 29th, 1937.
Subject Western Branch of Shanghai Telegraph Office taken over by
Japanese authorities.
Made by ............ and ............ Forwarded by Inspector Everest

Sir,
At 4 p.m. November 28, 1937, Consul Ichikawa and ten
Japanese Consular Policemen, accompanied by two foreign Sergts.
and five Japanese Constables of the S.M.P., took over the
Western Branch of the Shanghai Telegraph Office at Nos. 149-151,
Lane 591, Bubbling Well Road.
No untoward incident occurred during the taking over of
the premises. The Chinese staff remained at their posts,
evidently according to arrangements previously made, and
business was carried on as usual.
The Radio Broadcasting Station of the same office at No.
29, Lane 58, Love Lane, was also visited by the Japanese
authorities at 4.15 p.m. the same day, but no attempt was made
to occupy the premises. The majority of the equipment appeared
to have been taken from the building, and, according to the
Chinese watchman left in charge, this was done several days
ago by the Chinese Staff.

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER (DIVISIONS)）

B. Everest
Officer in charge

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
Sintza Police Station,
REPORT
Date November 30, 1937

Subject Chinese Government Radio Station, 145 Markham
Road.

Made by and Forwarded by Inspector Perkins.

Sir,
I beg to report that at about 6.15 p.m. 28.11.37, I
received a telephone message from D.C. Divisions to the effect
that the Japanese authorities had visited the Chinese Government
Radio Station in Love Lane that afternoon with a police escort
and were now at the Radio Station in Markham Road.
He had been informed by Mr. Uehara that there was
some trouble there and instructed me to personally visit the
premises and find out about it. I immediately proceeded by car
to the Government Radio Station at 145 Markham Road and on my
arrival found Japanese Consular Authorities and a J.P.S. attached
to Hongkew Station conversing together in the west block of the
building, on the ground floor, where radio apparatus was installed.
I inquired of them as to the trouble and was informed by them
that there was no trouble and that they had not had any trouble.
I then left the premises.

At 8 p.m. 28.11.37, the following message was received
from the Sergeant on duty at Gordon Road Station.
"We have two Japanese policemen on duty in the
vicinity of Markham Road bridge, I don't know
what they are there for, but I think it is the
Wireless Station at Markham Road, near the bridge."
(Sd). F.S. Prince.

With reference to the above message, J.P.C.s have been
doing duty daily behind locked gates in the grounds of the
Chinese Government Radio Station at 145 Markham Road, together
with Japanese Consular Police.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
A. Perkins Insp.
Officer in charge.

D.C.DIV.

新闸捕房，
报告
日期 1937年11月30日

事由 中国政府广播电台，麦根路145号。

制作人及转呈人 珀金斯（Perkins）巡官。

先生，
谨此报告，1937年11月28日下午约6时15分，我
接到分区副总监的电话留言，称日本当局当天下午在警察护送下
访问了爱文义路的中国政府广播电台，目前正位于麦根路的
广播电台。
他从上原（Uehara）先生处得知那里出现了一些麻烦，并指示我
亲自前往该处查明情况。我立即乘车前往麦根路145号的
政府广播电台，到达后发现日本领事当局和一名隶属于虹口捕房的
日本巡捕（J.P.S.）正在大楼西侧底层安装无线电设备的房间内交谈。
我向他们询问麻烦之事，他们告知我并无麻烦，也未遇到任何问题。
随后我离开了该处。

1937年11月28日晚上8时，收到戈登路捕房值班警长的如下消息。
“我们有两名日本警察在麦根路桥附近执勤，我不
知道他们为何在那里，但我认为是为了麦根路靠近桥边的
无线电台。”
（签名）. F.S. Prince.

鉴于上述消息，日本警察（J.P.C.s）一直与中国领事警察一起，
每日在麦根路145号中国政府广播电台院内紧锁的大门后执勤。

先生，
您顺从的仆人，
A. Perkins 巡官
负责人。

分区副总监。

......Jinza...... Station,
REPORT
Date. Nov. 30. 19 37.

Subject Re examination and inspection of the Chinese Government
Radio station situated at No. 145 Markham Road by Japanese
Consular authorities.
Made by D.S. Eyestone. Forwarded by Insp. i/c.

Sir,
At 6.10 p.m. 30/11/37 a telephone message was received
from Mr. R.J. Miers D.D.O. Divisions reporting that the Japanese
authorities were inspecting the premises of the Chinese
Government Radio station situated at No. 145 Markham Road and
in doing so had met with opposition from the inmates.
On receipt of this information Inspt. Perkins, S.I.
Alexandroff, J.D.C. SIF and the undersigned immediately
proceeded to the building in question and on entering the
premises it was observed that a party of Japanese Consular
Officials escorted by a foreign sergeant and a Japanese
constable (S.M.P.) were inspecting the switchboards etc and
asking the Chinese members of the staff various questions
regarding the apparatus and working conditions.
It was then ascertained from the S.M.P. Uniform escort
that whilst examining the premises the Japanese Consular
Officials had not met with any opposition and the examination
was conducted without any incident whatsoever.
Inspt. Perkins conveyed the above information to his
superior officers.

D.S. Eyestone
D.S. 128

Sen. Det. i/c.

D.D.O. "B" Division.

广播电台进行检查和视察。
制作人 艾斯通（Eyestone）副巡官。 转呈人 负责巡官。

先生，
1937年11月30日下午6时10分，收到分区副总监
R.J. Miers 先生的电话报告，称日本当局正在视察位于麦根路145号的
中国政府广播电台场所，在此过程中遭到了内部人员的反对。
收到此信息后，珀金斯（Perkins）巡官、高级督察亚历山德罗夫（Alexandroff）、
J.D.C. SIF 及本人立即前往该大楼，进入场所后观察到，
一群由一名外籍警长和一名工部局警务处日本巡捕护送的
日本领事官员正在检查配电盘等，并向中方职员询问有关
设备和工作条件的各种问题。
随后从工部局警务处制服护卫处获悉，日本领事官员在检查
场所时并未遇到任何反对，检查过程未发生任何事件。
珀金斯巡官将上述信息传达给了他的上级官员。

D.S. Eyestone
副巡官 128

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
Station,
REPORT
Date Nov. 20th 193.
Subject Sino-British escorting party of J.F.C.s C3 and J.D.C.101 proceeding to Chinese Telegraph Offices.
Made by C.A.D.C.L.C.L. Forwarded by C/I Perry

Sir,
I refer to your memo of 20/11/31, re-
porting that J.F.C.s C3 and J.D.
C.101, are detailed to escort duty to escort the Con-
sular Police officers travelling in the Western
District. The party was under the command of the Chinese Tel-
egraph Office.

At 9.30 a.m., the party, consisting of Consular Police, ris-
ing from the Station, proceeded to the Chinese Telegraph Office,
via the Circular Road.

The party of Consular Police left
the Consulate riding in three i/Cars, the lead car taken by
Consular Police C-r...ic. was followed by the station car,
via the Circular Road about 10.30 a.m.

The above party of police first proceeded to the Chinese
Telegraph Office situated at No. 551 and 149 Bubbling Well
Road.

After negotiations between the Consular Police and the
Chinese Officers of the Telegraph Office, two Consular Police
officers and J.F.C.C3 were left in the office for duty.

There the rest were divided into two parties and one
party proceeded to the Telegraph Engineers' Office at 149
Markham Road and the other to the Engineers' Office at No.
144 Sinza Road, the former being escorted by J.F.C.56 and
J.F.C.213 and the latter by J.D.C.101.

At each of the two offices, two Consular officers were
posted and, by order of D.C.(J) Mr.Uehara, J.F.C.213 and J.D.
C.101 were also left for duty at the Markham Road Office and
the Sinza Road Office respectively.

上午9时30分，该小队由领事警察组成，从捕房出发，

领事警察小队乘坐三辆 i/Cars 离开领事馆，领头的车辆由

中国电信局。

经过领事警察与中国电信局官员的谈判，两名领事警察
官员和 J.F.C.C3 留在局内执勤。

其余人员分为两组，一组前往麦根路149号的电信工程师办公室，

J.F.C.213 护送，后者由 J.D.C.101 护送。

在这两个办公室，各部署了两名领事官员，并根据日本副总监（D.C.(J)）
上原（Uehara）先生的命令，J.F.C.213 和 J.D.
C.101 也分别留在麦根路办公室和新闸路办公室执勤。

furniture and effects for removal, it being intended

1937年12月16日上午11时15分，在静安寺路591弄149-151号交通部电报局值班的华捕巡长（C.P.C.）2108通过电话向成都路捕房报告，数名中国男子正在搬走财物。

华捕侦探警长（C.D.C.）213及本人赶赴现场，发现十一名中国男子正将家具和物品从大楼搬至院内。带队的一名曾先生（K.Y. Tseng）称，他接到该局经理的指示，准备搬运上述家具和物品，计划于1937年12月16日夜間将楼内所有物品搬走。上述十一人中，无人持有任何证明其有权进入大楼的凭证，也无人能出示任何文件表明其有权从大楼搬走任何物品，因此所有十一人均被带至捕房。

Police Station, Chengtu Road Branch,
Present.

Sir,

As we are compelled to stop our business
and most of the machines for radio-communication
purposes have once more been taken away from
our Wireless Division at No.149-161, Lane 591
on Bubbling Well Road by the Japanese, it is
hard for us at present to work for the public.

We now decide to remove the remaining articles
and furnitures from the above premises, and vacate
the house so as to save unessential expenses. Mr.
K.Y. Tseng, our engineer, is appointed to take
charge of the removal, together with several coolies
of this Office. It takes about one week to complete
the work commencing to-day.

Besides writing to T.M.C. attached with a
specified list of the machines, etc., which are
taken away by the Japanese, we now write you in
the hope that you will instruct your men to take
necessary steps for the protection of the removal.

Thanking you very much for the repeated troubles

Yours truly,

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

At 11.15 a.m. on the 30-11-37, Sub-Inspector Moffat whilst on patrol proceeded to Nos. 149/151, Lane No. 591 Bubbling Well Road, premises occupied by the Chinese Telegraph Office, Western Branch, at which address C.P.C. 151 was on duty, at which time he had noticed a black motor car nearby.

A later visit was also made, when C.P.C. 251 reported to the above officer, that several male Japanese in civilian clothes had entered the premises and had removed two radio instruments (presumably transmitters) and one coil of wire, which they had placed in a large sedan motor car, previously observed by Sub-Inspector Moffat, license number not obtained, and had them driven off.

The Japanese party were not accompanied by any uniform members of the S.M.P. and appeared to be working entirely alone.

No Chinese staff were present on the premises at the time of removal, all members of the telegraph staff having failed to return to duty since the 29-11-37.

Nothing of an untoward nature occurred during the removal of the property.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Damage Done to Japanese Owned Property.

At 1.45 p.m. on 6-11-37, a telephone message was received from a private watchman named Ah Zung Sung (白榕生), employed at Lane 59 Love Lane to the effect that 2 male Japanese had smashed a window at the Radio Station No. 29/58 Love Lane.

S.I. Moffat attended together with J.P.C. 214 and a number of the Japanese Consular Police, who were on duty at Lane 591 Bubbling Well Road. It was ascertained that they had tried to gain entry by breaking the window, but were unsuccessful because of there being iron bars inside the window.

They immediately drove off in a M/car, number etc. not obtained.

The watchman alleged the two unknown men were Japanese.

The Japanese Consular Police later informed this station that no Japanese subjects had been in the vicinity of the Radio Station at the time the window was smashed.

The above place ceased functioning as a Radio Station on 6-11-37 when a party of Japanese removed part of the Radio Equipment (Misc. 255/37). No one resides or works on the premises.

Made by // and Forwarded by Inspector Everest

Sir,
At 11.15 a.m. November 2., 1937, a quantity of miscel-
laneous radio equipment, including one receiving set and one
loud speaker, was taken away from the Chinese Government Radio
Broadcasting Station at No. 29, Lane 58, Love Lane by the
Japanese Authorities.
According to the private watchman employed in the lane,
thirteen Japanese in plain clothes and two in military
uniform wearing arm bands stating that they were military
police arrived at the place in three motor cars, and gained
entry to the premises by climbing the wall of the small court
yard.
No report of the removal of the equipment was made
through official channels.

D.S. McHardy

Subject Western Branch of Shanghai Telegraph Office taken over by

Made by and Forwarded by Inspector Everest

Sir,
At 4 p.m. November 28, 1937, Consul Ichikawa and ten
Japanese Consular Policemen, accompanied by two Foreign Sergts.
and five Japanese Constables of the S.M.P., took over the
Western Branch of the Shanghai Telegraph Office at Nos. 149-151,
Lane 591, Bubbling Well Road.
No untoward incident occurred during the taking over of
the premises. The Chinese staff remained at their posts,
evidently according to arrangements previously made, and
business was carried on as usual.
The Radio Broadcasting Station of the same office at No.
29, Lane 58, Love Lane, was also visited by the Japanese
authorities at 4.15 p.m. the same day, but no attempt was made
to occupy the premises. The majority of the equipment appear-
ed to have been taken from the building, and, according to the
Chinese watchman left in charge, this was done several days
ago by the Chinese Staff.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Alleged Illegal operating of a Radio Transmitter.
At 10a.m. 6/12/37, D.S. Henchman attached to Special Branch H.Q. came to this station requesting assistance to visit the Burlington Hotel, B'Tell Road where, according to their information, a Radio Transmitter formerly operated by the Pan-American Air-Ways Ltd. was at present used by the Chinese Government.
The above address was visited and the operators, located in room No. 407, stated they had been employed by an American Mr. Max Polin of room 306 Dollar Bldg., Canton Road, but enquiries by the Special Branch showed that the American Consulate had no knowledge of the transmitter.
The operators were advised by D.S. Henchman to cease operating the transmitter pending verification of its legal standing. A C.D.C. was left on the premises to see that the transmitter was not used.
At 4.55p.m. even date D.S. Henchman informed the undersigned by telephone that it had been ascertained that the transmitter belonged to an American concern and there being no objection to its operating, the C.D.C. could be withdrawn.
This was done accordingly.

同日午后4时55分，Henchman 侦探警佐通过电话告知签署人，经查证该发射机属于一家美国公司，对其运行并无异议，因此可以撤回华人侦探警员。

Sir,
At 10.10 a.m. 30/11/37, a party of Japanese Military
and Consular Police in plain clothes accompanied by Japanese
Constable of the S.M.P. took over the Radio Station of the
Chinese Telegraphic Administration, Ministry of Communications,
at 1446 Sinza Road. As all the employees, with the exception
of two coolies, had already evacuated the premises, a guard
consisting of two Japanese in plain clothes and one J.P.C.
was left there. It is not known whether the Japanese authori-
ties intend to operate the station, but I understand that
most of the moveable machinery had been previously removed.

D. S. I.

December 1, 1937.

Special Branch, S.M.P.

We beg to inform you that we, the Hwa Mei
Electrical Shop, operate a radio station for broadcasting
amusement and cultural programmes as well as for
advertising, the funds of which are the charges for
advertisements from patrons. Recently, owing to business
depression, financial difficulties have been experienced.

functioning temporarily, until such time when business

REPORT
Date May 4, 19 40.

Subject. Ming Shing Broadcasting Station - change of wavelength.

Made by D.S.I. McAdie Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

The Ming Shing (民聲) Broadcasting Station,
X.L.H.O., K.C. 1420, 819 Nanking Road (Swedish),
changed its wavelength to K.C. 1320 with effect from
May 1, 1940.

It is to be noted that K.C. 1320 was formerly
used by Young's Broadcasting Station (defunct),
and was recently taken up by the North China Daily
News Broadcasting Station. The latter station
commenced trial broadcasts about the 20th of April
but went off the air on April 27, following persistent
interference believed to have been emanated from a
certain section of the Japanese military.

The Li-ng Yue (兩友) Broadcasting Station,
454 Nanking Road, X.I.C.T., K.C. 1460 (Swiss), on
May 2nd changed its wavelength to K.C. 1420, the
former wavelength of the Ming Shing Station.

Both the Ming Shing and Liang Yue Broadcasting
Stations are registered with the Japanese Broadcasting
Superintendent's Office, Hardoon Building, Nanking
Road and it is believed that the change of wavelength,
if not ordered, was at least suggested by the latter.

In neither case was the change of frequency reported
to the Municipal Police.

(印：SHANGHAI COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 2 MAY 1940)

D. S. I.

Date January 12, 1938

Subject Letter from Mr. Holdo Stromwall (Swedish) applying
for permission to establish a Broadcasting Station
call sign (XMHO) K.C.1420.

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford

The attached letter from Mr. Holdo Stromwall
(Swedish), 391 Kiangse Road, applying for permission to
establish a Commercial Broadcasting Radio Station (XMHO)
K.C.1420 in the Settlement, was handed in to the Special
Branch together with attached certificate from the
Chancellor-in-Charge, Royal Swedish Consulate-General,
by Mr. Stromwall at 11.30 a.m. January 12, 1938.

Mr. Stromwall was informed that the Police would
neither grant nor withhold permission for the establishment
of his station. He stated that he was negotiating with
the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office as he
did not wish to experience any trouble with the latter.

Shanghai, 11th January 1939.

The Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch)
S. M. P. Headquarters,
Foochow Road,
Local.

Dear Sir,

I hereby take the liberty to inform you that I intend
to open a Broadcasting Station for commercial purposes in the
International Settlement. The station will operate under the
letter XMHO and broadcast on a frequency of 1420 kc. which I
understand is vacant. The languages used will be:

ENGLISH for the Scandinavians listeners since
many of them do not speak our languages, and
CHINESE from whom the main source of income from
advertisements will be derived for a start at least.

I append a document from the Swedish Consulate General
from which you will see that they are fully supporting my scheme.

I shall be glad if you will let me know if, when and
where I will have to file future applications to make the for-
malities complete in regard to the registration of my proposed
Broadcasting Station.

Thanking you in advance,

I remain, Dear Sir,

Your's faithfully

H.S/T.

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.I.

The attached letter from Mr. Holdo Stromwall
(Swedish), 391 Kiangse Road, applying for permission to
establish a Commercial Broadcasting Radio Station (XMHO)
K.C.1420 in the Settlement, was handed in to the Special
Branch together with attached certificate from the
Chancellor-in-Charge, Royal Swedish Consulate-General,
by Mr. Stromwall at 11.30 a.m. January 12, 1938.

Mr. Stromwall was informed that the Police would
neither grant nor withhold permission for the establishment
of his station. He stated that he was negotiating with
the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office as he
did not wish to experience any trouble with the latter.
Further, that he hoped to be ready to commence broadcasting
by the end of January and would inform the Police of the
address of the station as soon as he is ready to operate.

Date December 19, 19 37.
Subject Closure of radio station at Burlington Hotel.
Made by D. S. Henchman Forwarded by C. Crawford. S. J.

In accordance with the instructions of the D. C.
(Special Branch) appended to the attached file, at 12.30 p.m.,
December 18, 1937, members of the Special Branch, accompanied
by representatives from Bubbling Well Station, visited the
radio station located in Room 407 of the Burlington Hotel
and informed the occupants that further operation of the
installation would not be permitted. The radio transmitter
was disconnected and a C.D.C. from Bubbling Well Station
was posted to ensure that activities were not resumed.
Mr. S. C. Hsu, who resides in the French Concession,
was informed by telephone of the closure of the station.
The undersigned received two telephone messages, one
from a Chinese who stated that he was speaking on behalf
of Pan-American Airways and one from a Mr. Nelson who
stated that he was Mr. Polin's attorney. Both the above
mentioned persons requested that Police reconsider their
action and suggested that discussions on the matter should
be reopened. Should the equipment be removed steps
have been taken to ascertain its destination.

The Secretary-General:

Major Gerrard has left with me some further
papers in connection with the wireless station at the
Burlington Hotel.

You will note from the latest report that
foreign supervision has ceased and that Major Bourne
recommends that the Police should close the station down
inasmuch as they have no control. I am myself inclined
to agree. I think the continued existence of this station
is dangerous. You might, however, think that perhaps
the specific wishes of the Japanese authorities should
be obtained.

Certified true copy:

IW/.
page_data.zh:
静安寺路伯灵顿酒店运营的
无线电发射机。

收到消息称，位于静安寺路伯灵顿酒店、此前由泛美航空有限公司（Pan-American Airways, Limited）运营的无线电发射机，正被中国政府特工用于维持上海与汉口之间的通信。

page_data.en:
I. E P O R T
- - - - - -

RADIO STATION AT BURLINGTON
HOTEL.
- - - - - - - - - -

In accordance with instructions of
E.O. (Special Branch) the Burlington Hotel,
Bubbling Well Road, was visited on the morn-
ing of December 6, 1937. Enquiries from
the management elicited the information that
a Radio Station operated from Room 407 of the
hotel. When this room was visited a radio
transmitter and receiving set were discovered.
Two Chinese operators were in charge of the
installation and when questioned as to the
purpose of the station, referred the under-
signed to Mr. H.S. Polin, U.S.A. citizen.

Mr. Polin, who is a director of China
Airways, an American Company, was interviewed
and gave the following explanation -: The Radio
Station at the Burlington Hotel, he stated, was
operated jointly by China Airways and by China
National Aviation Corporation, a Chinese concern
with Headquarters at 314, Avenue du Roi Albert
(vide D.6813/14) and Mr. T.J. Ho as Shanghai
manager. China Airways is responsible for the
Pan-American Airways Co.'s business affairs in
China. Pan-American Airways hold a 45% share
in C.N.A.C. - hence their interest in the station
at the Burlington Hotel. Mr. Polin went on to
explain that the Radio Station was used for
commercial purposes only and was in constant con-
tact with stations on the Yangtse Valley and
Hankow. Messages concerning movements of airplanes
on the Hankow-Chungking runs, as well as other
page_data.zh:
报 告
- - - - - -

伯灵顿酒店
的广播电台。
- - - - - - - - - -

根据特别处执行官（E.O.）的指令，于1937年12月6日上午探访了静安寺路的伯灵顿酒店。向管理层查询后获悉，酒店407室运营着一个广播电台。当探访该房间时，发现了一台无线电发射机和接收机。两名中国操作员负责该设备，当被问及电台的目的时，他们将签署人引荐给美国公民 H.S. 波林先生（Mr. H.S. Polin）。

波林先生是美国公司中国航空公司（China Airways）的董事，接受面谈并作出如下解释：他指出，伯灵顿酒店的广播电台由中国航空公司和中国航空公司（China National Aviation Corporation，一家中国公司，总部设在阿尔贝国王大道314号（见 D.6813/14），上海经理为何德奎（T.J. Ho）先生）共同运营。中国航空公司负责泛美航空公司在中国的业务事务。泛美航空公司持有中国航空公司45%的股份——因此他们在伯灵顿酒店的电台拥有利益。波林先生接着解释说，该广播电台仅用于商业目的，并与长江流域和汉口的电台保持恒定联系。关于汉口-重庆航线的飞机移动消息，以及其他

page_data.en:
- 2 -

information regarding commercial air-traffic, were
transmitted and received; no business of a polit-
ical or military nature, he stated, was conducted.
As evidence of his good faith, Mr. Palin said that
he would be prepared to allow the Police to instal
their own censor at the Radio Station.

The foregoing explanation does not make
it entirely clear whether the American or the Chinese
Company is responsible for the operation of the
station; it appears, however, that as the Pan-American
Shanghai-Canton run is suspended, the station is used
mainly to transmit and receive C.N.A.C. messages for
Hankow and the Yangtsze Valley.

There is no evidence, as yet, that the
station is being used by Chinese Government agents
and it has not, therefore, been called on to suspend
operations. A C.D.C. from Bubbling Well Station has,
however, been installed pending further instructions.

The station operates on a wavelength of
5769 kilocycles and uses alternate call signs :
X.S.A./3 ... X/28.

Certified true copy:
• • • • • • • • • •

TW/.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

有关商业空中交通的信息，均被发送和接收；他表示，不进行任何政治或军事性质的业务。为了证明其诚意，帕林先生（Mr. Palin，原文如此，应为Polin）表示，他愿意允许警方在广播电台安装他们自己的审查员。

上述解释并未完全阐明是由美国公司还是中国公司负责电台的运营；然而，看来由于泛美航空上海-广州航线暂停，该电台主要用于为中国航空公司发送和接收发往汉口及长江流域的电文。

目前尚无证据表明该电台正被中国政府特工使用，因此尚未要求其停止运营。然而，静安寺路警局的一名中国籍巡长（C.D.C.）已被派驻于此，以待进一步指示。

该电台工作在5769千周波长上，并使用交替呼号：
X.S.A./3 ... X/28。

认证真实副本：
• • • • • • • • • •

TW/.

page_data.en:
R E P O R T
- - - - -
RADIO STATION AT BURLINGTON
HOTEL.

With reference to the notes of the
D.C. (Special Branch) appended to the attached
report, Mr. Stanton of the U.S. Consulate when
interviewed stated that in the event of police
closing down the radio station at Room 407,
Burlington Hotel, the U.S. authorities would
not interfere. He pointed out, however, that
the question of ownership of the equipment
might arise. This equipment, he said, was be-
lieved to be the property of Pan-American Airways,
U.S. Company.

Inquiries to establish the ownership of
the installation at the Burlington Hotel have
proved unsatisfactory, Mr. Polin stating that
although he is of the opinion that the transmitter
and receiver are Pan-American Airways' property,
he cannot definitely say that such is the case.

Further reliable information concerning
the nature of the messages transmitted by the station
in question is to the effect that without Mr. Polin's
knowledge, news items have been broadcast.

In accordance with instructions, the C.D.C.
previously posted at Room 407, Burlington Hotel, has
been withdrawn pending further enquiries.

Certified true copy.
IW/.
page_data.zh:
报 告
- - - - -
伯灵顿酒店
的广播电台。

关于附呈报告中特别处副督察长（D.C.）所附的笔记，美国领事馆的斯坦顿先生（Mr. Stanton）在接受面谈时表示，如果警方关闭伯灵顿酒店407室的广播电台，美国当局不会干涉。然而，他指出，设备的所有权问题可能会出现。他说，据信该设备是美国公司泛美航空公司的财产。

为确定伯灵顿酒店设备所有权的调查结果并不令人满意，波林先生表示，虽然他认为发射机和接收机是泛美航空公司的财产，但他不能肯定地说情况确实如此。

关于涉案电台所发电文性质的进一步可靠消息显示，在波林先生不知情的情况下，新闻项目已被广播。

根据指令，此前派驻在伯灵顿酒店407室的中国籍巡长（C.D.C.）已被撤回，以待进一步调查。

认证真实副本。
IW/.

Made by ...D.S. Henchman................Forwarded by...C. Crawford D.S.

In accordance with instructions of J.C. (Special
Branch) the Burlington Hotel, Bubbling Well Road, was visited
on the morning of December 6, 1937. Enquiries from the
management elicited the information that a radio station
operated from Room 407 of the hotel. When this room was
visited a radio transmitter and receiving set were discovered.
Two Chinese operators were in charge of the installation and
when questioned as to the purpose of the station, referred
the undersigned to Mr. W.S. Polin, U.S.A. citizen.
Mr. Polin, who is a director of China Airways,
an American company, was interviewed and gave the following
explanation: The radio station at the Burlington Hotel,
he stated, was operated jointly by China Airways and by
China National Aviation Corporation, a Chinese concern
with headquarters at 314 Avenue du Roi Albert (vide D.6813/14)
and Mr. T.J. Ho as Shanghai manager. China Airways is
responsible for the Pan-American Airways Co.'s business
affairs in China. Pan-American Airways hold a 45% share
in C.N.A.C. - hence their interest in the station at the
Burlington Hotel. Mr. Polin went on to explain that the
radio station was used for commercial purposes only and
was in constant contact with stations on the Yangtse Valley
and Hankow. Messages concerning movements of airplanes
on the Hankow-Chunking runs, as well as other information
regarding commercial air-traffic, were transmitted and
received; no business of a political or military nature, he
stated, was conducted. As evidence of his good faith, Mr.
Polin said that he would be prepared to allow the Police to
instal their own censor at the radio station.

（批：P.A.
I shall take
U.S. Authorities
unofficial opinion
a comment if I
am prepared to
give it.
MB
- 8 DEC 1937）

根据特务科助理总监（J.C.）的指令，于1937年12月6日上午走访了位于静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）的礼查饭店。向管理层查询后获悉，该饭店407房间设有一个无线电台。走访该房间时，发现了一台无线电发射机和一套接收装置。两名中国操作员负责管理该设备，当被问及电台用途时，他们将询问者引荐给美国公民 W.S. Polin 先生。
Polin 先生是美国公司中国航空公司（China Airways）的董事，他接受了问询并作出如下解释：他说，礼查饭店的无线电台由中国航空公司和中国国家航空公司（China National Aviation Corporation，一家总部设在阿尔贝王大道314号的中国企业，见 D.6813/14，上海经理为何德奎 T.J. Ho 先生）共同运营。中国航空公司负责泛美航空公司在中国的业务事务。泛美航空公司持有中国国家航空公司45%的股份——因此他们对礼查饭店的电台感兴趣。Polin 先生接着解释说，该电台仅用于商业目的，并与长江流域和汉口的电台保持持续联系。有关汉口-重庆航线飞机飞行的消息，以及其他关于商业航空交通的信息，均在此收发；他说，不进行任何政治或军事性质的业务。为了证明他的诚意，Polin 先生说，他准备允许警方在无线电台安装他们自己的检查员。

（批：P.A.

The foregoing explanation does not make it entirely
clear whether the American or the Chinese company is
responsible for the operation of the station; it appears,
however, that as the Pan-American Shanghai-Canton run is
suspended, the station is used mainly to transmit and
receive C.N.A.C. messages for Hankow and the Yangtse Valley.
There is no evidence, as yet, that the station
is being used by Chinese government agents and it has not,
therefore, been called on to suspend operations. A C.D.C.
from Bubbling Well station has, however, been installed
pending further instructions.
The station operates on a wavelength of 5769
kilocycles and uses alternate call signs: X.S.A./3, X/28.

目前尚无证据表明该电台正被中国政府特工使用，因此尚未要求其停止运营。然而，来自静安寺路巡捕房的一名中国侦探队（C.D.C.）人员已部署到位，以待进一步指令。

Translation of Radiogram

To M. D. Copy Chen Secretary Chungking, Rush.

We intend to remove our office to the
Burlington Hotel and to sublet the shop-premises
of the downstairs portion of the house occupied by
our office at 314 Avenue du Roi Albert. This has been
approved by you, vide radiogram dated November 1st
from the Secretariat at Chungking.

Upon learning that we are going to sub-let
the shop premises, the Shanghai Postal Remittance
and Savings Bank is causing interferences. In consequence,
we have discussed the matter with the rent agent
the Fluner & Company who state that it will be better
for the Head Office to send a telegraphic notification
to the Shanghai Postal Remittance and Savings Bank.
We therefore suggest that the following radiogram be
dispatched to us:-
page_data.zh:
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处
S. G. 登记处
S. B. D. 15/3 / 37）

电报译文

致 M. D. 抄送陈秘书 重庆，加急。

我们打算将办事处迁至礼查饭店，并将我们位于阿尔贝王大道314号办事处所在楼房的下层店面转租。此举已获您批准，见重庆秘书处11月1日电报。

得知我们将转租店面后，上海邮汇局正在进行干扰。因此，我们与租赁代理福勒纳公司（Fluner & Company）讨论了此事，他们表示最好由总公司向上海邮汇局发送电报通知。因此，我们建议向我们发送以下电报：-

page_data.en:
-2-
" For the sake of safety, you are hereby instructed
to remove the office to some other place.and to sub-let
the shop premises of the downstairs portion of the
present house in order to make both ends meet.
Please notify the Postal Remittance and Savings
Bank accordingly."
This appears necessary in order to avoid
the misunderstanding of the Bank in question.
Yoh Jing Jui, December 19th, 1940.
page_data.zh:
-2-
“出于安全考虑，现指令你们
将办事处迁往其他地方，并将
现住房楼下部分的店面转租，
以维持收支平衡。
请据此通知邮汇局。”
为避免相关银行产生误解，
此举似乎很有必要。
姚景瑞，1940年12月19日。

Subject Shanghai International Radio Office - gratuities.

Made by D.S. Henchman Forwarded by C Crawford L.J

At 11.20 a.m. January 26, 1938, approximately
150 of the 180 ex-employees of the Shanghai International
Radio Office visited the Chung Wei Bank, 16 Rue de la
Porte du Nord, where in Room 608 the International Radio
Office has set up its temporary headquarters. The
employees who were interviewed by Mr. Loo Chung-tseng
(盧宗澄), demanded in addition to the issue of retiring
gratuities, the payment of a repatriation allowance of
$50 per man. In reply to this demand, Mr. Loo stated that
while he had received instructions to issue a gratuity
of 3 months' wages, the Ministry of Communications had
not informed him concerning the payment of a repatriation
allowance. At this the employees expressed their
dissatisfaction and adopted an attitude so threatening
that it became necessary to call upon the French Police
to disperse them.

The workers then re-assembled at 69 Avenue du Roi
Albert, branch office of International Radio Office, and
once more submitted their demands. Receiving no reply they
remained on the premises until 7 p.m. when again the police
were called on to disperse them.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 22 JAN 1938）

Subject Mackay Radio - operation in conjunction with
Japanese authorities.

Made by D.S. Henchman Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.I.

Using equipment, the property of the Chinese
Ministry of Communications and recently seized by the
Japanese, the Mackay Radio Company in co-operation
with members of the Japanese Ministry of Communications
is operating the radio transmitters located at 314
Medhurst Road. Communication is maintained, it is
stated, with Manila and Batavia and a much curtailed
service is offered to the public through the receiving
office of the former C.G.R.A. at Jinkee Road. The
truth of the statement that in operating thus the
Mackay Radio Company is guilty of contravention of
certain agreements with the Chinese Ministry of
Communications, is however open to debate.

In connection with the foregoing it is of interest
to note that when the management of the C.G.R.A.
Shanghai Office was taken over by R.C.A. in July of
this year, it was agreed that the latter company should
be permitted to nominate a company or companies with
whom the administration of the Chinese Office in Shanghai
should be shared. Mackay Radio and a French concern
were the companies chosen. This arrangement entailed
only the management of C.G.R.A.; equipment and staff
both being found and financed by the Chinese Ministry
of Communications.

Following the hostilities around Shanghai and the
taking over of the C.G.R.A. by the Japanese, a split
occurred between Mackay Radio and R.C.A. R.C.A., it
appears, desired to acquire sole controlling rights in

据称，麦基无线电公司使用属于中国交通部、近期被日军缴获的设备，并与日本通信省成员合作，运营位于梅赫斯特路（Medhurst Road）314号的无线电发射台。据悉，该公司与马尼拉和巴达维亚保持通信联络，并通过前中央广播电台管理局（C.G.R.A.）位于金奇路（Jinkee Road）的接收站向公众提供大幅缩减的服务。然而，关于麦基无线电公司以这种方式运营违反了与中国交通部某些协议的说法，其真实性的确值得商榷。

鉴于上述情况，值得注意的是，今年七月当美国无线电公司（R.C.A.）接管中央广播电台管理局（C.G.R.A.）上海办事处管理权时，双方曾达成协议，允许后者提名一家或多家公司，共同分担中国方面在上海办事处的行政管理。麦基无线电公司和一家法国公司是被选中的公司。这一安排仅涉及中央广播电台管理局的管理工作；设备和人员均由中国交通部提供并资助。

随着上海周边战事的爆发以及日本对中央广播电台管理局的接管，麦基无线电公司与美国无线电公司之间发生了分裂。看来，美国无线电公司希望获得对中央广播电台管理局（即后来的“国际无线电台”）的独家控制权，

而日本当局则倾向于成立一个国际委员会，并得到麦基无线电公司的支持。起初美国无线电公司取得了成功，但当中国员工拒绝继续操作时，“国际无线电台”被迫停止运作。随后，在日本人的协助下，麦基无线电公司利用其外部线路，开始使用从日本派来的雇员维持一种最低限度的服务。在中国员工复工之前，这项服务必须保持缩减状态；鉴于这些员工已领取当月工资，并期望领取二月和三月的工资，他们复工的可能性不大。另一个阻碍是，大量中央广播电台管理局的设备位于法租界内，据悉，法国当局拒绝允许将这些设备移出，也拒绝允许日本人操作这些设备。显然，能够全面恢复中央广播电台管理局此前提供的服务的唯一解决方案，是中国政府接受上海的事实地位，并同意由一个国际委员会运营无线电通信。据报道，旨在实现这一目标的谈判已经尝试进行，但迄今尚未成功。

Japanese Resume
Wireless Service

Messages Of Mackay
Sent; Transmitters
Of CGRA Used

International radio communica-
tions which were resumed some
days ago by Mackay Radio are
being sent via Japanese-controlled
transmitters, but the company
states that no official notice of
censorship has been received.
Transmitters XOB and XGL,
taken by the Japanese from the
former Avenue Road station of
the Chinese Government Radio
Administration shortly after they
took over Chinese government
functions here, are reportedly used
in sending the messages.

It is understood that messages
are being relayed by Japan-
ese from Shanghai to Manila,
Osaka, Dutch East Indies and
Hongkong. R.C.A. Communica-
tions has not yet resumed declin-
ing to file its messages with the
Nipponese operated system.
Messages are still received from
America by the firm, however,
being sent to Manila or Hongkong
by radio and relayed by cable to
Shanghai.

After Mackay Radio received a
notification from the Chinese
Government stating that owing to
force majeure it was unable to
continue operation of the radio
service from Shanghai, the com-
pany felt at liberty to handle
service from this city in any man-
ner which it could arrange.

Mackay Radio is "not concern-
ed" with the question of what
equipment is used in sending
messages from Shanghai, being
only interested in keeping the
service in operation. An official of
the company stated that he did
not know whether his messages
were being sent by transmitters
which the Japanese had confiscat-
ed from the Avenue Road station
although the frequency was the
same as that of XOB and XGL,
former Chinese government own-
ed stations.

As far as could be learned to-
day, none of the former Chinese
employees of the radio adminis-
tration are working for the
Japanese. All have been paid for
January and are expected to re-
ceive pay for February as well.

日本人恢复
无线服务

麦基发送讯息；
使用中央广播电台
管理局的发射机

几天前由麦基无线电公司恢复的国际无线电通信，正通过受日本控制的发射机发送，但该公司表示未收到任何官方审查通知。据悉，用于发送讯息的发射机是 XOB 和 XGL，这两台发射机是日本人在接管此地的中国政府职能后不久，从前大西路（Avenue Road）的中国政府无线电管理局站台缴获的。

据了解，讯息正由日本人从上海中继至马尼拉、大阪、荷属东印度和香港。美国无线电通信公司（R.C.A. Communications）尚未恢复服务，因其拒绝将其讯息提交给由日本人运营的系统。不过，该公司仍接收来自美国的讯息，这些讯息通过无线电发送至马尼拉或香港，再通过电缆中继至上海。

在麦基无线电公司收到中国政府通知，称因不可抗力无法继续从上海运营无线电服务后，该公司认为可以自由以任何其能安排的方式处理来自本市的业务。

麦基无线电公司对“使用何种设备从上海发送讯息”的问题“不感兴趣”，只关心保持服务运营。该公司一名官员表示，他不知道其讯息是否正由日本人从大西路站台没收的发射机发送，尽管频率与前中国政府所有的 XOB 和 XGL 电台相同。

据今日所知，前无线电管理局的中国雇员中无人受雇于日本人。所有人均已领取一月份工资，并预计也将领取二月份工资。

Mackay Radio
Service To
U.S. Resumes

Radio communications to the
United States, through their station
in Manila, have been established by
Mackay Radio, it was learned last
night from an official of the com-
pany.
Denial was made at the same
time of reports appearing in a local
Chinese evening paper that the
company's contract with the Minis-
try of Communications has been
violated, the official pointing out
that when C.G.R.A. service was
officially suspended due to force
majeure by the Ministry, under the
terms of the contract, the terms
of the agreement, the official con-
tinued, provide that when condi-
tions arise preventing a continua-
tion of the service from Shanghai
the company is at liberty to handle
its traffic from Shanghai "in the
best way suited to the public in-
terest."
Because further interruptions in
the cable service out of Shanghai
were thought possible in the future,
it was deemed advisable, the official
said, to open a circuit to the United
States even though it was necessary
under prevailing conditions to relay
messages through Manila.
Tariffs remain unchanged, being
identical for all cable and radio
services accepting messages here for
transmission abroad, he said.
Reports in a Chinese paper that
an offer had been made by Mackay
Radio to purchase C.G.R.A. were
also emphatically denied. Resump-
tion of radio communications to the
United States was effected nearly
a week ago.

D. S. Henderson SMC .91

670

麦基无线电
恢复对美
服务

昨晚从该公司一名官员处获悉，麦基无线电公司已通过其在马尼拉的站台建立了通往美国的无线电通信。
该官员同时否认了当地一家中文晚报上出现的报道，即该公司违反了与交通部的合同。该官员指出，当交通部以不可抗力为由正式暂停中央广播电台管理局的服务时，根据合同条款——该官员继续说道——协议规定，当出现阻碍从上海继续提供服务的情况时，公司有权以“最符合公共利益的方式”处理其来自上海的流量。
该官员称，由于考虑到未来上海的电报服务可能会进一步中断，因此认为开通一条通往美国的电路是明智之举，尽管在现有条件下有必要通过马尼拉中继讯息。
他说，费率保持不变，与所有在此接受讯息并向国外传输的电报和无线电服务相同。
中文报纸上关于麦基无线电公司提出购买中央广播电台管理局的报道也遭到断然否认。对美无线电通信的恢复是在近一周前实现的。

Dear Sirs:

As you are doubtless aware, the Shanghai International Radio Office (formerly the C.G.R.A.) has been taken over by the Japanese, with all furniture and equipment. The Japanese Officials told us they would take over, and pay, all obligations of the Shanghai International Radio Office, including the rent, light, taxes etc.

We are notifying you, as you will doubtless wish to make some arrangement with the Japanese so that the amounts due to you for rates and taxes on these premises will be paid during the time these premises are occupied by the Japanese.

The premises now occupied by the Japanese include our offices and operating rooms in Sassoon House, and our transmitting station at Avenue and Medhurst Roads.

The Japanese notified us that they had taken control of all of the premises on January 3.

As you know, the Shanghai International Radio Office would like to protect its furniture and equipment on the premises, and no payment has been made by the Japanese for the same; and we have only a letter from the Japanese Consul General that the Japanese Military Authorities are taking active control of the international radio stations, equipment and offices.

We requested you, as the police authority in the International Settlement of Shanghai, to protect this property and prevent its removal. We have a contract, dated July 7, 1937, with the Ministry of Communications of the National Government of the Republic of China, whereby the offices, stations and equipment of the International Radio Central were turned over to R.C. A. Communications, Inc., to be held in its custody and control (for operation of the C.G.R.A. and the Shanghai International Radio Office) as security for some U.S. $450,000.00 due from the Ministry to RCA, until such time as these debts are liquidated.

Very truly yours,

George F. Shecklen.

想必贵方已知悉，上海国际无线电台（前身为中华无线电管理局）已被日本人接管，所有家具和设备均在其内。日本官员告知我们，他们将接管并支付上海国际无线电台的所有债务，包括租金、电费、税款等。

特此通知贵方，因为贵方无疑希望与日方做出某种安排，以便在这些场所被日方占用期间，支付欠付贵方的这些场所的捐税和税款。

目前被日方占用的场所包括我们在沙逊大厦的办公室和报务室，以及位于爱文义路（Avenue Road）和麦赫斯特路（Medhurst Road）的我们的发射台。

日方通知我们，他们已于1月3日控制了所有这些场所。

如贵方所知，上海国际无线电台希望保护其留在这些场所内的家具和设备，而日方并未为此支付任何款项；我们仅有一封来自日本总领事的信函，称日本军事当局正在积极控制国际无线电台站、设备和办公室。

我们请求贵方作为上海公共租界的警务当局，保护这些财产并防止其被搬走。我们与中华民国国民政府交通部签订有一份日期为1937年7月7日的合同，据此，国际无线电中央台的办公室、台站和设备已移交给美国无线电通讯公司（R.C.A. Communications, Inc.），由其保管和控制（用于运营中华无线电管理局和上海国际无线电台），作为交通部欠付美国无线电通讯公司约45万美元债务的担保，直至这些债务清偿为止。

January 8, 1938. Morning Translation.

Ta Kei Wan Pao Morning Edition and other local newspapers :-

THE JAPANESE AUTHORITIES AND THE TELEGRAPHS

Owing to the suspension of operations by the Shanghai International Radio Office and the damage to the cables connecting Shanghai with Hongkong and Manila, Shanghai is now in direct telegraphic communication with Japan only. All messages for Hongkong and Manila have to be sent to Japan by cable, from Japan to Vladivostock, from Vladivostok to London via the U.S.S.R., and from London to Hongkong or Manila. The fee charged is $2.85 per word as compared with $0.20 per word for messages from Shanghai to Hongkong at normal times. In view of the danger of a total disruption of telegraphic communications, certain private bodies here are planning to establish an emergency radio communication organ for the purpose of maintaining direct communication with Hongkong and Manila from where messages can be relayed to other parts of the world.

The cables of the Great Northern and the Pacific Companies running to Hongkong and Manila respectively were damaged at sea on January 6. The Great Northern line is broken off the South China coast and the Pacific line near Formosa. A cable repairing ship is attending to the damage at Hongkong after which it will repair the damage at Formosa.

As all messages have now to pass through Japan, the Japanese censors here are not very strict. Cablegrams however are subject to severe censorship in Japan.

The censorship of cablegrams by the Japanese authorities has been reported to their respective Consulates at Shanghai by the Great Eastern, the Great Northern and the Pacific Companies, but up to the present no action has been taken by the Consulates.

It is reported that the three companies have also telegraphed the Ministry of Communications of the Chinese Government at Changsha explaining their inability to prevent the unexpected turn of affairs. The General Manager of the Great Northern Telegraph Company stated that the agreement signed between the company and the Ministry of Communications will continue to be effective despite the present situation. The annual sum paid by the company to the Ministry will be put on record. Up to yesterday morning, the Japanese censors had not detained any message, but in case a message is detained, the company will refund the charges on request.

The Great Eastern Telegraph Company employs a Chinese staff of 50 persons, the Great Northern Company has 50, and the Pacific Company has 20. At present Japanese officials are stationed in the traffic departments of the companies, where only foreigners are employed. The Chinese employees are attached to the receiving and dispatching offices. A meeting has been held by the Chinese staffs at which it was resolved to remain in the companies' service until such time as the Japanese should interfere with the administration of the companies, in which event they would walk out.

1938年1月8日。晨间译稿。

《大基湾报》晨报版及其他本地报纸：-

日本当局与电报

由于上海国际无线电台停止运营，以及连接上海与香港和马尼拉的电缆受损，上海目前仅与日本保持直接电报通信。所有发往香港和马尼拉的电讯必须通过电缆发送至日本，从日本至海参崴，经苏联从海参崴至伦敦，再从伦敦至香港或马尼拉。收费标准为每字2.85美元，而平时上海至香港的电讯收费为每字0.20美元。鉴于电报通信完全中断的危险，此地某些私人团体正计划建立一个紧急无线电通信机构，旨在维持与香港和马尼拉的直接通信，以便将讯息转播至世界其他地区。

大北公司和太平洋公司分别通往香港和马尼拉的电缆于1月6日在海上受损。大北线路在中国南海岸附近断裂，太平洋线路在台湾附近断裂。一艘电缆修理船正在香港处理损坏情况，之后将前往台湾修复损坏。

由于所有电讯现在都必须经过日本，此地的日本检查员并不十分严格。然而，电报在日本国内会受到严厉审查。

大东公司、大北公司和太平洋公司已就日本当局对电报的检查向其驻上海各自的领事馆提出报告，但截至目前，各领事馆尚未采取任何行动。

据报道，这三家公司也已致电位于长沙的中国政府交通部，解释其无法防止这一意外事态的发展。大北电报公司总经理表示，尽管目前局势如此，该公司与交通部签署的协议将继续有效。公司每年支付给交通部的款项将记录在案。截至昨天上午，日本检查员未扣留任何电讯，但如果发生电讯被扣留的情况，公司将应要求退还费用。

大东电报公司雇佣了50名华籍职员，大北公司有50名，太平洋公司有20名。目前，日本官员驻扎在各公司的业务部门，这些部门仅雇佣外国人。华籍雇员隶属于收报和发报部门。华籍职员曾举行会议，决议继续为公司服务，直到日本干涉公司管理为止，若发生此种情况，他们将集体离职。

THE CHINESE STAFF OF THE CHINESE GOVERT.
RADIO ADMINISTRATION CEASE WORK.
At 9.10 a.m. 5-1-38, Sub. Insp. Oikawa reported that
at 4.30 a.m. 5-1-38, the Chinese staff of the Chinese
Government Radio Administration, Sassoon House, Jinkee
Road, left the building and stated they were going on
strike. No reason was given for this decision. One
clerk remained on duty in the premises.
Mr. George F. Shecklen(American), vice-president,
R.C.A. Communications Inc., Sassoon House, Nanking Road,
has been managing the office of the Chinese Government
Radio Administration since shortly after the outbreak of
the Sino-Japanese hostilities. Following the withdrawal
of the Chinese troops from the vicinity of Shanghai Mr.
Shecklen has continued to manage the Administration pend-
ing a definite decision being reached regarding the future
control.
Mr. Shecklen was interviewed, regarding this latest
development in connection with the Administration and
denied that the employees had gone on strike. Mr.
Shecklen stated that the Chinese staff of the Administrat-
ion were employed by the Ministry of Communications, and
acting on instructions issued by that Department they had
cease work.
An incident of an untoward nature occurred.

最近被日本当局占领的上海国际无线电台，目前仅接受发往华北地区的电讯。不接受发往华中和华南地区的电讯。据报道，在华籍职员撤离后，某些机器设备遭到损坏。发往华北的电讯虽被接受，但是从塞瓦德路（Seward Road）和天潼路（Tiendong Road）拐角处的日本电报局发出。受雇于日本电报局的信差负责投递收到的电讯。

支付传输费用仅接受中国银行、交通银行和中国银行发行的钞票。

位于爱多亚路15号的上海国际无线电管理局分支办事处未安装任何发射或接收设备，其职能仅为接收或递送电讯。截至目前，尚无日本人访问过该分支办事处。

Chinese Radio Offices
Change Hands; Control
Taken Over By Japanese

Change Occurs At Early Hour In Morning; Hope
Expressed That Service May Continue; New
Operators At Work; Contracts Hold

JAPANESE AGAIN STATE THAT THERE
WILL BE NO NEWS CENSORSHIP

The Chinese Government Radio Administration in Sassoon
House changed hands yesterday morning when the Japanese
authorities assumed control over radio telegraphic facilities here
by taking over from the Chinese Government its traffic contracts
with the various wireless networks in all parts of the world.

At about the same time that the Japanese announcement
was made Mr. George F. Shecklen, Vice-President of R.C.A.
Communications, issued a statement to the effect that he had
severed his connections with the international radio services
from Shanghai.

A representative of "The Shang-
hai Times" was informed through
reliable sources yesterday afternoon
that the Japanese were operating
the former Chinese Government
Radio Administration with a staff
of about 30, all the Chinese former-
ly employed there having abandon-
ed their jobs. Ever since the de-
parture of the Chinese officials of
the Administration from Shanghai
it has been operated by R. C. A.
Communications.

The financial interests of R.C.A.
Communications in the former
Chinese Government Radio Ad-
ministration, a Japanese spokesman
declared yesterday morning, would
be respected by the Japanese Gov-
ernment. The spokesman charged,
however, that R.C.A. Communica-
tions, managed by Mr. Shecklen,
had "up to the present received its
instructions from the Chinese
Ministry of Communications."

Contracts Maintained

Ordinary radio traffic contracts
between the C.G.R.A. and the R.C.A.
Communications, Inc., as well as
with the Mackay Radio and Tele-
graph Co., the German Telefunken
and other wireless communications
systems would also be recognized,
the spokesman said.

Admitting the presence of Japan-
ese censors in the Radio Adminis-
tration offices, the spokesman
declared that they were being
stationed there in order to ensure
Japanese control of the radio com-
munications system as well as to
prevent the dispatch of messages
detrimental to the safety of the
Japanese Expeditionary Forces.

"We are not censoring press
messages," the spokesman declared.
"As stated before we hope we
never will have to do so and this
policy will remain unchanged until
our hand is forced."

Control Extended

Japanese control had to be
extended to the Radio Administra-
tion, he said, to prevent "sabotage"
by employees and executives.

"Such activities are clearly de-
trimental to the interests of the
public and will have to be curbed,"
he stated.

The Embassy spokesman em-
phasized that in assuming control
of the C.G.R.A. the Japanese auth-
orities had "the eager wish that
operations might continue for the
convenience of everyone."

"We are in a position to take
over the functions of the Chinese
Government vis-a-vis R.C.A.," he
declared.

"We wanted only the collabora-
tion of the Chinese staff and the
R.C.A., so that if there is a dis-
turbance because of anything such
as sabotage on the part of the
Chinese staff, it would only injure
the public. It is far from our
wishes that the service should be
disrupted."

Mr. George F. Shecklen, Vice-
President of R.C.A. Communica-
tions, Inc., stated yesterday morn-
ing that it was not practical for
him to carry on the international
radio communication services from
Shanghai, which R.C.A. Communica-
tions took over some months ago,
because the Japanese authorities
had assumed active control at
Sassoon House on Monday, and
were exercising a Japanese censor-
ship and Japanese control of the
revenues. These actions of the
Japanese made it impossible to
carry out the terms of the agree-
ment R.C.A. Communications had
with the Ministry, whereby R.C.A.
Communications took over the man-
agement and operation of C.G.R.A.,
he added.

The Japanese military authorities,
by placing Japanese censors on
active duty in the Shanghai In-
ternational Radio Office (formerly
C.G.R.A.) at Sassoon House yester-
day, caused the Ministry of Com-
munications to order the suspension
of the services and the staff to
walk out, Mr. Shecklen said. The
Ministry took these steps also be-
cause the Japanese had started to
take control of the revenues, he
explained. The circuits to London,
Paris, Berlin, San Francisco,
Manila, Hongkong, Batavia, Moscow,
Rome, Geneva, Saigon and Osaka
were closed at 5 o'clock yesterday
morning and the various adminis-
trations abroad were notified, Mr
Shecklen concluded.

中国无线电管理处
易手；控制权
落入日本人之手

变动发生于清晨；有人表示希望服务得以延续；新操作员已上岗；合同依然有效

日本人再次声明将不实施新闻审查

位于沙逊大厦的中国政府无线电管理局于昨晨易手，日本当局通过接管中国政府与世界各地各无线电网的交通合同，接管了此地的无线电报设施。

就在日本方面发布声明的同时，美国无线电公司（R.C.A. Communications）副总裁乔治·F·谢克伦（George F. Shecklen）先生发表声明，称其已切断与上海国际无线电服务的联系。

《上海泰晤士报》记者于昨日下午从可靠渠道获悉，日本人正在运营原中国政府无线电管理局，员工约30人，此前受雇于此的所有中方人员均已离职。自该管理局的中方官员离开上海以来，其一直由美国无线电公司（R.C.A. Communications）运营。

一位日本发言人于昨晨宣称，日本政府将尊重美国无线电公司在原中国政府无线电管理局中的经济利益。然而，该发言人指责称，由谢克伦先生管理的美国无线电公司“迄今为止一直接受中国交通部的指令”。

合同得以维持

该发言人称，原中国政府无线电管理局与美国无线电公司（R.C.A. Communications, Inc.）、麦凯无线电电报公司（Mackay Radio and Telegraph Co.）、德国德律风根公司（Telefunken）及其他无线通信系统之间的普通无线电交通合同也将得到承认。

在承认无线电管理局办公室内有日本检查员存在的同时，该发言人宣称，部署他们是为了确保日本对无线电通信系统的控制，并防止发送有损于日本远征军安全的电文。

“我们并未审查新闻电文，”该发言人宣称。“如前所述，我们希望永远不必这样做，除非被迫无奈，否则这一政策将保持不变。”

控制范围扩大

他说，必须将对无线电管理局的控制权扩展至日本方面，以防止雇员和高管进行“破坏”。

“此类活动显然损害公众利益，必须予以遏制，”他 stated。

大使馆发言人强调，日本当局在接管中国政府无线电管理局时，“热切希望业务能够继续，以方便各方”。

“我们有能力接管中国政府对美国无线电公司的职能，”他宣称。

“我们只希望中方员工和美国无线电公司予以合作，这样，如果因中方员工的破坏等行为引发骚乱，只会损害公众利益。服务中断绝非我们所愿。”

美国无线电公司（R.C.A. Communications, Inc.）副总裁乔治·F·谢克伦先生于昨晨表示，他从上海开展国际无线电通信服务已不切实际，该项服务于数月前由美国无线电公司接管，因为日本当局已于周一在沙逊大厦实行实际控制，并实施日本式审查及对收入的控制。他补充说，日本的这些行动使得美国无线电公司无法履行其与交通部签订的协议条款，根据该协议，美国无线电公司接管了中国政府无线电管理局的管理和运营工作。

谢克伦先生称，日本军方当局昨日在沙逊大厦的上海国际无线电局（原中国政府无线电管理局）部署日本检查员执行公务，导致交通部下令暂停服务，员工集体离职。他解释说，交通部采取这些步骤还因为日本人开始控制收入。谢克伦最后总结道，通往伦敦、巴黎、柏林、旧金山、马尼拉、香港、巴达维亚、莫斯科、罗马、日内瓦、西贡和大阪的线路于昨晨5时关闭，并已通知国外各相关管理部门。

Japanese control was extended to

中国政府无线电管理局
中方员工
奉命离职

日本人继续工作，
通过电缆传输电文

乔治·谢克伦
发表声明

日方官员称
美国无线电公司利益将受尊重

中国政府无线电管理局中方员工集体离职、中国与外国之间的无线电服务暂停，以及日本当局重申希望员工及相关外籍人士予以合作，是昨日本地无线电局势的焦点。

昨晚，原中国政府无线电管理局办公室仍在接收电文，但这些电文正通过本地三家外商拥有的电报公司转发。然而，发送至原中国政府无线电管理局待发的电文寥寥无几。

各电报公司管理层报告称，尽管城市无线电出口中断导致业务量激增，但其所有服务均正常运行。

美国无线电公司副总裁乔治·F·谢克伦先生于昨晨发表声明，其中详述了与日本接管控制权有关的一些细节。

他表示，他从上海开展国际无线电通信服务“该项服务于数月前由美国无线电公司接管”已不切实际，因为日本当局已于周一在沙逊大厦实行实际控制，并“实施日本式审查及对收入的控制”。

他说，日本的这些行动使得美国无线电公司无法履行其与交通部签订的协议条款，根据该协议，美国无线电公司接管了美国无线电公司的管理和运营工作。（注：此处原文似有笔误，重复提及R.C.A.，依上下文应指接管CGRA的管理运营）

下令暂停

谢克伦先生的报告称，日本军方当局于周一在沙逊大厦的上海国际无线电局（原中国政府无线电管理局）部署日本检查员执行公务，导致交通部下令暂停服务，员工集体离职。

他的报告继续指出，交通部采取这些步骤还因为日本人开始控制收入。

通往伦敦、巴黎、柏林、旧金山、马尼拉、香港、巴达维亚、莫斯科、罗马、日内瓦、西贡和大阪的线路于昨晨5时关闭，并已相应通知国外各相关管理部门。

谢克伦先生的报告最后声明，日本人现在完全负责沙逊大厦无线电服务办公室的工作。

日本当局通过其大使馆发言人，也于昨晨正式宣布，他们已通过接管中国政府与世界各地各无线电网的交通合同，接管了此地的无线电通信设施。

自中国官员离开上海以来，原中国政府无线电管理局的设施一直由美国公司美国无线电公司（R.C.A. Communications, Inc.）运营。发言人指责称，由乔治·R·谢克伦先生管理的美国无线电公司“迄今为止一直接受中国交通部的指令”。

尊重美国无线电公司利益

该发言人宣称，日本政府将尊重美国无线电公司在原中国政府无线电管理局中的经济利益。

他说，原中国政府无线电管理局与美国无线电公司、麦凯无线电电报公司、德国德律风根公司及其他无线通信系统之间签订的普通无线电交通合同也将得到承认。

在承认无线电管理局办公室内有日本检查员存在的同时，该发言人宣称，部署他们是为了确保日本对无线电通信系统的控制，并防止发送有损于日军安全的电文。

“我们并未审查新闻电文，”该发言人宣称。“如前所述，我们希望永远不必这样做，除非被迫无奈，否则这一政策将保持不变。”

他继续说，将对无线电管理局的控制权扩展至日本方面，是为了“防止”雇员和高管进行“破坏”。“此类活动显然损害公众利益，必须予以遏制，”他 stated。

日本发言人强调，日本当局在接管中国政府无线电管理局时，“热切希望业务能够继续，以方便各方”。

“我们有能力接管中国政府对美国无线电公司的职能，”他宣称。“我们只希望中方员工和美国无线电公司予以合作，这样，如果因中方员工的破坏等行为引发骚乱，只会损害公众利益。服务中断绝非我们所愿。”

Japanese Assume Radio
Operations As Chinese
Quit; Service Stopped

NIPPON CENSORS
TAKING CONTROL
OVER MESSAGES

Shanghai International Radio Office Chief
Explains Impossibility To Carry Out
RCA - Chlaotungpu Working Pact

Circuits To World Closed At 5 A.M.

Acting on instructions from the Ministry of Communications in Changsha, the 300 Chinese employees of the Chinese Government Radio Administration walked out at 6 o'clock this morning to protest against the Japanese taking over of the radio facilities. They decided not to "cooperate" with the Japanese.

Meanwhile, the telegraphic communications between Shanghai and the interior continued to function with most of the incoming and outgoing messages handled via Hongkong. The line to Tientsin, however, has been disrupted as result of the walkout of the Chinese employees from the Chinese Telegraph Office there as result of the Japanese taking over of the administration.

Shecklton Explains
Mr. George F. Shecklton, vice-president of R.C.A. Communications, Inc., stated this morning that it was no longer practical for him to carry on international radio communication services from Shanghai which RCA took over some months ago, because the Japanese authorities had assumed active control at the Sassoon House on Monday and were exercising a Japanese censorship and control of the revenues.

These actions of the Japanese made it impossible to carry out the terms of the agreement RCA had with the Ministry of Communications, whereby RCA took over the management and operations of the CGRA.

Service Suspended
The Japanese military authorities, by placing Japanese censors on active duty in the Shanghai International Radio Office (formerly CGRA) at the Sassoon Hotel yesterday, caused the Ministry of Communications to order the suspension of services and a staff walk-out. The Ministry took these steps because the Japanese had started to take control of the revenues.

The circuits to London, Paris, Berlin, San Francisco, Manila, Hongkong, Batavia, Moscow, Rome, Geneva, Saigon and Osaka were closed at five o'clock this morning and the various administrations abroad were notified.

The Japanese are now in complete charge of the Sassoon House Office of the radio services.

Contracts Respected
Ordinary radio traffic contracts concluded between the C.G.R.A. and the R.C.A. Communications, Inc., as well as with the Mackay Radio and Telegraph Co., the German Telefunken and other wireless communications systems will be recognized, a Japanese spokesman said today.

Admitting the presence of Japanese censors in the radio administration offices, the spokesman declared that they were being stationed there in order to ensure Japanese control of the radio communications system as well as to prevent the despatch of messages detrimental to the safety of the Japanese Expeditionary Forces.

"We are not censoring press messages," the spokesman declared. "As stated before we hope we never will have to do so and this policy will remain unchanged until our hand is forced."

It is reported that newspapermen filing stories from Japan have met with no censorship interference since the opening of hostilities.

Chinese Walk Out
Acting on instructions from the Ministry of Communications in Changsha, the 300 Chinese employees of the Chinese Government Radio Administration walked out at 6 o'clock this morning to protest against the Japanese taking over the radio facilities. They decided not to "cooperate" with the Japanese.

Meanwhile, the telegraphic communications between Shanghai and the interior continued to function with most of the incoming and outgoing messages handled via Hongkong. The line to Tientsin, however, has been disrupted as a result of the walkout of the Chinese employees from the Chinese Telegraph Office there because the Japanese took over the administration.

（批：S. D.S. Hendman C4 2/6/38）

127
日军接管无线电业务，中方人员离职；服务停止

日本审查员
接管电报控制

上海国际电台台长
解释无法履行 RCA - 交通部工作协议

通往世界各地的线路于上午5时关闭

遵照长沙交通部的指示，中国政府无线电管理局的300名中国雇员于今晨6时罢工，以抗议日军接管无线电设施。他们决定不与日本人“合作”。

与此同时，上海与内地的电报通信继续运作，大部分进出电报均经由香港处理。然而，由于中国电报局的中国雇员因日军接管行政而罢工，通往天津的线路已中断。

谢克顿作出解释

R.C.A. Communications, Inc. 副总裁乔治·F·谢克顿（George F. Shecklton）今晨表示，他已无法继续从上海开展国际无线电通信服务，该服务由 RCA 于数月前接管，因为日本当局已于周一在沙逊大厦（Sassoon House）实施实际控制，并实行日式审查及收入管控。

日方的这些行动使得 RCA 无法履行其与交通部达成的协议条款，根据该协议，RCA 接管了中国政府无线电管理局（CGRA）的管理和运营。

服务暂停

日本军方当局昨日在沙逊饭店的国际无线电台（前身为 CGRA）部署现役日本审查员，导致交通部下令暂停服务并引发员工罢工。交通部采取这些措施是因为日本人开始控制收入。

通往伦敦、巴黎、柏林、旧金山、马尼拉、香港、巴达维亚、莫斯科、罗马、日内瓦、西贡和大阪的线路于今晨五时关闭，并已通知国外各管理部门。

日本人现在完全掌控了无线电服务的沙逊大厦办事处。

合同得到尊重

一位日本发言人今日称，中国政府无线电管理局（C.G.R.A.）与 R.C.A. Communications, Inc. 以及麦凯无线电报公司（Mackay Radio and Telegraph Co.）、德国德律风根公司（Telefunken）和其他无线通信系统之间签订的普通无线电业务合同将得到承认。

该发言人在承认日本审查员存在于无线电管理机构办公室的同时宣称，派驻他们是为了确保日本对无线电通信系统的控制，并防止发送有害于日本远征军安全的电报。

“我们并没有审查新闻稿件，”该发言人宣称。“如前所述，我们希望永远不必这样做，除非迫不得已，否则这一政策将保持不变。”

据报道，自战事爆发以来，从日本发回报道的新闻记者未遇到任何审查干扰。

中方人员离职

遵照长沙交通部的指示，中国政府无线电管理局的300名中国雇员于今晨6时罢工，以抗议日军接管无线电设施。他们决定不与日本人“合作”。

与此同时，上海与内地的电报通信继续运作，大部分进出电报均经由香港处理。然而，由于中国电报局的中国雇员因日军接管行政而罢工，通往天津的线路已中断。

（批注：S. D.S. Hendman C4 2/6/38）

ascertained that this station was under the

for operating to Hongkong and U.S.A.

The 15 Chinese attached to this station
were not interfered with and were requested by
the Japanese to continue operating.

the premises to ensure that property is not
removed.

page_data.en:
Japanese In
Full Control
Of C.G.R.A.

Shanghai's Only Int'l
Wireless Service
Taken Over

EFFORTS MADE TO
CONTINUE SERVICE

Chinese Staff Waiting
For Instructions
From Changsha

Japanese authorities were last
night in complete control of the
Chinese Government Radio Admini-
stration, Shanghai's only inter-
national wireless communications
agency, after they had stationed
officials on the premises to act as
censor on all incoming and out-
going messages.

At a late hour last night, the
C.G.R.A. services were going on as
usual the Japanese officials having
not interfered with the operations
in any way.

An organization of the Chinese
Ministry of Communications, the
C.G.R.A., since the withdrawal of
the Chinese troops from Shanghai,
has remained in full operation
under the management of Mr.
George F. Shecklen, Vice-President
and Representative for China of
the R.C.A. Communications, Inc.

Mr. Shecklen was yesterday con-
tinuing negotiations with the Chin-
ese and the Japanese in an effort
to maintain the radio service of the
C.G.R.A., the disruption of which
would completely isolate Shanghai
with the rest of the world from
radio contact.

Waiting Instructions

The Chinese staff of the organiza-
tion continued at a late hour last
night to carry on their work. They
have communicated with the Mini-
stry of Communications authorities
in Changsha and were last night
waiting for definite instructions.

Actual control over the C.G.R.A.
was assumed by the Japanese yes-
terday afternoon following their
announcement late Monday evening
that they were taking charge of the
radio office. Some 12 to 14 Nippon-
ese officials arrived at the office
Monday evening and several of
these were yesterday afternoon
carrying out their duties as censors.
THE CHINA PRESS was informed. It
was also stated that the Japanese,
following their assumption of con-
trol, will impound the revenues of
the office.

The Japanese announcement,
which was in the form of a notice
posted at the C.G.R.A., stated that
Nipponese authorities were taking
over control of the radio office and
requested the Chinese members of
the staff to continue their work as
usual.

Denies Removal Plan

An official of the C.G.R.A. denied
yesterday that employees of the
office were about to remove some of
the valuable equipment from the
station. He pointed out that on
Monday morning, furniture belonging
to the former XQHC, broadcasting
station maintained by the Ministry
of Communications, was being re-
moved from its studio in the Sas-
soon House. The removal was being
undertaken in order to save the
broadcasting station from paying
rent, since the station has been
closed down for nearly a month,
he stated. The official explained
that no radio equipment was in-
cluded in the things that were being
moved.

The Japanese Embassy spokesman
stated yesterday that the action
taken by the Nipponese authorities
was made necessary by the fact
that Chinese employees were about
to remove some equipment from
the premises.

He explained that the Japanese
authorities are interested only in
maintaining the service and have
every intention of respecting the
rights of foreign communications
companies interested in the opera-
tion of the C.G.R.A.

Under R.C.A.

The C.G.R.A. services, he stated,
had been maintained under the
supervision of the R.C.A., which to-
gether with Mackay Radio net-
work, Italian, French, German and
Japanese systems were interested in
keeping up the radio services from
Shanghai.

Negotiations were still underway,
he said, for assumption of complete
control by the Japanese over the
service. The local representatives
of the R.C.A. headed by Mr. Sheck-
len, were not regarded by the Jap-
anese as representatives of the
Chinese Government, he stated.
page_data.zh:
日军完全掌控
中国政府无线电管理处

上海唯一的国际
无线电台服务被接管

努力维持服务

中方职员等待
长沙方面的指示

昨晚，日本当局已完全控制了中国政府无线电管理处（C.G.R.A.），这是上海唯一的国际无线通信机构。日方已在该处派驻官员，对所有进出电文实施审查。

昨晚深夜，中国政府无线电管理处的服务仍照常进行，日本官员未以任何方式干扰其运作。

中国政府无线电管理处系中国交通部下属机构，自中国军队撤离上海以来，一直由美国无线电公司（R.C.A. Communications, Inc.）副总裁兼驻华代表乔治·F·谢克伦（George F. Shecklen）先生管理，并保持全面运作。

谢克伦先生昨日继续与中日双方进行谈判，力图维持中国政府无线电管理处的无线电服务，因为该服务一旦中断，上海将与世界其他地区完全失去无线电联系。

等待指示

该机构的中方职员昨晚深夜仍继续工作。他们已与长沙的交通部当局取得联系，昨晚正等待明确指示。

日本政府于周一晚间宣布将接管无线电办公室后，于昨日下午实际接管了对中国政府无线电管理处的控制权。据《字林西报》（THE CHINA PRESS）获悉，约12至14名日本官员于周一晚间抵达办公室，其中几人于昨日下午履行审查员职责。另据悉，日本人在接管控制权后，将扣押该办公室的收入。

日本方面的声明以张贴在中国政府无线电管理处的告示形式发布，称日本当局正在接管无线电办公室的控制权，并要求中方职员继续照常工作。

否认搬迁计划

中国政府无线电管理处的一名官员昨日否认该处员工正准备从电台搬走一些贵重设备。他指出，周一上午，原属前XQHC广播电台（由交通部维持）的家具正从其位于沙逊大厦（Sassoon House）的演播室搬出。他表示，此次搬迁是为了使该广播电台免付租金，因为该台已关闭近一个月。该官员解释说，正在搬运的物品中不包含任何无线电设备。

日本大使馆发言人昨日表示，日本当局采取此举是因为中国员工正准备从 premises（办公场所）搬走一些设备，故实属必要。

他解释说，日本当局仅对维持服务感兴趣，并有意尊重那些对中国政府无线电管理处运营感兴趣的外国通信公司的权利。

在美国无线电公司（R.C.A.）监管下

他表示，中国政府无线电管理处的服务一直是在美国无线电公司（R.C.A.）的监管下维持的，该公司与麦凯无线电网络（Mackay Radio network）以及意大利、法国、德国和日本的系统一样，都致力于保持从上海发出的无线电服务。

他说，关于由日本完全接管该服务的谈判仍在进行中。他表示，日本人并不视由谢克伦先生领导的美国无线电公司当地代表为中国政府的代表。

page_data.en:
No Censorship Of Press
Despatches; Explanation
Given Of C.G.R.A. Affair

Japanese Spokesman States Guards Were Placed
To Prevent Removal Of Equipment; Others
Claim Only Studio Furniture Wanted

SECRECY FOR MILITARY REASONS IS
STRESSED ON TWO OCCASIONS

Referring to the attitude of the Japanese in connection with
the Chinese Government Radio Administration here, an official
spokesman stated last evening that it had been decided that full
control must be exercised. The Japanese he explained, expected
to assume the same powers over the Administration that
formerly accrued to the Chinese Government.

Asked if the Japanese wished to assume the powers of
censorship, the spokesman stated that if the Chinese formerly
enjoyed such control they would expect to do likewise. It was
stated that the safety of the military forces in Shanghai was
closely related to the question of censorship. The spokesman
added, however, that it was hoped that there would be no need
to establish a system of censorship for press despatches.

In a statement made to a representative of "The Shanghai Times"
last evening, Mr. George F. Sheck-
len, Vice-President of R.C.A. Com-
munications, stated no attempt had
been made at any time to remove
equipment from the company offices.
He added that some furniture had
been taken from the broadcasting
studio, a list of this having been
given to the Shanghai Municipal
Police and later to the Japanese
Consulate.

Spokesman Questioned
The question of the Chinese Gov-
ernment Radio Administration
called forth no little interest dur-
ing the course of the regular Japan-
ese press conference in the Metro-
pole Hotel yesterday morning. The
Japanese Embassy spokesman re-
plied to a question concerning de-
velopments at the Sassoon House
offices of the Administration by
stating that a guard had been post-
ed on the premises to prevent the
removal of equipment.

Status Discussed
The spokesman then went on to
say that the Japanese authorities
wished to obtain the necessary con-
trol in order to ensure that secrecy
would be maintained regarding
military operations and so that the
public would not be hindered. It
was further explained that the Jap-
anese authorities had learnt that
some equipment was being removed
from the offices and called upon
the manager concerned in order to
ask him to prevent the removal.

The spokesman then went on to
say that in the opinion of the Jap-
anese authorities the R.C.A. Com-
munications had the same status as
other foreign radio companies in
Shanghai. The C.G.R.A. services,
he stated, had been maintained
under the supervision of the R.C.A.,
which, together with the Mackay
Radio network and the Italian,
French, German and Japanese sys-
tems, were interested in keeping up
the radio services from Shanghai.

Negotiations Under Way
Negotiations were still under
way, the spokesman said, for the
assumption of complete control by
the Japanese over the service. Ask-
ed if any obstacles had been placed
in the progress of such arrange-
ments by the R.C.A Communica-
tions, the spokesman replied: "We
do not like to think so."

Asked if the Japanese had taken
over actual control, the spokes-
man said that guards had been
posted to see to it that there was
no removal of equipment and that
was all. The spokesman also said
that nothing had been done as yet
concerning what might be done with
the revenue of the company.

In a press release from the local
Japanese news agency shortly after
the conclusion of the conference
attention was called to the fact that
representatives of the R.C.A. Com-
munications in Shanghai were not
regarded by the Japanese as agents
of the Chinese Government.

Office At Chengtu
It was stated in Chinese reports
published here yesterday that the
Government was under the impres-
sion that the C.G.R.A. in Shanghai
had been turned over to R.C.A.
Communications for "safekeeping."
It was added, however, that some
of the equipment had originally
been removed to Chengtu, where
most of the officers of the adminis-
tration are located at the present
time.

Many of the officers and em-
ployees of the Administration were,
however, left in Shanghai to carry
on. It is understood that the
officers are taking part indirectly in
the conversations which are being
carried on between R.C.A. Com-
munications and the Japanese.

According to one Chinese report,
the misunderstanding between the
Administration and the Japanese
with regard to the alleged removal
of property was caused by the re-
moval of a piano and other furnish-
ings from the Ministry of Commu-
nications broadcasting studio. It was
stated that this room was formerly
used by the Administration but
later re-rented to the Ministry of
Communications for broadcasting
purposes.

新闻电讯不受审查；
就中国政府无线电管理处事件作出解释

日本发言人称部署卫兵旨在防止设备被搬走；其他人称仅欲搬走演播室家具

两次强调出于军事原因的保密性

昨晚，一位官方发言人在谈及日本方面对本地中国政府无线电管理处的态度时表示，已决定必须实行全面控制。他解释说，日本人期望获得以前归属于中国政府的那些对该管理处的权力。

当被问及日本是否希望行使审查权时，该发言人表示，如果中国人以前享有这种控制权，他们也会期望如此。据说，上海军队的安全与审查问题密切相关。不过，该发言人补充说，希望没有必要为新闻电讯建立审查制度。

美国无线电通信公司副总裁乔治·F·谢克伦先生昨晚向《上海泰晤士报》（The Shanghai Times）的一位代表发表声明称，从未试图从公司办公室搬走任何设备。他补充说，已从广播演播室搬走了一些家具，清单已提交给上海公共租界工部局警务处，随后又提交给日本领事馆。

质询发言人

昨天上午在大都会酒店（Metropole Hotel）举行的例行日本记者招待会上，中国政府无线电管理处的问题引起了不小的关注。日本大使馆发言人在回答有关该管理处沙逊大厦办公室事态发展的问题时表示，已在该处部署卫兵，以防止设备被搬走。

讨论地位问题

发言人接着说，日本当局希望获得必要的控制权，以确保军事行动的机密性得以维持，并使公众不受阻碍。进一步解释说，日本当局得知有人正从办公室搬走一些设备，遂召见相关经理，要求他阻止搬迁。

发言人随后表示，在日本当局看来，美国无线电通信公司在上海的地位与其他外国无线电公司相同。他说，中国政府无线电管理处的服务一直是在美国无线电公司的监管下维持的，该公司与麦凯无线电网络以及意大利、法国、德国和日本的系统一样，都致力于保持从上海发出的无线电服务。

谈判正在进行中

发言人说，关于由日本完全接管该服务的谈判仍在进行中。当被问及美国无线电通信公司是否在此类安排的进展中设置了障碍时，发言人回答说：“我们不愿这样认为。”

当被问及日本是否已接管实际控制权时，发言人说，已部署卫兵以确保没有设备被搬走，仅此而已。发言人还表示，关于如何处理公司收入的问题，目前尚未采取任何行动。

在记者招待会结束后不久，当地日本新闻社发布的一份新闻稿提请注意这样一个事实：在上海的美国无线电通信公司代表不被日本人视为中国政府的代理人。

成都办事处

昨日在此间发表的中文报道指出，政府认为上海的中国政府无线电管理处已移交给美国无线电通信公司“保管”。但报道补充说，部分设备最初已被运往成都，目前该管理处的大部分官员都位于那里。

然而，该管理处的许多官员和雇员仍留在上海继续工作。据悉，这些官员正间接参与美国无线电通信公司与日本之间正在进行的会谈。

据一份中文报道，管理处与日本之间关于所谓财产搬迁的误解，是由于从交通部广播演播室搬走了一架钢琴和其他家具所致。据说，该房间以前由管理处使用，但后来转租给交通部用于广播目的。

January 5, 1938. Morning Translation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition :-

THE SHANGHAI INTERNATIONAL RADIO OFFICE

In connection with the report published
in this paper yesterday regarding the taking over of
the Shanghai International Radio Office by the Japanese
authorities, it is learned that the Japanese authorities
yesterday detailed an additional number of officers to
guard the office in order to prevent the destruction of
its machinery. They desire the co-operation of the
Chinese employees of the Radio Office.
The following notice in Chinese was posted
up within the Shanghai International Radio Office last
night by the Japanese authorities :-
"Commencing from this date the Shanghai
International Radio Office which was originally under
the control of the Ministry of Communications of the
National Government will be taken over by the Special
Affairs Department of the Dai Nippon Imperial Army and
will continue to operate as usual to facilitate
communications.
"All employees are urged to remain at work;
they are assured that no changes will be made in their
positions and they will be accorded the usual treatment.
"This notice is issued for general
information.
"The Special Affairs Department of
The Dai Nippon Imperial Army.
"January 4 of the 27th Year (1938)
of the Republic."
Despite the assurances given in this
notice, the entire body of Chinese employees have decided
to withdraw and to give up their positions as from
to-day, January 5. The employees who were on night duty
yesterday left the premises late last night. Consequently,
there will be no radio communications between this port
and abroad as from this morning.
The Office employs in all more than 300
employees, including the workers and staff members.
A number of the employees have already been transferred
to the interior and the rest will either be sent to
other parts of the country or be given discharge
gratuities as in the case of the employees of the Shanghai
Telegraph Administration.
This Office was formerly known as the
International Radio Administration. It was established
in the 19th Year (1930) of the Chinese Republic under
the management of the National Reconstruction Commission
of the National Government. Later it was amalgamated
with the Ministry of Communications. It has direct
communications with San Francisco, London, Paris, Berlin,
Rome, Tokyo, Moscow, Manila, Hongkong and other places.
Recently it was transferred to the Radio Corporation of
America.

《华美晚报》晨刊：-

上海国际电台

就本报昨日刊登的关于日本当局接管上海国际电台的报道，据悉日本当局昨日增派多名警官守卫该电台，以防其机器设备遭到破坏。他们希望得到电台中国员工的合作。
昨晚，日本当局在上海国际电台内张贴了如下中文告示：-
“自即日起，原属国民政府交通部管辖之上海国际电台，将由大日本帝国陆军特务部接管，并照常运作，以便利通讯。
“望全体员工安心工作；兹保证各位职位不变，待遇照旧。
“此布。
“大日本帝国陆军
“特务部
“民国二十七年（1938年）一月四日”
尽管告示中作出了上述保证，但全体中国员工已决定自今日（1月5日）起离职并放弃职位。昨夜值夜班的员工于深夜离开了办公场所。因此，自今晨起，本埠与海外之间的无线电通讯将中断。
该电台共有员工300余人，包括工人和职员。
部分员工已调往内地，其余员工将被派往国内其他地区，或像上海电报局员工那样发给遣散费。
该电台前身为国际无线电台管理处。它成立于中华民国十九年（1930年），由国民政府建设委员会管理。后来并入交通部。它与旧金山、伦敦、巴黎、柏林、罗马、东京、莫斯科、马尼拉、香港等地有直接通讯联系。最近已移交给美国无线电公司（Radio Corporation of America）。

January 4, 1938.
Morning Translation

Hwe Li an Pao Morning Edition :-

SHANGHAI INTERNATIONAL RADIO OFFICE TAKEN OVER BY JAPANESE

Formerly the Despatching Station of the
International Radio Administration of the Ministry of
Communications, Sassoon building, Nanking Road, was located
at Chenju, with a Receiving Station at Liuhang. These two
stations were destroyed by fire following the outbreak of
the hostilities. In order to maintain telegraphic
communications, the Administration set up small stations
in a safe district and at the same time made arrangements
for the transfer of its interests to the Radio Corporation
of America. The agreement for the sale was formally
concluded on December 15 last year and the administration
became known as the "Shanghai International Radio Office."
At noon yesterday about 30 Japanese, some
armed and others in civilian clothes, called at the Office
and demanded that the Office be handed over to them. The
demand was rejected and a deadlock set in. At midnight
the Japanese posted up a notification in English stating
that the Office had been completely taken over by the
Japanese as from January 3, 1938, and all employees should
remain at work and will be accorded the usual treatment.
As this happened at a very late hour, the Office continued
to maintain the service while ways and means to deal with
the situation were being considered.
It is learned that the Office will make a
strong endeavour to protect its interests and should this
fail the Office will be closed.
The Japanese authorities commenced to take
over all telegraph administrations under China's Government
control immediately after the withdrawal of Chinese troops
from Shanghai. The Shanghai Telegraph Administration of
the Ministry of Communications on Foochow Road ceased to
function on November 28 last year when it was taken over
by the Japanese and since then all the telegrams between
Shanghai and various places in the interior have been
handled by the Shanghai International Radio Office and
the Great Northern Telegraph Office via Hongkong.

1938年1月4日。
晨间译稿

《华力安报》（Hwe Li an Pao，音译）晨刊：-

日本人接管上海国际电台

前身为交通部国际无线电台管理处的发报台，位于南京路沙逊大厦，发射台位于陈菊（Chenju，音译），接收台位于六行（Liuhang，音译）。这两座电台在战事爆发后毁于火灾。为了维持电报通讯，管理处在安全地区设立了小型电台，同时安排将其权益转让给美国无线电公司。出售协议于去年12月15日正式签订，该管理处遂更名为“上海国际电台”。
昨天中午，约30名日本人，部分武装，部分便衣，来到电台并要求接管该电台。这一要求被拒绝，陷入僵局。午夜时分，日本人张贴了一份英文通知，声明自1938年1月3日起，电台已由日本人完全接管，所有员工应继续工作，并将获得通常的待遇。由于此事发生在很晚的时候，电台在考虑应对局势的方法的同时，继续维持服务。
据悉，电台将大力努力保护其权益，若失败，电台将关闭。
在中国军队撤离上海后，日本当局立即开始接管所有由中国政府控制的电报管理机构。位于福州路的交通部上海电报局于去年11月28日被日本人接管后停止运作，此后，上海与内地各地之间的所有电报均由上海国际电台和大北电报公司经香港处理。

Hwa Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition :- 16.12.17 (AM)

GOVERNMENT RADIO OFFICE SOLD TO R.C.A.

According to information secured from a
reliable source, the agreement for the sale of the
Chinese Government Radio Administration to the R.C.A.
was formally signed on December 15.
Commencing from to-day it will be known as
the "Shanghai International Radio Office." All the
telegram forms, envelopes, receipts, etc. have been
changed. No changes in the staff have taken place
except in the case of a few superior officers. As
regards the despatching of messages, quickness and
accuracy are guaranteed.
It was reported in the local press the other
day that the Japanese have been visiting the place during
office hours. This paper now learns that these Japanese
have ceased their visits. At present only Japanese
policemen of the Shanghai Municipal Police are on duty.
Nobody has interfered with the administration of the
Radio Office.

日前本地报刊报道，日本人曾在办公时间前往该处。本报现获悉，这些日本人已停止前往。目前只有上海公共租界工部局警务处的日本巡警在该处执勤。无人干涉无线电台的管理工作。

Letter of complaint from N.C.A. Radio Corporation, Sassoon House.
Made by and Forwarded by Chief Inspector C. Bishop.

Sir,
At 6 p.m. 8-12-37 I interviewed in the absence of Mr.
G. F. Shecklen Vice President of the N. C. A. Radio Corporation
a Mr. James Sub-Manager at the Radio Administration Building
Sassoon House re the attached complaint. He explained to me
that they have no objections whatever to the Japanese Police
being on the premises if they would only keep to the duties
assigned to them. The Chinese operators naturally resent
their interference with their duties, which involves rather
delicate work, and cannot be done correctly under such
conditions. What the management really fears is a general
strike of operators which would be disastrous in these times.
I would ask that the Japanese Police be given strict
instructions as to their duties, and told that they are particularly
there to guard the machines and building and not on any
account to interfere with the staff. A Foreign Officer could
be detailed to show them the extent of their duties as to
where they should patrol etc.
I see no need for a Foreign Officer to be posted there
all the time. I believe they have even gone to the extent of
tampering with the machines, and taking photographs in
different parts of the offices without permission. This of
course is wrong as they were placed there to protect the
property and any Japanese Subjects present who would have
business with the Administration.
The following Japanese Police are on duty in the building.
