Shanghai
Dear Sir:
With regard to the presence of the Japanese constables
and plainclothesmen who have been stationed in and around the
premises of the International Radiotelegraph Offices in Sassoon
House, I wish to point out that some of the actions of these men
have been causing much uneasiness among the Chinese employees of
the radio service, which has created a state of inefficiency as
far as the work of the Chinese is concerned.
We fully understand the reason that the Japanese police
have been stationed there, and can readily appreciate that there
would naturally be a certain amount of uneasiness among the
Chinese clerks. However, the actions of these Japanese police-
men, I believe, have exceeded the bounds of propriety. There
have been placed for their use and comfort adequate chairs and
benches in the reception offices of the various departments, but
the Japanese have not been using these facilities, and have been
going behind the counters in the various departments, where the
Chinese clerks have their desks and chairs to carry on their
duties, and have been sitting at these desks and making the
Chinese clerks stand about the office, thereby interfering with
their legitimate duties.
We do not wish to interfere with the Japanese policemen
in the performance of their duty, and they may patrol the various
departments to carry out their duties. However, I wish to ask
your kind assistance in requesting them, in making their tours
of inspection, to please use the chairs provided for them in the
reception offices, and not occupy the desks and chairs of the
various Chinese staffs or annoy the operators, or read the con-
fidential messages filed by the public.
As you are aware, we are working very hard, night and
day, to keep the Chinese employees calm and remaining at their
duties under the existing emergency, and anything you can do to
ease this situation will be of great assistance to us in our
endeavor to keep the international communications services
operating normally.

亲爱的先生：
关于驻扎在沙逊大厦国际无线电报局办公处所内及周围的日本巡警和便衣人员的存在，我想指出，这些人的某些行为已在无线电服务的中国雇员中引起极大不安，就中国人的工作而言，这造成了一种效率低下的状态。
我们完全理解日本警察驻扎在那里的原因，并能充分体谅中国职员中自然会产生一定程度的不安。然而，我认为这些日本警察的行为已超出了得体的界限。在各部门的接待办公室内，已为他们放置了充足的椅子和长凳以供使用和舒适休息，但日本人并未使用这些设施，而是走到各部门柜台后面，那里是中国职员拥有桌椅以履行职责的地方，他们坐在这些办公桌前，让中国职员在办公室里站着，从而干扰了他们的正当职责。
我们无意干涉日本警察履行职责，他们可以巡视各部门以执行任务。然而，我希望请求您协助，要求他们在进行巡视检查时，请使用接待办公室为他们提供的椅子，不要占用各类中国职员的桌椅，也不要打扰报务员，或阅读公众存档的机密电文。

November 23, 1937. Morning Translation.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-
INTERNATIONAL RADIO STATION UNDER U.S. OWNERSHIP
Following the retreat of the Chinese forces from Shanghai, the Ministry of Communications entered into negotiations with the "Ma-Kay" Telegraph Company of the U.S.A. and the American Radio Corporation for the transfer to them of the International Radio Station in Sassoon House. The agreement for this transfer was formally signed the other day, whereupon the American flag was hoisted over the station.
According to reliable information obtained from the station, it recently received a telephone message from the Japanese authorities asking for the name of the responsible officer, to which a reply was made that the station had been transferred to American ownership.
Yesterday afternoon a high official of the Japanese Telegraph Administration in Shanghai, in company with several plainclothes Japanese military officers, called at the International Radio Station in Sassoon House. Accompanied by a responsible official of the station, they made an inspection of the various departments of the station after which they took their leave.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers:
CHINESE POLICE BUREAU WINDING UP ITS AFFAIRS
The Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government yesterday issued the following circular notice:-
"This Bureau has been ordered to wind up its affairs. The wages of the officers and men for the month of October were issued on November 14 to the officers-in-charge of the various branch Bureaux for distribution, but the pay of those sergeants who are detained in the camp in the French Concession will be issued through their respective officers as soon as a report on the investigation into the their names and numbers has been completed and submitted by the French Police on behalf of this Bureau.
"With the exception of the superannuation fund of sergeants under the control of the reserve unit of this Bureau, which has already been issued, the superannuation fund of the sergeants under the control of the various branch Bureaux will be paid through officers according to the lists and photographs of men submitted by the various branch Bureaux."

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-
ARRIVAL OF FIRST CONSIGNMENT OF RICE : DISCHARGE STOPPED
The s.s. "Kaying" of Butterfield & Swire carrying the first consignment of 25,000 bags of foreign rice, ordered jointly by the S.M.C. and the South China Rice Company, arrived in Shanghai on the evening of November 21.
The Rice Shop Owners' Association then designated 500 of its shop members to apply to the S.M.C. for supplies to be sold by retail.

1937年11月23日。晨间翻译。

《立报》及其他本地报纸：
国际电台归美方所有
继中国军队从上海撤退后，交通部与美国“麦克雷”电报公司及美国无线电公司就转让沙逊大厦国际电台事宜进行了谈判。转让协议已于日前正式签署，随后该台升起了美国国旗。
据从该台获得的可靠消息，该台最近接到日本当局打来的电话，询问负责人姓名，答复是该台已转让给美方所有。
昨日下午，日本电信管理局驻上海的一名高级官员，在几名便衣日本军官的陪同下，造访了沙逊大厦的国际电台。在该台一名负责人的陪同下，他们视察了该台的各个部门，随后离去。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：
中国警察局正在结束事务
上海市政府警察局昨日发布如下通令：
“本局奉命结束事务。十月份员警薪饷已于11月14日发给各分局主管分发，但被拘禁在法租界营房内的警士薪饷，待法国警察代表本局完成并提交对其姓名和人数的调查报告后，将通过其各自的主管发放。
“除已由本局后备队控制的警士退休金基金已发放外，由各分局控制的警士退休金基金，将根据各分局提交的人员名单和照片，通过警官发放。”

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：
首批大米抵达：卸货停止
怡和洋行所属的“嘉英”号轮船载有首批25,000袋外国大米，由工部局和华南米业公司联合订购，于11月21日晚抵达上海。
随后，米店业主公会指定其500家会员店铺向工部局申请供应零售大米。

CENTRAL NEWS SERVICE. SHANGHAI

4.

LOCAL SERVICE

C.G.R.A. REPORTEDLY TAKEN OVER BY
TWO AMERICAN RADIO COMPANIES

Shanghai, Nov. 23.- Signature was formally
affixed "the other day" to an agreement, whereby the
Ministry of Communication transferred its entire assets
in the C.G.R.A. (Chinese Government Radio Administra-
tions) to two American firms, namely, the Mackay Radio
and Telegraph Company and the American Wireless
Communication Corporation, according to the vernacular
press this morning.

An American flag, the report in the Chinese
press said, is now flying from the C.G.R.A.'s offices
at the top floors of the Sassoon House on the Bund,
all signs of the Ministry of Communications having
been removed.

Negotiations for the transfer of the radio
station, the report proceeded, were entered into
immediately after the withdrawal of Chinese troops from
Shanghai about a fortnight ago.

An official of the Mackay Radio and Telegraph
Company, when asked by a representative of the Central
News Agency this morning, said he could neither confirm
or deny the report. - Official News.

本地服务

据报道两家美国无线电公司
接管中国政府无线电管理局

上海，11月23日。- 据今晨中文报刊报道，交通部已於“日前”正式签署一项协议，将其在中国政府无线电管理局（C.G.R.A.）的全部资产转让给两家美国公司，即麦克雷无线电电报公司和美国无线通信公司。

中文报刊的报道称，一面美国国旗现在正飘扬在外滩沙逊大厦顶层的中国政府无线电管理局办公室上，交通部的所有标志已被移除。

报道接着称，无线电台的转让谈判是在约两周前中国军队从上海撤退后立即开始的。

今天上午，当中央通讯社记者询问麦克雷无线电电报公司的一名官员时，他表示既不能证实也不能否认该报道。- 官方新闻。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Sinsa Station,
REPORT
Date Nov. 27th. 19 39.
Subject Reported visit of Japanese with Truck to C.J.R.f. Premises, 145
Markham Road.
Made by. D.S.I. Read. Forwarded by. Inspector.
Officer in Charge.

Sir,
At 9.45 a.m. 27/11/39 telephone message was received
from C.P.C. 2586 Box No. 1 (Markham Road) to the effect
that a Motor Truck on which were several coolies and 2
or 3 Japanese had driven into the C.J.R.A. premises 145
Markham Road just previously.
Insp. i/c., D.S.I. Read, C.P.C. 309 accompanied
by Supt. Tobato visited above premises and Supt. Tobato
conversed with Mr. K. Nakama who had arrived on the
truck and who satisfied Supt. Tobato that he was in the
employ of the C.J.R.A. Freight Office. He stated they
had called merely to remove some old wood from the
premises. It is known that those premises are now un-
occupied being in a dilapidated state and under the care
of a private watchman/caretaker.
Supt. Tobato explained the Police visit and
enquiries were being made in the normal course of police
activity i.e. to prevent any unauthorised persons from
removing property.
The truck in use was a Fargo, L'c. No. 20671 Chinese
Lic. No. 5268.
Report submitted for information on instructions
of D.O. "B".
Copy to Special Branch.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant.
D.S.I.

D.D.O. "B".
/Chen.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH）

主题：据报道日本人乘卡车前往马克姆路145号
C.J.R.f.（原文如此，疑为C.G.R.A.笔误） premises。
制作人：D.S.I. Read。转呈人：督察。
主管警官。

先生，
1939年11月27日上午9时45分，收到来自中央公园捕房（C.P.C.）2586信箱1号（马克姆路）的电话留言，称一辆载有几名苦力和2或3名日本人的摩托卡车刚刚驶入马克姆路145号 C.J.R.A.（原文如此，疑为C.G.R.A.笔误） 大院。
主管督察、D.S.I. Read、中央公园捕房309号在Tobato警司的陪同下访问了上述地点，Tobato警司与乘卡车到达的中间名（K. Nakama，音译）先生进行了交谈，中间名先生使Tobato警司确信他受雇于C.J.R.A.货运办公室。他说他们来只是为了从该处移除一些旧木头。众所周知，这些地方目前无人居住，处于破败状态，由一名私人看守/ caretaker 照看。
Tobato警司解释了警方的来访，并表示询问是正常警务活动的一部分，即防止任何未经授权的人员移除财产。
使用的卡车是一辆 Fargo，伦敦车牌号 20671，中国车牌号 5268。
根据“B”区值班警官的指示，提交本报告供阅知。
副本送特务科。

我是，先生，
您顺从的仆人。
D.S.I.

“B”区副值班警官。
/陈。

Sir,

Mr. S. Koshino and Mr. H. Matsuda, Special Section of the
Japanese Military, came to Sinza Station with S.I. Fukuda,
attached to Gordon Road Station, and Superintendant Shibuye, "B"
Division.

Assistance was requested by the above members of the
Japanese Military to proceed to the Chinese Government Radio
Station, No.145 Markham Road, to inspect the property and to
place a new private watchman there.

D.C. 71 and the undersigned attended and the inspection
was carried out.

Two private watchmen who have been looking after the
property since the Chinese Forces withdrew from the Shanghai
area were informed that they could either continue their
employment under their new employers or leave the premises.

These two watchmen elected to continue their employment,
and the new watchman was also installed, he taking over the
keys to various doors.

Dr. Watson.

June 28, 1938.

Communicated dated June 23, 1938 from the Japanese Consulate-
General in regard to premises located at 145 Markham Road and
1446 Sinsa Road

In regard to the attached communication dated June 23, 1938,
from the Japanese Consulate-General addressed to the Chairman of
the Shanghai Municipal Council,
(1) Premises situated at No.145 Markham Road were originally
employed by the Ministry of Communications' Shanghai Telegraph
Office as a Radio Transmitting Station. On November 28, 1937
Japanese Consular officials conducted an inspection of the
premises but removed nothing. On December 18, 1937 four motor
trucks carrying Japanese naval officers and ratings, soldiers
and reservists entered the premises. Objections to this
procedure were raised by the United States Marine Corps in whose
sector the Transmitting Station was located, but formal
permission was given later the same day by the Marine Corps
for the Japanese to function. During December 18, several
truck loads of radio equipment were removed by the Japanese
from the premises, whilst on December 19, a party of plain
clothed Japanese entered this address and removed therefrom
a further quantity of radio equipment. Since that time no
further activities have been observed on these premises which
are now in charge of a Chinese watchman.
(2) Premises at No. 1446 Sinsa Road were formerly employed as a
Radio Station by the Ministry of Communications' Shanghai
Telegraphic Administration. On November 30, 1937 a party
of Japanese military and Consular police officers in plain
clothes inspected and assumed charge of the premises which
were again visited on December 19 by a number of Japanese
soldiers who removed a quantity of radio equipment. Since
that time no further activities have been observed on these
premises which are now in charge of a Chinese watchman.

1938 年 6 月 28 日。

关于日本总领事馆 1938 年 6 月 23 日来函，涉及位于马克姆路 145 号和新闸路 1446 号的处所

关于附上的日本总领事馆于 1938 年 6 月 23 日致上海公共租界工部局总董的来函，
(1) 位于马克姆路 145 号的处所原由交通部上海电报局用作无线电发报台。1937 年 11 月 28 日，日本领事官员对该处所进行了检查，但未取走任何物品。1937 年 12 月 18 日，四辆载有日本海军军官和水兵、士兵及后备军人的卡车进入该处所。由于该发报台位于美国海军陆战队的防区内，美方对此程序提出异议，但同日稍后，海军陆战队正式许可日本人进行活动。在 12 月 18 日期间，日本人从该处所运走了数卡车的无线电设备，而在 12 月 19 日，一群便衣日本人进入该地址，又搬走了大量无线电设备。自那时起，未观察到该处所有进一步的活动，目前由一名中国更夫看管。
(2) 位于新闸路 1446 号的处所前由交通部上海电政管理局用作电台。1937 年 11 月 30 日，一群便衣日本军方和领事警察官员检查并接管了该处所，12 月 19 日又有许多日本士兵再次到访，搬走了大量无线电设备。自那时起，未观察到该处所有进一步的活动，目前由一名中国更夫看管。

总领事拒绝签发任何进一步的证书，指出注册副本对工部局来说应该足够了，特别是考虑到工部局已经接受了该法国商行的地税，并已接受其为注册业主的事实。

Gary 先生进一步指出，如果工部局承认日本人的主张，就不应接受该法国公司为注册业主。另一方面，如果工部局接受该法国公司的税款，就自动承认该公司为合法业主，因此应在支持此类主张时给予该公司充分保护。

Gary 先生还指出，此事现已交由律师处理，以便与有关领事馆和/或领事团交涉，在做出决定之前，法国公司准备等待时机，而不是引发事件。

Misco. 616/38
Central
21st. June '38

Disputed ownership of property previously occupied by the
Shanghai Telegraph Office, 70 Foochow Road.

D.C. Guess

Sir,
At 4.50.p.m. on 21.6.1938 Mr.J.H.Melman of Messrs
Baboud, Mary & Cie, 17 Canton Road, came to the station and
reported that at about 4.p.m. even date a party of Japanese
civilians accompanied by three uniformed officers of the
S.M.Police, Japanese Branch, had proceeded to the premises at
70 Foochow Road and had forcibly entered by breaking the door
on Szechuen Road and had, thereafter, taken full possession.
This information had been made known to Messrs Baboud, Mary & Cie
by one of the Russian watchmen employed there who added that he
had offered the key to the visitors but that this had been ig-
nored in preference to said forcible entry.

（批：immediately copy）
Enquiries were made by D.C.Guess and a visit was
immediately paid to the scene but neither of the Russian watch-
men were then present and it was ascertained that they had left
shortly prior to the police visit. Examination was made of the
door on Szechuen Road but no trace of forcing could be found it
being noted, however, that a new padlock had been affixed.
Japanese S.I.Okawa and one J.P.C. were found outside the premises
and stated that they had been posted there to avert any untoward
incident. A number of Japanese and Chinese were seen inside
the premises.

On return to station it was found that the two Russian
watchmen, having returned to their employers' offices had made
their report and had been instructed to proceed to Central Stat-
ion and make a full report. Statements were taken from these
watchmen by D.S.I.Ovsiannikoff and copies are attached to this
report.

It was ascertained at Station that the Japanese
officers concerned in the affair were S.I.Okawa, J.P.C.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 21 JUN 1938）
（批：DCS B, S/, C, 28/6/38）

中央巡捕房
1938年6月21日

关于此前由上海电报局占用的福州路70号房产的所有权争议。

D.C. Guess（盖斯副督察）

先生：
1938年6月21日下午4时50分，广东路17号 Baboud, Mary & Cie 公司的 J.H. Melman 先生来到巡捕房报案称，当日下午4时许，一群日本平民在三名身穿制服的上海公共租界工部局警务处日本分队的警官陪同下，前往福州路70号的处所，并通过砸开四川路上的门强行进入，随后完全占据了该处。这一情况是由受雇于该处的一名俄罗斯更夫告知 Baboud, Mary & Cie 公司的，该更夫还补充说，他曾向来访者提供钥匙，但对方未予理会，而是选择了上述强行进入的方式。

（批注：立即复印）

D.C. Guess 进行了查询，并立即前往现场查看，但当时两名俄罗斯更夫均不在场，经查他们是在警方到达前不久离开的。对四川路上的门进行了检查，未发现任何强行闯入的痕迹，但注意到门上挂了一把新挂锁。在处所外发现了日本特别警员 Okawa 和一名日本警员 J.P.C.，他们声称被派驻此地以防止发生意外事件。在处所内看到数名日本人和华人。

回到巡捕房后得知，两名俄罗斯更夫返回雇主办公室后已作了报告，并奉命前往中央巡捕房作详细报告。Ovsiannikoff 高级副督察从这两名更夫处取得了口供，副本附于本报告之后。

经在巡捕房查明，卷入此事的日本警官为特别警员 Okawa、日本警员

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处特务科 1938年6月21日）
（批注：DCS B, S/, C, 1938年6月28日）

page_data.en:
J.P.C.163 who have also made statements copies of which are
attached.
From these statements and from enquiries made it is
ascertained that on the afternoon of 21.6.1938 instructions were
received by Insp.Oikawa from Mr.Uyehara, Deputy Commissioner,
to the effect that two J.P.Cs were to be despatched to the
Shanghai Telegraph Office, 70 Foochow Road, to prevent any
untoward incident when members of the staff of the Japanese
Imperial Communication Attache's office visited the premises.
J.P.Cs. 165 and 163 proceeded to the point being followed by
S.I.Oikawa after Insp.Oikawa had relayed his instructions to
C.I.Barry, Officer I/c Station. On arrival they met three
Japanese members of the above staff and proceeded to the entrance
in Szechuen Road which they found locked and guarded by the two
Russian watchmen. A request was made by the Japanese civilians
for the gate to be opened but this was refused by the watchmen
and the party thus remained outside for about 10 minutes after
which another party accompanied by Mr.E.Matsuda, Director of
the International Radio Administration, and Sergeant Major
Katohda, attached to the Japanese Military Police, approached
from the inside they having gained admittance via the gate on
Foochow Road.
At this juncture the Russian watchman, A.C.Hemelman opened
the gate with the key in his possession and proceeded to the
offices of Messrs Babeuf, Mary & Cie where he reported the
matter and was instructed to return to the scene and to hand over
his keys to the Japanese Police sub-inspector. He returned to
the scene but the custody of the keys was refused by S.I.Oikawa.
During this interval the three Japanese civilians, being unable
to enter by the Szechuen Road gate had entered by the Foochow
page_data.zh:
J.P.C.163，他们也提供了口供，副本附后。
根据这些口供及所作查询，查明1938年6月21日下午，大川（Oikawa）督察收到副局长上原（Uyehara）先生的指示，大意是派遣两名日本警员前往福州路70号上海电报局，以便在日本帝国通信武官处工作人员访问该处所时防止发生意外事件。在大川督察将指示转达给负责该巡捕房的 Barry 首席督察后，日本警员165号和163号前往该地点，大川特别警员随后也前往。到达后，他们遇到了上述机构中的三名日本成员，并前往四川路的入口，发现门锁着，并由两名俄罗斯更夫看守。日本平民要求打开大门，但遭到更夫拒绝，因此这群人在门外停留了约10分钟。随后，另一群人从内部接近，陪同人员包括国际无线电管理局局长松田（E. Matsuda）先生和隶属于日本宪兵队的加藤田（Katohda）军曹，他们已通过福州路的大门进入。
此时，俄罗斯更夫 A.C. Hemelman 用其持有的钥匙打开了大门，并前往 Baboud, Mary & Cie 公司（原文误作 Babeuf）办公室报告此事，奉命返回现场并将钥匙移交给日本警察副督察。他返回现场，但大川特别警员拒绝接管钥匙。在此期间，三名日本平民因无法通过四川路大门进入，便经由福州

□□d □te leavin□ the Police o ficers outside.
Custody of the keys having been refused by S.I.Okawa
the watchman returned to his employers and made a further report
thereafter returning to his post but being refused admittance by
the Japanese who stood on guard and who had placed an additional
padlock on the Szechuen Road gate. The watchman then informed
the Japanese that his bicycle and some personal property was
inside the building and requested that he be allowed to enter
to remove same. This was permitted and the Russian watchmen
(The company(s)
removed their/padlock whilst the Japanese removed theirs.
Hammelmann collected his bicycle and other property and was about
to leave when the Japanese told the other watchman Zeleniak to
leave also. Both watchmen left the premises and the gate was then
secured with the padlock produced by the Japanese. Both watchmen
proceeded to their employers' officers and were instructed to
proceed to Central Police Station and make full report.
The two Russian watchmen were questioned but both denied
that they had witnessed the entry of the Japanese through the
Foochow Road gate. They added that they knew of the existence
of this gate but, being stationed in the compound with instructions
not to leave, they had no access to same.
S.I.Oikawa, J.P.C.185 and J.P.C.163 were questioned
and stated that as they were at the entrance on Szechuen Road
they were ignorant of the presence of Mr.Matsuda and his party
until after entry had been effected. They denied having taken
any part in the matter but had remained at the scene in accordance
with their instructions to prevent any untoward incident. S.I.
Okawa confirms that he was offered custody of the keys by the
Russian watchman but stated that he was in no position to accept
same and therefore refused.
page_data.zh:
□□路 □□电□□ 留下警察在门外。
由于大川特别警员拒绝接管钥匙，该更夫返回雇主处再次报告，随后回到岗位，但被站岗的日本人和他们在四川路大门上加装的另一把挂锁拒之门外。该更夫随即告知日本人，他的自行车和一些个人财物在建筑物内，请求允许他进入取回。此请求获准，俄罗斯更夫们
（公司方）
取下他们的/挂锁，而日本人则取下他们的挂锁。
Hammelmann 取回自行车及其他财物，正欲离开时，日本人告诉另一名更夫 Zeleniak 也离开。两名更夫离开了该处所，随后大门用日本人提供的挂锁锁好。两名更夫前往雇主办公室，奉命前往中央巡捕房作详细报告。
对两名俄罗斯更夫进行了讯问，但两人都否认目睹日本人通过福州路大门进入。他们补充说，虽然知道该大门的存在，但由于他们被指派在院内值守且不得离开，因此无法接触到该大门。
对大川特别警员、日本警员185号和日本警员163号进行了讯问，他们陈述说，由于他们在四川路入口处，直到进入完成后才知道松田先生及其随行人员的存在。他们否认参与此事，称只是按照指示留在现场以防止发生意外事件。大川特别警员证实，俄罗斯更夫曾向他提出移交钥匙保管权，但他表示无权接受，因此予以拒绝。

page_data.en:
Instructions have since been issued by Messrs Baboud, Mary
& Cie, to their watchman not to attend their duty on the night of
21.6.1938 but to communicate with the office on 22.6.1938 and
receive further instructions.

At the time of making this report two Japanese, one
Chinese interpreter and C.P.W.1528 employed by the C.G.R.A. are
on duty at the premises the Japanese police officers having been
withdrawn.

It is reported for information that subsequent to the
affairs of 19.6.1938, reported on that date, arrangements were
made between the Japanese authorities and Messrs Baboud, Mary &
Cie for two Japanese to remain on the premises during the day
and one Japanese and C.P.W.1528 to remain on the premises night
& day.
These persons represented the Japanese claimants whilst four
Russian watchmen in two shifts were on duty on behalf of the
French company.

Following the Japanese occupation of the premises at
4.30.p.m. on 21.6.1938 nine Japanese members of the staff of
the C.G.R.A. and two members of the Japanese Military Police
remained on the premises until 8.p.m. being then relieved by the
party referred to above.

On behalf of Messrs Baboud, Mary & Cie, Mr.McLennan
complains that the S.M.Council has, by accepting payment of land
tax and rates, acknowledged the correctness of the company's
claim to ownership of the property and should not, therefore,
have detailed Police officers to assist in the forcible entry to
the premises by the Japanese or the eviction of the Russian
watchmen but it is pointed out that the police did in no way
assist or countenance this they being posted there purely to
prevent an incident.
J.Hayes
D.S.
Sen.Set.I/o.
page_data.zh:
此后，Baboud, Mary & Cie 公司已向其更夫发出指示，不要在1938年6月21日晚值班，而是于1938年6月22日与办公室联系并接受进一步指示。

在撰写本报告时，两名日本人、一名中文翻译以及由中国政府铁路局（C.G.R.A.）雇用的中国警员1528号正在该处所值班，日本警察已撤离。

据报以供参考，在1938年6月19日（当日已报告）的事件之后，日本当局与 Baboud, Mary & Cie 公司之间达成协议，安排两名日本人在白天留守该处所，一名日本人和中国警员1528号日夜留守该处所。
这些人代表日本索赔方，而四名俄罗斯更夫分两班倒，代表法国公司值班。

在1938年6月21日下午4时30分日本占领该处所后，中国政府铁路局的九名日本工作人员和两名日本宪兵队成员留在该处所直至晚上8时，随后由上述人员换班。

代表 Baboud, Mary & Cie 公司，McLennan 先生投诉称，上海工部局董事会既然接受了土地税和捐税的缴纳，即承认了该公司对该房产所有权的正当性，因此不应派遣警官协助日本人强行进入该处所或驱逐俄罗斯更夫；但需指出的是，警察并未以任何方式协助或纵容此举，他们被派驻那里纯粹是为了防止发生事件。
J. Hayes
高级副督察
高级警长负责人

Alexis Carl Hemmelman
Russia                                      xx D.S.I. Ovsianikoff
6.35p.m.                21 June 1938

I, the undersigned Alexis Carl Hemmelman, 59 years of age,
Russian Emigrant, watchman employed by Messrs. Baboud Mary Coy,
residing at 8 Tracey Terrace, Ru des Soeurs, F.C. make the
following statement of my own free will.
    On June 17th, 1938 I was engaged as a watchman by Messrs
Baboud Mary & Coy. to guard the premises of the former Shanghai
Telegraph Coy, 70 Poochow Road. My instructions were to keep all
the gates leading into the building always locked and not allow
any Chinese or Japanese to enter the building. In case of any
incident I was told to communicate immediately with the Shanghai
Municipal Police and to inform either Mr. M. Mary or Mr. Barrion
regarding the same. On June 19th Mr. Barrion
/ brought into the building two persons, one Japanese and one Chinese
and told me that the said persons can stay in the building
together with us. He gave them two written passes. Since June
19th two men, sometimes two Japanese or one Japanese and one
Chinese were always on duty inside the building together with us.
On June 21st, a Russian watchman named Zeleniak and I started our
duty at 9a.m. A Japanese and a Chinese watchman were also on duty
inside the building.
    At about 4p.m. the same date whilst Zeleniak and I were sitting
inside the building on the ground floor guarding the locked front
iron gate door over-looking the Szechuen Road, I noticed 3 other
civilian Japanese coming towards me from inside the building. The
Japanese approached me and started to demand the keys to the front
door. I told them that I can not hand the keys over to them
without permission of Mr. M. Mary. I noticed at this time one
Japanese Inspector and two Japanese constables of the S.M.P.
page_data.zh:
Alexis Carl Hemmelman
俄罗斯                                      xx Ovsiannikoff 高级副督察
下午6:35                1938年6月21日

本人，下述签署人 Alexis Carl Hemmelman，59岁，俄罗斯移民，受雇于 Baboud Mary 公司的更夫，居住在法租界姐妹路（Rue des Soeurs）Tracey Terrace 8号，自愿作出如下陈述。
    1938年6月17日，我受雇于 Baboud Mary & Coy. 公司，负责看守前上海电报公司位于福州路70号的处所。我的指示是始终保持通往建筑物的所有大门上锁，并不允许任何华人或日本人进入建筑物。如发生任何事件，我被告知应立即与上海公共租界工部局警务处联系，并向 M. Mary 先生或 Barrion 先生报告。6月19日，Barrion 先生
/ 带两人进入建筑物，一人为日本人，一人为华人，并告诉我这些人可以和我们一样留在建筑物内。他给了他们两张书面通行证。自6月19日以来，总是有两名男子，有时是两名日本人，或一名日本人和一名华人，与我们一起在建筑物内值班。
    6月21日，名为 Zeleniak 的俄罗斯更夫和我于上午9时开始值班。建筑物内还有一名日本人和一名华人更夫在值班。
    同日约下午4时，当 Zeleniak 和我坐在建筑物一楼，看守着面向四川路的锁着的前铁栅门时，我注意到另外三名日本平民从建筑物内部向我走来。这些日本人走近我，开始索要前门的钥匙。我告诉他们，未经 M. Mary 先生许可，我不能将钥匙交给他们。此时我注意到一名日本巡官和两名上海公共租界工部局警务处的日本警员

-2-

standing outside the iron grade gates. After refusing to give
key I immediately went inside the building with intent to find
the door through which the men entered the building. I discovered
that they entered the building through a side door overlooking the
Foochow Road. I think there were about 20 Japanese wearing
civilian clothing who entered the building at the same time. When
I discovered the door; I immediately proceeded to the office of
Messrs Baboud Mary & Co. 17 Canton Road and reported the matter to
Mr. Barrion through Mrs. Schulte. Mr. Barrion instructed me to
return to the building and hand-over the keys to the Japanese
Inspector of the S.M.P. I returned to 70 Foochow Road and handed
over the keys to the Japanese Insp. of the S.M.P. He first took
the keys but then changed his mind and returned the keys to me.
After the man refused to take the keys I again visited the office
of Messrs Baboud Mary & Coy. and reported it to Mr. Barrion. Mr.
Barrion told me to return to the building at 70 Foochow Road and
wait for relief. On return to the building I found two civilian
Japanese standing at the side door on the Foochow Road and they
refused me to enter the building. I went to the main gates on the
Szechuan Road and found that the Japanese locked the gates with
their own padlock. I again returned to the office of Messrs
Baboud Mary & Coy. and reported that I was not allowed to enter the
building although my personal property was inside the building. I
was told to return to the building and inform the other Russian
watchman named Zeleniak to remain inside the building until he is
relieved by other watchmen. In case the Japanese would not allow
the relieve watchman to enter the building, the men should report
page_data.zh:
-2-

站在铁栅门外。在拒绝交出钥匙后，我立即进入建筑物内部，意图寻找这些人进入建筑物的门。我发现他们是通过一扇面向福州路的侧门进入建筑物的。我想当时大约有20名穿着便服的日本人同时进入了建筑物。当我发现那扇门后，我立即前往广东路17号 Baboud Mary & Co. 办公室，通过 Schulte 夫人向 Barrion 先生报告了此事。Barrion 先生指示我返回建筑物，将钥匙移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处的日本巡官。我返回福州路70号，将钥匙移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处的日本巡官。他起初接过了钥匙，但随后改变主意，将钥匙还给了我。在该人拒绝接收钥匙后，我再次前往 Baboud Mary & Coy. 办公室并向 Barrion 先生报告。Barrion 先生让我返回福州路70号的建筑物等待换班。回到建筑物后，我发现两名日本平民站在福州路的侧门旁，拒绝让我进入建筑物。我走到四川路的主大门，发现日本人用他们自己的挂锁锁上了大门。我再次返回 Baboud Mary & Coy. 办公室，报告说虽然我的个人财物在建筑物内，但不允许我进入。我被告知返回建筑物，并通知另一名名为 Zeleniak 的俄罗斯更夫留在建筑物内，直到有其他更夫来换班。如果日本人不允许换班的更夫进入建筑物，这些人应向警方

page_data.en:
the matter to the Police. I returned to the building and as I
was not allowed to enter the same I shouted to the Russian
watchman Zeleniak that he should remain inside until he is
relieved. After that I explained to the Japanese that there was
my bicycle and some other property inside the building and they
allowed me to enter the same and take it away. Zeleniak was
inside the building but when I collected my property, the
Japanese ordered Zeleniak to leave the building and he left the
building together with me. We returned to the office Messrs
Baboud Mary & Coy. and reported the matter to Mr. Barrion. Mr.
Barrion instructed us to report the matter to the Police. We
reported it to the Central Police Station. The above is my true
statement.
Herman Sima
Signed.
page_data.zh:
报告此事。我返回建筑物，由于不被允许进入，我向俄罗斯更夫 Zeleniak 喊话，让他留在里面直到有人来换班。之后，我向日本人解释说，里面有我的自行车和其他一些财物，他们允许我进入并取走。Zeleniak 当时在建筑物内，但当我收拾财物时，日本人命令 Zeleniak 离开建筑物，他便与我一同离开了建筑物。我们返回 Baboud Mary & Coy. 办公室并向 Barrion 先生报告了此事。Barrion 先生指示我们向警方报告此事。我们向中央巡捕房作了报告。以上是我的真实陈述。
Herman Sima
签名。

page_data.en:
Alexis Carl Hammelman
Russia                                          x D.S.I. Ovsianikoff
8.35p.m.                21 June 1938

    I, the undersigned Alexis Carl Hammelman, 59 years of age,
Russian Emigrant, watchman employed by Messrs. Baboud Mary Coy,
residing at 8 Tracey Terrace, Ru des Secours, F.C. make the
following statement of my own free will.
    On June 17th, 1938 I was engaged as a watchman by Messrs
Baboud Mary & Coy. to guard the premises of the former Shanghai
Telegraph Coy, 70 Foochow Road. My instructions were to keep all
the gates leading into the building always locked and not allow
any Chinese or Japanese to enter the building. In case of any
incident I was told to communicate immediately with the Shanghai
Municipal Police and to inform either Mr. Mc Mary or Mr. Barrion
regarding the same. On June 19th Mr. Barrion
/ brought into the building two persons, one Japanese and one Chinese
and told me that the said persons can stay in the building
together with us. He gave them two written passes. Since June
19th two men, sometimes two Japanese or one Japanese and one
Chinese were always on duty inside the building together with us.
    On June 21st, a Russian watchman named Seleniak and I started our
duty at 6a.m. A Japanese and a Chinese watchman were also on duty
inside the building.
    At about 4p.m. the same date whilst Seleniak and I were sitting
inside the building on the ground floor guarding the locked front
iron gate door overlooking the Szechuen Road, I noticed 3 other
civilian Japanese coming towards me from inside the building. The
Japanese approached me and started to demand the keys to the front
door. I told them that I can not hand the keys over to them
without permission of Mr. Mc Mary. I noticed at this time one
Japanese Inspector and two Japanese constables of the S.M.P.
page_data.zh:
阿列克谢·卡尔·哈梅尔曼 (Alexis Carl Hammelman)
俄罗斯                                          x 特别巡捕 Ovsianikoff (音译)
晚上8点35分                1938年6月21日

    本人，下述签署人阿列克谢·卡尔·哈梅尔曼，59岁，
俄罗斯流亡者，受雇于 Baboud Mary 公司 (Messrs. Baboud Mary Coy) 的看守，
居住于法租界救济路 (Rue des Secours) 特雷西露台 (Tracey Terrace) 8号，自愿作出如下陈述。
    1938年6月17日，我受雇于 Baboud Mary & Coy 公司，担任福州路70号原上海电报公司 (Shanghai Telegraph Coy) 房产的看守。我的指令是始终保持通往大楼的所有大门上锁，并不允许任何中国人或日本人进入大楼。如遇任何事件，我被告知应立即与上海公共租界工部局警务处联系，并就此通知 Mc Mary 先生或 Barrion 先生。6月19日，Barrion 先生
/ 带两人进入大楼，一人为日本人，一人为中国人，
并告诉我这些人可以与我们一起留在楼内。他给了他们两张书面通行证。自6月19日以来，楼内始终有两名男子与我们一起值班，有时是两名日本人，有时是一名日本人和一名中国人。
    6月21日，一名名叫 Seleniak (音译) 的俄罗斯看守和我于早上6点开始值班。楼内还有一名日本看守和一名中国看守在值班。
    同日约下午4点，当 Seleniak 和我坐在楼内一楼，守卫着俯瞰四川路的已上锁的前铁栅门时，我注意到另外三名平民日本人从楼内向我走来。这些日本人走近我，开始索要前门的钥匙。我告诉他们，未经 Mc Mary 先生许可，我不能将钥匙交给他们。此时我注意到一名日本巡官和两名上海公共租界工部局警务处的日本巡捕。

page_data.en:
Sub-Inspector Okawa, attached to Central
Station.
xx self.
21-6-38

I beg to state at about 3.40p.m. on the 21-6-38, acting on
instructions of Inspector Oikawa I attended the Chinese Telegraph
Administration Office located at the corner of Szechuan and
Foochow Road. On my arrival at the Szechuan Road entrance I saw
that Mr. Matsuzaki, employee of the Shanghai International Radio
Office was standing at the front of the entrance together with
two other Japanese and J.P.C. 163 Izumi and J.P.C. 185 Yamaguchi
five persons in all.

I noticed that two Russian watchmen and two Japanese were in
the premises, the gate of which had been secured by a lock.

Whilst we were keeping guard outside the above entrance,
and at about 4p.m., I saw Mr. Matsuda, the director of C.I.R.A.
(Shanghai International Radio Office) and Sergeant Major Kotchda
of the Japanese Military Police appear in the premises together
with other Japanese.

At about 4.30p.m. one of the Russian watchmen who was in
the premises approached me from outside and requested me to keep
the keys for the lock of Szechuan Road entrance I questioned him
who gave an order to hand the key to the Police, and he replied
that Mr. Mary gave him instruction to do so. I explained to him
that I was not in a position to receive the key and so I refused
to touch it.

The watchman then kept the keys in his possession and walked
away toward Foochow Road.

At about 5.30p.m. I was still on guard outside the entrance
when the said Russian watchman returned and opened the entrance
with a key. Shortly afterwards he left the premises by riding a
page_data.zh:
中央巡捕房副巡官 Okawa (大川)。
xx 本人。
1938年6月21日

谨陈述如下：1938年6月21日下午约3点40分，我奉 Okawa (大川) 巡官之命，前往位于四川路与福州路转角的中国电政管理局办公室。当我到达四川路入口时，我看到上海国际电台 (Shanghai International Radio Office) 职员 Matsuzaki (松崎) 先生与另外两名日本人以及日本巡捕 163号 Izumi (泉) 和 185号 Yamaguchi (山口) 站在入口前，共计五人。

我注意到楼内有两名俄罗斯看守和两名日本人，其大门已被锁住。

当我们在上述入口外警戒时，约下午4点，我看到中国国际无线电管理处 (C.I.R.A., 即上海国际电台) 主任 Matsuda (松田) 先生和日本宪兵军曹 Kotchda (音译) 与其他日本人一同出现在楼内。

约下午4点30分，楼内的一名俄罗斯看守从里面走出来接近我，请求我保管四川路入口门锁的钥匙。我询问他是谁下令将钥匙交给警察的，他回答说是 Mary 先生指示他这样做的。我向他解释我无法接收钥匙，因此拒绝触碰它。

随后该看守自行保管钥匙，向福州路方向走去。

约下午5点30分，我仍在入口外警戒，此时前述俄罗斯看守返回并用钥匙打开了入口。不久后，他骑着一辆

page_data.en:
-2-

bicycle together with another Russian watchman, who had been in
the premises.
I returned to the station at 5.40p.m. on the instructions
of Inspector Oikawa.

Signed.
R. Okawa.
page_data.zh:
-2-

自行车与另一名曾在楼内的俄罗斯看守一同离开了该处。
我于下午5点40分奉 Okawa (大川) 巡官之命返回巡捕房。

签名。
R. Okawa (大川)。

page_data.en:
J.P.C. 163 X. Izumi, attached to Central
Station.
XX self.
Central Stn.          21-6-38           /translated by Inspt. Oikawa.

At about 3.30p.m. on the 21-6-38, I was sent by Inspt.
Oikawa to guard the staff of the Japanese Imperial Communication
the
Attaché Office t/Chinese Government Telegraph Administration, No.
20C Szechuan Road together with J.P.C. 185 Yamazuchi, I saw Mr.
S. Matsuzaki and 2 other members of the Japanese staff of the above
office were standing at the gate of the Administration.

On the request of Mr. S. Matsuzaki, I interpreted between he
and 2 Russian Watchmen who were inside of the entrance to open
the gate and allow the 3 Japanese to enter the premises. As the
Russian watchmen refused their entrance, they were standing at
the outside.

Soon after the above occurrence, S. Inspt. Okawa came to
the scene with whom I was still stood guard to prevent trouble
occurring. About 10 minutes later I saw Mr. E. Matsuda, a
director of International Radio Administration (C.U.R.A.) with
several other Japanese staff led by Sergeant Major Katohda and
another Military police all in plain clothes appear inside the
gate and call Mr. Matsuzaki and 2 others who were still standing
outside the entrance, to come into the premises via another rear
gate facing Foochow Road and which they did so. At about 4.30p.m
whilst we were still guarding the Szechwan Road gate, one of the
2 Russian watchmen who were inside the premises, came from the
outside to our place and tried to hand over their keys to S.
Inspt. Okawa. Sub-Inspt. Okawa refused to receive the keys, and
the watchmen then left the scene toward the south. We continued
to guard the outside of the building until we were called back
to Station, at about 5.30p.m.
                                            Signed.
（签名）
page_data.zh:
日本巡捕 163号 X. Izumi (泉)，隶属中央巡捕房。
XX 本人。
中央巡捕房          1938年6月21日           /由 Okawa (大川) 巡官翻译。

1938年6月21日下午约3点30分，我奉 Okawa (大川) 巡官之命，与日本巡捕 185号 Yamazuchi (山口) 一同前往四川路20C号中国政府电政管理局/日本帝国通信武官室，负责警卫工作。我看到上述办公室的日本职员 S. Matsuzaki (松崎) 先生及其他两名日方人员正站在管理局的大门口。

应 S. Matsuzaki (松崎) 先生的请求，我在他与入口内的两名俄罗斯看守之间进行传译，要求打开大门允许这三名日本人进入楼内。由于俄罗斯看守拒绝他们进入，他们便站在外面。

上述事件发生后不久，Okawa (大川) 副巡官抵达现场，我继续与其一同站岗以防发生骚乱。约10分钟后，我看到国际无线电管理处 (C.U.R.A.) 主任 E. Matsuda (松田) 先生，在军曹 Katohda (加藤田, 音译) 率领下，与另一名便衣宪兵及数名其他日本职员出现在大门内，并召唤仍站在入口外的 Matsuzaki (松崎) 先生及其他两人，经由面向福州路的另一扇后门进入楼内，他们随即照办。约下午4点30分，当我们仍在守卫四川路大门时，楼内的两名俄罗斯看守之一从里面走到我们这里，试图将钥匙交给 Okawa (大川) 副巡官。Okawa (大川) 副巡官拒绝接收钥匙，随后该看守向南离开现场。我们继续在大楼外警戒，直到约下午5点30分被召回巡捕房。
                                            签名。
（签名）

page_data.en:
J.P.C. 185 Toshio Yamaguchi, attached
to Yulin Road Station.

Central Stn.           2 -6-38           XX self.
                                       translated by D.S. Kobayashi
                                       /----------

I beg to state that at 3.30p.m. on the 21-6-38 acting on
instructions from Inspector Oikawa I attended the Chinese
Telegraph Administration located at No. 200 Szechuen Road together
with J. P. C. 185 Izumi. On arrival at the above entrance I saw
Mr. Matsuzaki attached to the Japanese Imperial
Communication Attache Office and two other Japanese standing
outside the gate on the inside the bamboo fence. Soon after our
arrival Sub-Inspt. Okawa attended to the scene, then we stood
guard at this point to prevent trouble.

About 10 minutes later whilst we were guarding the Szechuen
Road entrance presence of above Japanese, I saw Mr. Eiichi
Matsuda, the director of The International Radio Administration
(C.U.R.A.) and several employees of the above office accompanied
by Sergeant Major Katohda attached to Military Police and/all in
plain clothes appear from the interior of the premises and call
Mr. Matsuzaki and his two companions who were still standing
outside the entrance to enter via the entrance facing Foochow
Road.

About 5 or 6 minutes later I was instructed by Sub-Inspt.
Okawa to go to the outside the rear entrance on Foochow Road
to keep a guard. Then I went to the rear entrance, at this
entrance where I saw a Japanese employee of the C.U.R.A. was
standing at the entrance.

At about 4.30p.m. I was called by a foreign sergeant to
attend a traffic accident occurred in the vicinity of the
Garden Bridge, so I left the scene.

                                            Signed.
page_data.zh:
日本巡捕 185号 Toshio Yamaguchi (山口敏雄)，隶属榆林路巡捕房。

中央巡捕房           1938年6月21日           XX 本人。
                                       由特别巡捕 Kobayashi (小林) 翻译
                                       /----------

谨陈述如下：1938年6月21日下午3点30分，我奉 Okawa (大川) 巡官之命，与日本巡捕 185号 Izumi (泉) 一同前往四川路200号的中国电政管理局。到达上述入口时，我看到隶属日本帝国通信武官室的 Matsuzaki (松崎) 先生及另外两名日本人站在竹篱笆内的大门外侧。我们到达后不久，Okawa (大川) 副巡官抵达现场，随后我们在此处站岗以防发生骚乱。

约10分钟后，当我们在上述日本人在场的情况下守卫四川路入口时，我看到国际无线电管理处 (C.U.R.A.) 主任 Eiichi Matsuda (松田荣一) 先生及该办公室的几名雇员，在隶属宪兵队的军曹 Katohda (加藤田, 音译) 陪同下，均身着便衣，从楼内出现，并召唤仍站在入口外的 Matsuzaki (松崎) 先生及其两名同伴，经由面向福州路的入口进入。

约5或6分钟后，我奉 Okawa (大川) 副巡官之命前往福州路后门外侧进行警戒。于是我前往后门，在该入口处我看到一名 C.U.R.A. 的日本职员正站在入口处。

约下午4点30分，一名外籍巡佐召我去处理外白渡桥附近发生的一起交通事故，于是我离开了现场。

                                            签名。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Enquiries into ownership of property previously occupied by Shanghai Telegraph office.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / JUNE 1938 / SPECIAL BRANCH）
（批：Special Branch Copy）
（批：2csb）
（批：S.I 20/6）
（批：D.D.O. "A" Div）
（批：6 20/6）
Sir,
Further to the report submitted on 18-6-38 by D.S. Kobayashi, Messrs A. Gemmelman and B. Zelinviuk, Russian watchmen employed by Messrs Baboud, Mary & Cie to protect the property at 70 Foochow Road, came to station at 8.25a.m. on 19-6-38 and reported that proceeding to above address on duty on the morning of 19-6-38 they found that Chinese watchmen from the C.G.R.A. had already installed themselves and having locked themselves in refused to allow the Russians to enter. After making this report they returned to their post but at 10a.m. even date, Mrs. Schultz of Baboud, Mary & Cie, telephoned to station requesting that the watchmen be informed not to create any disturbance but, if they found themselves unable to gain entry to the premises, to leave the scene as the whole question would be settled on 20-6-38. This was done and the two watchmen left the scene.
A C.P.C. has now been posted to patrol in the vicinity of the aforementioned property to avert any untoward incident pending settlement of the disputed ownership.
Mr. Robertson, D.O. "A" informed by telephone.
（签名）
J O'Gues
D. S.
Sen. Det. 1/c.

Zelinviuk (音译) 两位先生，于1938年6月19日上午8点25分来到巡捕房报告称，他们在1938年6月19日上午前往上述地址执勤时，发现来自中国无线电管理局 (C.G.R.A.) 的中国看守已经进驻，并将自己锁在屋内，拒绝让俄罗斯人进入。作出此报告后，他们返回了岗位，但在同日（19日）上午10点，Baboud, Mary & Cie 公司的 Schultz (舒尔茨) 夫人致电巡捕房，要求通知看守不要制造任何骚乱，但如果发现无法进入该物业，则离开现场，因为整个问题将于1938年6月20日得到解决。此事已照办，两名看守离开了现场。

June 18th,    38.

Enquiries into ownership of property previously
occupied by Shanghai Telegraph Office.

Sir,

With reference to further development of the above
matter the following information was revealed.

At about 11p.m. on the 17-6-38 an armed Chinese
Watchman 1528 employed by C.G.R.A. (Shanghai International
Radio Office) Sassoon House reported to the station that
he was instructed by his employer to attend for duty at
the branch office No. 70 Foochow Road from that night.
Consequently a letter addressed to the Chief Superintendant
of S.M.P. giving information of the fact was produced by
the watchman at Central Station. The letter was signed
by H. Matsuda, manager of C.G.R.A.

This watchman was posted duty in the premises of
Shanghai Telegraph Office together with a Russian watchman
employed by Messrs Deboud Mary & Cie over night and
returned to the C.G.R.A. at 7a.m. on the 18-6-38.

A wooden signboard written in black ink read as
"Branch Office of Shanghai International Radio Office" was
placed outside No. 70 Foochow Road inside the bamboo fence

At 9a.m. on the 18-6-38 four Japanese employees of
the C.G.R.A. (Shanghai International Radio Office) who
were despatched to operate the business at abovementioned
address arrived but a Russian watchman closed the back
gate of the premises and refused to open same for them

1938年6月18日。

关于此前由上海电报局占用的物业所有权之查询。

先生，

关于上述事项的进一步进展，现披露如下信息。

1938年6月17日晚上约11点，受雇于 C.G.R.A.（上海国际电台）沙逊大厦的一名武装中国看守 1528号向巡捕房报告称，他接到雇主指令，从当晚起前往福州路70号分部执勤。因此，该看守在中央巡捕房出示了一封致上海公共租界工部局警务处总巡长的信，告知了这一事实。该信由 C.G.R.A. 经理 H. Matsuda (松田) 签署。

这名看守与一名受雇于 Deboud Mary & Cie 公司的俄罗斯看守在上海市电报局物业内共同过夜值班，并于1938年6月18日早上7点返回 C.G.R.A.。

Sir,

Acting on instructions of C.I. Barry, Officer i/c station, I interviewed Mr. Mary, manager of Messrs Baboud, Mary & Cie, 17 Canton Road, in connection with the ownership of property at the intersection of Foochow and Szechuan Roads, previously occupied by the Shanghai Telegraph Office of the Ministry of Communications, and obtained the following information from him.

Mary, manager of Baboud, Mary & Cie, on the one part, and Mr. C.R. Nieh, acting Manager, Shanghai Telegraph Office, on behalf of the Ministry of Communications, on the other.

Made by/ [签名] and Forwarded by Chief Inspector Bishop.

Sir,

The Shanghai Telegraph Office, No. 70 Foochow Road was taken over by the Japanese Military Authorities on November 27, 1937 and since then C.P.Cs. have been placed nearby to watch that no unauthorised person attempts to or take away any property from the aforementioned address.

The employees of the Shanghai Telegraph Office named Yuan Hai Ling (袁海林), Soo You Ziang (蘇玉祥) Chen Nyi Sun (陳義生) and Tsao Kin (曹景) who are paid from the Chinese Post Office, Szechuen Road take turn in watching the premises of the Shanghai Telegraph Office, which gates are closed and locked.

As far as can be learned this particular office is under the control of the Japanese Military Authorities but conducted by the Japanese Imperial Communications Bureau and is not functioning yet owing to shortage of staff.

On December 27, 1937 Mr. Azuma, Communications Attache in Shanghai visited the Shanghai Telegraph Office No. 70 Foochow Road with members of his staff and on January 8, 1938 Mr. Matsuzaki a representative of the Japanese Imperial Communications Bureau visited the above place escorted by J.P.S. 103 and J.P.C. 163 and took away eight desk lamps to the C. G. R. A. Sassoon House.

Police on duty and Watchmen inside the building communicate with the station at all times when anybody visits the premises.

[签名]

POLICE FORCE FOR
Translation of despatch No. 10.. to Council
from the Shanghai Telegraph Administration,
Ministry of Communications.
Dated 11th December, 1937.

Radio Station and Japanese

Owing to force of circumstances we some time ago temporarily
suspended work and requested the Council to adequately protect
our houses, land, machinery and other property in the International
Settlement. Later, we received reports from our Radiogram Station
in Lane 591 Bubbling Well Road, transmitting Station in Markham
Road and Broadcasting Station in Joffre Road, to the effect that
various machines and a truck had been taken away by the Japanese.
We wrote to the Council and asked for action. We have now received
another report from our Radiogram Station, Lane 591 Bubbling Well
Road, saying that on the 10th instant the Japanese with a truck
and a motor car again removed from the Station many receiving
machines and typewriters; the case was also reported to the Chen-
du Road Police Station and is on record there. In the interest of
property rights will the Council please pay attention to this
matter and afford efficient protection. Reply solicited.

(Signed) LOO YUEN
Director

(Note: Received for translation A.M. 11th Dec. 1937.)

无线电台与日本人

由于形势所迫，我方于不久前暂时停工，并请求工部局充分保护我们在国际租界内的房屋、土地、机器及其他财产。随后，我们收到位于静安寺路591弄的电报站、马克姆路（Markham Road）的发射台以及霞飞路（Joffre Road）的广播站的报告，称各种机器和一辆卡车被日本人搬走。我们致函工部局要求采取行动。现又收到静安寺路591弄电报站的另一份报告，称本月10日，日本人再次用一辆卡车和一辆汽车从该站搬走了许多接收机和打字机；此案也已向成都路警察局报案并记录在案。出于对财产权益的维护，请工部局关注此事并提供有效保护。盼复。

（签名）陆元（LOO YUEN，音译）
局长

Made by D.S.I. Watson. Forwarded by O. S. Perkins Inspr. I/C

Sir,

Further to the report regarding the above subject which was forwarded on 30/11/37, I beg to submit the following details regarding the removal of equipment by members of the Japanese Armed Forces on 17/12/37.

At 8-15am. on 17, S.I. Alexandroff observed four motor trucks carrying Japanese Naval Officers and other ranks, also soldiers and apparently reservists, entering the Radio Station. They were not carrying arms, but several rifles were seen on the drivers' seats.

S.I. Chang and two constables were posted on Markham Road Bridge to note developments.

Centers of the 4th. U.S.M.C. on duty at Markham Road Bridge observed the party arriving, and communicated with their senior officers. Captain Cole attended the scene and entered the Radio Station to find that equipment was being loaded on to the trucks. J.P.C.s 108 and 110 from Gordon Road Station were on duty inside the building, and through them Captain Cole suggested that the Japanese forces should have communicated with the U.S.M.Corps.

Lieut-Colonel Rupertus, U.S.M.C., later telephoned to Inspector Perkins, i/c Sinza Station, and stating that he was considering a protest to the Japanese Authorities, asked that an interpreter be sent to the Radio Station to assist Captain Cole.

D.D.O. "B" was communicated with, and S.I. Nakane, Gordon Road Station, was sent to the scene.

先生，

继1937年11月30日提交的关于上述主题的报告之后，谨就1937年12月17日日本武装部队成员搬走设备一事，提交以下详情。

17日上午8时15分，印度籍巡长 Alexandroff 观察到四辆载有日本海军军官及其他军衔人员、士兵以及似乎是预备役人员的卡车进入无线电台。他们未携带武器，但在驾驶座上发现数支步枪。

张姓（Chang，音译）印籍巡长及两名华捕被部署在马克姆路桥上以观察事态发展。

当时在马克姆路桥执勤的美国海军陆战队第四团中心哨位观察到该伙人到达，并与他们的上级军官取得联系。科尔（Cole）上尉赶赴现场并进入无线电台，发现设备正在被装上卡车。来自戈登路警署的日本籍巡捕 108号和 110号在大楼内执勤，科尔上尉通过他们建议日军应与美国海军陆战队进行沟通。

后来，美国海军陆战队鲁珀特斯（Rupertus）中校致电新闸警署主管帕金斯（Perkins）警司，表示他正考虑向日本当局提出抗议，并要求派遣一名翻译前往无线电台协助科尔上尉。

已与"B"区副总监联系，戈登路警署的中根（Nakane，音译）印籍巡长被派往现场。

Dated 7th Dec 1937, F337281b/
Date 9 / 12 / 37

Radio Station and Japanese

Some time ago the Japanese military authorities sent officers
to our radiogram station in Bubbling Well Road and attempted to
take forcible possession; for this reason we suspended operations.
On 28th November we addressed a letter (No.1001) to the Council
asking for protection for our houses, land, machinery and other
property in the International Settlement, and on 29th we sent a
representative to call to make verbal arrangements.

According to reports the Japanese on the 30th ultimo removed
two receiving machines of the Marconi type from our Radiogram
Station at Nos.149 and 151, Lane 591, Bubbling Well Road. The
protest lodged by the watchman on the premises and the remonstra-
tion of a British Policeman from the Chengtu Road Police Station
were ignored. The Japanese also drove away truck No.16296 parked
at our transmitting station, No.145, "irkham Road"; they forced
their way through a window into our Broadcasting Station, No.29
Lane 8, Love Lane and seized one receiving machine and accessories.
Such audacious acts on the part of the Japanese soldiery not only
encroach upon the right of ownership but also endanger the peace
and good order of the Settlement. The Council is asked to recover
the seized property for us as soon as possible. Reply solicited.

(Chopped) Po Lu-yung
Director

(Note: Received for translation a.m. 8th Dec. 1937.)

日期：1937年12月9日

电台与日本人

不久前，日本军方派遣军官前往我方位于静安寺路的无线电报站，企图强行占领；为此，我们暂停了运营。11月28日，我方致信工部局（第1001号），请求保护我们在公共租界内的房屋、土地、机器及其他财产，并于29日派代表前往进行口头协商。

据报道，上月30日，日本人从我方位于静安寺路591弄149和151号的无线电报站搬走了两台马可尼型接收机。现场看守提出的抗议以及成都路捕房一名英籍巡捕的交涉均被无视。日本人还驱走了停在我方位于“irkham Road”（原文不清，疑为Markham Road）145号发射站的第16296号卡车；他们强行破窗进入我方位于爱文义路8弄29号的广播电台，抢走了一台接收机及配件。日本军人的这种大胆行径不仅侵犯了所有权，也危及租界的和平与良好秩序。恳请工部局尽快为我方追回被扣财产。盼复。

（盖章）鲍鲁永
局长

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Damage Done to Japanese Owned Property.

On the 7th instant, a telephone message was received from the Sikongtu Road Police Station (白石路), stating that a report had been made to the effect that a window had been broken at the Radio Station, No. 155, Sikongtu Road.

C. P.C. 1114 and number of the Japanese Consul's Guard were on duty at the spot at 11 a.m. It appears that they saw two men break the window, but were unable to apprehend them as they ran away immediately after breaking the window.

They have not yet been identified.

The victims alleged the two unknown men were Japanese.

The Japanese Consul's police later informed this station that no Japanese subjects had been in the vicinity of the Radio Station at the time the window was smashed.

The above place ceased functioning as a Radio Station on 8-11-37 when a party of Japanese removed part of the Radio Equipment. (Misc. 155/37). No one resides or works on the premises.

（印：DETECTIVE DIVISION）

At 11.15 a.m. November 29, 1937, a quantity of miscellaneous radio equipment, including one receiving set and one loud speaker, was taken away from the Chinese Government Radio Broadcasting Station at No. 29, Lane 58, Love Lane by the Japanese Authorities.

According to the private watchman employed in the lane, thirteen Japanese in plain clothes and two in military uniform wearing arm bands stating that they were military police arrived at the place in three motor cars, and gained entry to the premises by climbing the wall of the small court yard.

No report of the removal of the equipment was made through official channels.

Officer in charge.

May 16th, 1938.

The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Foochow Road,
Shanghai.

Sir,

Having been granted by you to open our business as a broadcasting station, we have tried our best to select the contents of our programmes in order to avoid unnecessary misunderstanding and make our station conducted on pure commerical nature.

On last Friday, 13th. inst. at 3 p.m., we were much astonished to be told by you to cease broadcasting until further notice.

We learned that this Order was due to the story told during the period at 8. - 8.45 on Thursday evening, 12th. instant.

This story was told by a professional story-teller Sung Jiu-ying with regard to the history of the three-hundred years reign of Tsin dynasty. After careful investigation, we wish to state that there is nothing referring to the present political or international affairs and further more this story has been many times told in the air by the same person during the programmes of other stations recently. Therefore we did not excluded this programme in the first instance.

Now we admit the error and decide not to allow this Story-teller to broadcast any longer in our Station, and will pay special attention to the contents of our all programmes in future.

We beg to ask your kind permission to restore our broadcasting and allow us to carry on our business as usual.

Thanking you,

we are, Sir,

Yours respectfully,

Dah Kwong Ming Broadcasting
Station.

1938年5月16日。

警察总监，
上海工部局，
福州路，
上海。

先生：

承蒙贵方批准我方作为广播电台开业，我们已尽力甄选节目内容，以避免不必要的误解，并使本台保持纯粹的商业性质。

上周五，即本月13日下午3时，获悉贵方命令我方停止播音，直至另行通知，对此我们深感惊讶。

我们得知，此项命令是由于本月12日（星期四）晚上8点至8点45分期间播出的一段故事所致。

该故事由职业说书人宋久英（Sung Jiu-ying，音译）讲述，内容涉及清朝三百年的统治历史。经仔细调查，我们要声明，其中并无涉及当前政治或国际事务的内容，而且近期同一人在其他电台的节目中也多次讲述过这个故事。因此，我们起初并未将该节目排除在外。

现在我们承认错误，并决定不再允许这位说书人在本台播音，今后我们将特别注意所有节目的内容。

恳请贵方恩准恢复我们的播音，允许我们照常经营业务。

此致，

敬礼，

大光明广播电台。

COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE.

Translation of a letter from Great Asia Broadcasting Station, Shanghai.
May 13, 1938.

Commissioner of Police,
S. M. P.

Sir,

In connection with your notification received by us at 12.30 p.m. on the 12th inst. instructing us to stop broadcasting forthwith as the humourous program broadcasted by Liu Chuen San at 8.15 p.m. on the 11th inst. has something to do with political problems, we have to submit the fact that on that evening Liu broadcasted at first the advertisement of the Hwa Chen Tobacco Co. following which he reported the contents of his personal draft letters. At that time we were under the impression that what he would broadcast were of advertising nature and were not aware that his private letters had bearings on political problems until his broadcasting intimating letters critising Liu had been sent out.

Therefore, we submit the above for your information with the request that our broadcasting service be resumed to maintain our business, thus obliging.

(Chopped) Great Asia Broadcasting Station.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。

先生：

关于我们于本月12日中午12时30分收到的通知，指令我们立即停止播音，原因是刘春山（Liu Chuen San）于本月11日晚上8时15分播出的幽默节目涉及政治问题，我们必须陈述如下事实：当晚，刘春山首先播出了华成烟草公司的广告，随后播报了他个人草稿信的内容。当时我们以为他播出的内容是广告性质的，并未意识到他的私人信件涉及政治问题，直到他播出暗示批评刘某的信件为止。

因此，特将上述情况呈报贵方知悉，并请求恢复我们的广播服务以维持我们的业务，不胜感激。

May 13, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

COMEDIAN LIU TSUNG-SAN PUBLISHES ADVERTISEMENT

The following advertisement appears in the
"Sin Wan Pao" and other local newspapers on May 13, 1938:-
Lawyer Sih Li-sun (薛麗生), who has been
appointed by Mr. Liu Tsung-san (劉宗山) as his legal
advisor, publishes the following notice on behalf of his
client:-
"I have been appointed by Mr. Liu Tsung-san
as his legal advisor and will hereafter give him legal
protection should anybody impair his business, his
reputation or his interests. Mr. Liu has made the
following statement to me:-
'I was much surprised to read in the local
leading newspapers during the past few days reports
about broadcasting stations in which my name has
been mentioned. I am at a loss to know where
these reports come from. I have been engaged in
the amusements business for more than ten years.
I am known to the public as a comedian who deals
with up-to-date topics, but as a matter of fact I
am interested in social education and in the course
of my work, I always persuade people to do good
and to correct their habits.
'On the outbreak of hostilities in Shanghai,
I made appeals, through the broadcasting stations,
for the relief of refugees. I am very busy with
stage work and with broadcasting and I have no time
to attend meetings on social functions nor am I
being utilized by anybody. The public have sent
me letters containing advice and I will observe
their wishes. But on some points which are
incorrect, I have to deal with them, otherwise these
incorrect reports are liable to mislead the public
and do me harm. I request you to publish a
notice in the newspapers on my behalf to explain
any misunderstanding that may have arisen and to
protect my reputation.'
"I hereby publish this notice on behalf of
my client.

喜剧演员刘宗山刊登广告

以下广告刊登于1938年5月13日的《新闻报》及其他本地报纸上：-
薛丽生律师，受刘宗山先生委任为其法律顾问，代表其客户发布如下通告：-
“本人受刘宗山先生委任为其法律顾问，今后若有人损害其业务、声誉或利益，本人将为其提供法律保护。刘先生向本人作了如下陈述：
‘近日我在本地主要报纸上看到提及我的广播电台相关报道，深感惊讶。我不清楚这些报道源自何处。我从事娱乐业已十余年。公众知我是一名涉及时事话题的喜剧演员，但事实上，我关注社会教育，在工作中始终劝人向善并纠正陋习。
’上海战事爆发时，我曾通过广播电台呼吁救济难民。我忙于舞台演出和广播工作，无暇参加社交活动会议，也未受任何人利用。公众寄来含有建议的信件，我将遵从他们的意愿。但对于某些不实的说法，我必须予以处理，否则这些不实报道容易误导公众并对我造成伤害。我请求你代表我在报纸上刊登通告，以澄清可能产生的误解并维护我的声誉。’
“本人谨代表客户发布此通告。

C. P.

I have been officially requested by the
Japanese Military Authorities that rigorous steps be
taken by the S.M.P. to suspend the undermentioned
Chinese broadcasting stations in the Settlement without
delay as they continue to disseminate propaganda of anti-
Japanese nature and maintain an antagonistic attitude
towards the Japanese military.

I am of the opinion that necessary measures be taken
by the S.M.P. to suppress these stations for otherwise
the continuation of this state of affairs is likely to
lead to some unpleasant incidents thereby adversely
affecting peace and good order of the Settlement.

The radio stations the Japanese Military Authorities
take exception to are:-

(1) The Dah Ya Broadcasting Station, 545 Hwa Ngoh
Fong (大亚电台,
(九江路華安坊10号)), Kiukiang Road, and

(2) The Dah Kwong Ming Broadcasting Station(大光明电台),
548 Park Road.

Deputy Commissioner (Japanese).

P. A.
Put up report as soon when established,
amend, if come before action details.
EARLY.

Date MAY 5, 19 38.
Subject Dah Yah Broadcasting Station - receives despatch from
Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.I.

The Dah Yah (大亞) Broadcasting Station, 545
Kiukiang Road (1,280 k.c. - Xma') received on the afternoon
of May 4, 1938, notification no.4 from the Japanese
Broadcasting Superintendence Office, Nardoon building,
Nanking Road, ordering it to suspend broadcasting for
failing to register with the office. According to the
document, the management of the station will be subject
to severe punishment, should it again ignore this order.
A copy of the order, together with translation, is
attached.

It is to be noted that the Dah Yah Broadcasting
Station is newly established, and application for permission
to operate was made to the Municipal Police Headquarters
(Vide Special Branch report dated April 6, 1938). The
station also forwarded to the Police Headquarters on
April 29, particulars required for registration with the
Broadcasting Superintendence Office.

In view of the fact that negotiations are still
in progress between the S.M.C. and the Japanese authorities
on the subject of supervision in the Settlement and
registration of Chinese Broadcasting Stations (vide
Commissioner of Police's memo dated May 4, 1938, to D.C.
(Special Branch)), it is difficult to understand the reason for
sending the notification mentioned to the Dah Yah Broadcasting
Station unless they hope by doing so to force the issue in
the case of this particular station.

D. C. (Special Branch)
F. A. to D. C. (Sp. Br.)
Logan
D. S. I.

值得注意的是，大亚广播电台是新近成立的，并向警务处总部申请了运营许可（参见1938年4月6日的特务科报告）。该电台还于4月29日向警务处总部 forwarded 了向广播监理事务所注册所需的具体信息。

鉴于上海工部局与日本当局仍在就租界内的监管和中国广播电台注册问题进行谈判（参见1938年5月4日警务处处长致特务科副总监的备忘录），很难理解向大亚广播电台发送上述通知的原因，除非他们希望通过此举在这一特定电台的案件中迫使问题得到解决。

（批：C.P. Better keep closed unless D.C.(J) thinks Military have some use for it? H.M. Yes G.P.7 D.C.(J) Copy and file B 18 DEC 1937 D.C.(J) For further comment）
（印：SPECIAL BRANCH M3 21 DEC 1937 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）

In accordance with instructions received, members of the Special Branch accompanied by representatives of the S.P.O. and Chengtu Road Station visited No.395 Bubbling Well Road at 4.05 p.m. December 17, 1937.

In a room on the 2nd floor of the above mentioned premises, which are now occupied by the Lien Mei Tobacco Company, was found a radio transmitter of 50 watt power.

Inquiries revealed that this station operated on a wave length of 1240 metres with the call sign X.M.H.Y., and was known as the Lee Lee Broadcasting Station. The owner of this station is Wong Wei Ts (王緯之), who resides at 417 Chekiang Road. From him it was ascertained that prior to the outbreak of hostilities in August, the Lee Lee Station operated from 9, An Kyi Terrace, North Tibet Road. The station, Mr. Wong stated, registered with the Ministry of Communications and broadcast programmes of a commercial and advertising nature.

From August until December 6, when it was transferred, the station suspended operations. On transfer the transmitter and other necessary apparatus were leased to the above mentioned tobacco company and installed in the company's premises at 395 Bubbling Well Road. Since that date, Mr. Wong stated, no regular programmes had been transmitted, but, he said, there had been several test broadcasts.

Mr. Woo Ts Chuan (吳表權), a representative of the Lien Mei Tobacco Company, stated that only programmes of a commercial nature had been transmitted. The station was closed and a C.P.C. from Chengtu Road Station posted to ensure that operations ceased pending further investigation.

根据收到的指示，特科成员会同特别政治官员（S.P.O.）代表及成都路巡捕房人员，于1937年12月17日下午4时05分访问了静安寺路395号。

在上述 premises（现由联美烟草公司占用）的二楼房间内，发现了一台功率为50瓦的无线电发射机。

经查询，该电台工作波长为1240米，呼号为X.M.H.Y.，被称为“Lee Lee”广播电台。该电台业主为王緯之（Wong Wei Ts），居住于浙江路417号。据王先生称，在八月战事爆发前，“Lee Lee”电台在北西藏路安基里9号运营。王先生表示，该电台已在交通部注册，播放商业和广告性质的节目。

从八月至12月6日迁移期间，该电台暂停运营。迁移时，发射机及其他必要设备租赁给上述烟草公司，并安装在公司位于静安寺路395号的 premises 内。王先生称，自那以后，未播放常规节目，但他说进行过几次试播。

联美烟草公司代表吳表權（Mr. Woo Ts Chuan）先生表示，仅播放过商业性质的节目。电台已关闭，并由成都路巡捕房派出一名华籍巡捕（C.P.C.）驻守，以确保在进一步调查之前停止运营。

With reference to the attached anonymous

Station referred to is located on the roof of

ascertained the Station is used for transmitting
morse code to ships on the China coast by the
Shipping Department of Reuter, Brockelmann and
Company, and is operated by a Chinese named Sz
Ngoh Kyi (施玉麒).

At 11 a.m., July 29, 1940, Mr. O. Zwank,
Chief of the Technical and Stationery Department,
was interviewed by D.S.I. Logan. He admitted
that the Station in question is owned and operated
by his Company but claimed that he was not in
possession of details of wave length, call sign,
etc. According to Mr. Zwank, the Station is used
solely for communicating with ships on the China
coast by the Shipping Department of his firm.

Information has been received that the
Station transmits on 46 metres and that the call
sign is D.L.M. but it has not been possible to
confirm this information.

Shanghai, October 23rd 1939.
525, Avenue Foch.

The Chief of Police
SMP
SHANGHAI

（印：COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE）

Sir,
I am herewith complaining against a chinese commercial transmitting station, situated at 354 Seymour Road, House 5, 2nd floor.
This station is transmitting code telegraph day and night and is creating such a noise that no one is able to sleep.
On the other hand, their transmissions are on all the bands & frequencies that no radio reception can be heard with such a nuisance.
I do understand that no transmitting station is allowed within the limits of the city or at a residential quarter, disturbing the quietness of the people and also all radio receptions.
I heard that these chinese or who they are, are making S$1000 every day by sending their telegrams to Chungking or elsewhere.
If so, they have plenty of money to put their station elsewhere, in a business quarter of the city.
My complaint is not a suggestion of myself alone, but from everybody leaving in this quarter and, if necessary, I am willing to let sign this complaint by every body concerned.
Your testing on XSMP last evening was greatly inconvenienced by hum and interferences on this band, was nothing and nobody else, as this mentionned station.
I would and also every body would, be grateful to you if you could do something in this matter.
With my best thanks,

Yours truly.
Oscar P. Gendre

先生，
本人特此投诉位于西摩路354号5幢2楼的一家中资商业发射台。
该台日夜发送码式电报，产生的噪音使人无法入睡。
另一方面，他们的发射占据了所有波段和频率，导致在此类滋扰下无法收听任何无线电广播。
本人深知，市区内或住宅区内不得设立发射台，以免扰乱民众安宁及干扰所有无线电接收。
本人听说这些中国人或其他什么人，通过向重庆或其他地方发送电报，每天赚取1000银元。
若是如此，他们有足够的资金将电台迁至城市的商业区。
本人的投诉并非仅仅代表个人，而是代表居住在该街区的所有人，如有必要，本人愿意让所有相关人士在此投诉信上签名。
昨晚贵处在 XSMP 进行的测试受到该波段嗡嗡声和干扰的严重妨碍，而这除了上述电台外，别无其他来源。
若您能对此事采取某些措施，本人及所有人均将不胜感激。
谨致谢忱，

REPORT    Date April 26, 1939.
Subject Letter from Mr. A. R. St. Louis of Frost, Bland & Co., Ltd.:
Proposal to establish Radio Station to transmit weather reports to
Coast Shipping in Chinese.
Made by D.J.T. Logan    Forwarded by C. Crawford

Mr. A. R. St. Louis was interviewed on 26.4.39 in
his office at 190 Kiukiang Road in regard to his
proposal to establish a Radio Station in the Settlement
for the purpose of transmitting Zikawei Observatory
weather reports in the Chinese language to Chinese
mariners on the China Coast and Yangtsze Delta, when
he explained that the primary purpose of the station
would be to make weather reports available to Chinese
shipping though a programme of Chinese music will also
be broadcast during the two hour morning, afternoon
and evening periods when the broadcast will take place.
It was pointed out to Mr. St. Louis that the S.M.C.
would neither grant nor withhold permission for the
establishment of the station and also that as far as is
known practically the entire wave band covering the
local area is already occupied. In reply, Mr. St.
Louis stated that he hoped to arrive at an arrangement
with either the Sun Sun Radio Station (XLnA) K.C. 800
or the Dah Wei Radio Station (XHM) K.C. 1140, whereby
one of these stations will agree to go off the air
during the two hour periods mentioned while the
weather report broadcasts are being made and that full
particulars concerning whatever arrangement is reached,
location of the proposed station, etc., will be
communicated to the Police in due course.
Mr. St. Louis does not intend to seek the permission
of the Japanese Radio Control Office concerning his
proposed station.
D.C. (Special Branch)    D. J. T.

24th April, 1939.

The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

Dear Sirs,

We have been requested to establish a 100 Watt Broadcasting Station in Shanghai for Chinese transmission only and would seek the necessary authority to place such a Station in operation.

Primarily, the purpose of this Station will be to relay in the Chinese language, weather reports obtained from the Ziccawei Observatory to Chinese mariners on the China Coast and Yangtsze Delta.

At this moment weather reports are transmitted in the Morse Code and are broadcast by English speaking Stations at various times throughout the day, but no particular provision is made for the transmission of weather warnings in Chinese.

Under the proper authority we are prepared to establish this Station and would make a 100 Watt Carrier power unit, crystal controlled as to frequency, of modern design.

Hours of operation would be mainly for two hours in the morning; two hours in the afternoon and two hours in the evening; and in addition to the weather broadcast, an ordinary Chinese programme would be transmitted.

We would greatly appreciate if you would advise us as to the proper steps to take in order to secure official sanction for this Station.

Yours faithfully,
FROST, BLAND & CO., LTD.

A. R. St. Louis

尊敬的先生们，

我们受委托在上海建立一座功率为100瓦的广播电台，仅用于中文广播，并寻求必要的授权以使该台投入运营。

该台的主要目的是将以中文转播从徐家汇天文台获得的气象报告，提供给中国沿海和长江三角洲的中国海员。

目前，气象报告以莫尔斯电码发送，并由讲英语的电台在全天不同时间广播，但没有专门安排用中文传输气象预警。

在获得适当授权的情况下，我们准备建立该电台，并将制造一台现代设计的、频率由晶体控制的100瓦载波功率单元。

运营时间主要为早晨两小时；下午两小时和晚上两小时；除气象广播外，还将播出普通中文节目。

如蒙告知为获得该电台官方批准所需采取的正确步骤，我们将不胜感激。

Subject Information given by Mr. H. P. Krogh, Great Northern Telegraph
Co. - Pirate radio station believed receiving messages from Tientsin
and transmitting same to Chartered Bank of India, Australia & China.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by /s/ Logan DSI
（批：29/6/38 29/6/38）

At 10 a.m., 27.6.38, Mr. H. P. Krogh of the Great
Northern Telegraph Co. visited Special Branch, Headquarters
and reported that he had obtained information from Chinese
sources that both the Chartered Bank of India, Australia
and China, 18 The Bund, and The Chase Bank, 99 Nanking Road,
have recently been receiving wireless telegraph messages
from Tientsin through some American believed to have his
station or office in the vicinity of Szechuen Road. Mr.
Krogh was unable to give any clue to the identity of the
American or to give a description of him but promised to
endeavour to obtain some description of the person delivering
the messages to the different banks.

Mr. Krogh was informed that apart from the fact that
the Police are interested in knowing the identity of persons
engaged in transmitting wireless messages, there is
practically no legal machinery for the control of such of
those persons who enjoy extra-territoriality rights.

In connection with the foregoing information it is
worthy of note that Capt. A. R. St. Louis has a station at
Kiukiang Road, with which Mr. Al. Lucy (American) is
connected in some way. Mr. Lucy is one of the wireless
pioneers in this area and could therefore quite conceivably
be in touch with amateur radio enthusiasts or others in
North China. Mr. Mense, in charge of C.C.R., has been
informed and will report any further information received.

/s/ Logan
D. S. I.

事由 大北电报公司 H. P. Krogh 先生提供的情报 - 据信有一海盗电台接收来自天津的电讯，并将其转发至印度新金山中国汇理银行。
由副督察长 Logan 制作 转呈人 /s/ Logan 副督察长
（批：29/6/38 29/6/38）

1938年6月27日上午10时，大北电报公司的 H. P. Krogh 先生造访警务处总部特务科，报告称他从中方消息来源获悉，位于外滩18号的印度新金山中国汇理银行以及位于南京路99号的大通银行（The Chase Bank），最近均通过某位美国人接收来自天津的无线电报讯息，该美国人的电台或办事处据信位于四川路附近。Krogh 先生无法提供关于该美国人身份的任何线索或其外貌描述，但承诺将尽力获取向各家银行递送讯息之人的相关描述。

已告知 Krogh 先生，除了警方对查明从事无线电讯息发送人员的身份感兴趣这一事实外，实际上并无法律机制来管控那些享有治外法权的人员。

就上述情报而言，值得注意的是，A. R. St. Louis 上尉在九江路设有一处电台，美国人 Al. Lucy 以某种方式与其有关联。Lucy 先生是本地区无线电领域的先驱之一，因此完全有可能与华北地区的业余无线电爱好者或其他人士保持联系。中央无线电台（C.C.R.）负责人 Mense 先生已获知此事，并将报告收到的任何进一步信息。

/s/ Logan
副督察长

Sir,

Referring to your letter of April 27 regarding private radio transmission installations, you are undoubtedly aware that radio transmission is a matter of National Government control supplemented by international agreement.

The International Settlement is not in any sense a National Government and has no legal power to control radio transmission.

Foreign owned installations in so far as the Council is concerned are under the jurisdiction of the local judicial authorities of their respective governments.

Prior to the outbreak of hostilities between China and Japan the Nationalist Government of China exercised a partial control over radio transmission which, in the case of foreign owned installations, was more or less by consent for obvious reasons of expediency.

Since the outbreak of hostilities the Council has exercised to some extent emergency police powers to prevent Chinese owned installations from broadcasting matters which would intensify the tension between Chinese and Japanese or tend to disturb the peace and good order of the Settlement.

国际租界在任何意义上都不是一个国民政府，没有管制无线电发射的法律权力。

就工部局而言，外商拥有的装置受其各自政府当地司法当局的管辖。

在中日敌对行动爆发之前，中国国民政府对无线电发射行使部分控制权，对于外商拥有的装置，出于明显的权宜原因，这种控制或多或少是基于同意的。

自敌对行动爆发以来，工部局在一定程度上行使了紧急警察权力，以防止中方拥有的装置广播会加剧中日紧张局势或倾向于扰乱租界和平与良好秩序的事项。

就工部局而言，外商拥有的装置受其各自政府当地司法当局的管辖。

在中日敌对行动爆发之前，中国国民政府对无线电发射行使部分控制权，对于外商拥有的装置，出于明显的权宜原因，这种控制或多或少是基于同意的。

自敌对行动爆发以来，工部局在一定程度上行使了紧急警察权力，以防止中方拥有的装置广播

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford

Further to Special Branch report on above subject, dated 3.5.38, Central Registry file No. 2938, in which the intention of Capt. A.R. St. Louis to establish a commercial radio station with connections in Manila, etc., is referred to, Mr. N.D. Brown of the Robert Dollar Steam Ship Co., visited Special Branch, Headquarters, and complained that he had heard several rumours to the effect that Capt. St. Louis was giving people to understand that his proposed British Radio Company, 220 Kiukiang Road, had completed arrangements with the Globe Wireless Company, Manila, for the receiving of wireless telegraph messages by the latter concern. Mr. Brown, who is the Shanghai representative of Globe Wireless Co. in Shanghai, while admitting that Capt. St. Louis had approached him in connection with his wireless project denied that any arrangement had been made and expressed a doubt that it could be arranged. He was informed that Capt. St. Louis had never intimated to the Shanghai Municipal Police that he had completed arrangements with Globe Wireless. It appears that the Globe Wireless Co. is a subsidiary company of the Robert Dollar Company, as also is the Heintz and Kaufman Radio Manufactures Company, Los Angles, which formerly supplied wireless equipment to the Chinese Government and that Mr. Brown is local agent. Mr. Brown appeared relieved when informed that Capt. St. Louis had not mentioned his name to the Police and left the Special Branch stating that he was going to take the matter up direct with Capt. St. Louis so that a stop may be put to current rumours.

D.C.(Special Branch)
D.S.I.

With reference to the attached copy of a letter
dated April 27, 1938, addressed jointly by The Great
Northern Telegraph Co., Ltd. The Eastern Extension
Australasia & China Telegraph Co., Ltd., and the Commercial
Pacific Cable Co. to the Chairman of the Shanghai Municipal
Council on the subject of the unfair competition to which
their legitimately established concerns are being exposed
by the activities of private radio installations, certain
of which are suspected of operating on a commercial basis,
and requesting that adequate steps be taken by the
Shanghai Municipal Council to "prevent the continuation,
enlargement or extension of the practice", D.S.I. Logan
called upon Mr. .... Poulsen, General Manager in the Far
East, of the Great Northern Telegraph Co., at 2 p.m.
April 29, 1938. Mr. Poulsen stated that his complaint
was directed, not so much at the private radio installations
which are being operated by certain large firms locally,
which are in the nature of emergency necessities due to
the peculiar existing conditions, as at private radio
installations which are reputed either to be accepting,
or preparing to accept, messages for transmission on a
commercial basis. Asked to give details of any particular
concern, Mr. Poulsen stated that he was not in possession
of any concrete facts but that he had good reason to
believe that Capt. A.R. St. Louis, Engineering, Electrical
specialities and Communications, 190 and 220 Kiukiang Road,
was completing arrangements to undertake large scale
transmission of messages to Manila and perhaps elsewhere.

兹提及附后之1938年4月27日信函副本，该函由大北电报有限公司、东方延线澳中电报有限公司及太平洋商业电缆公司联合致上海公共租界工部局总董，事由为其合法设立的企业因私人无线电装置的活动而遭受不正当竞争，其中部分装置涉嫌以商业基础运营，并请求上海公共租界工部局采取适当措施以“防止该做法的持续、扩大或延伸”。特别处督察长洛根于1938年4月29日下午2时拜访了大北电报公司远东总经理波尔森（Poulsen）先生。波尔森先生表示，其投诉所指并非当地某些大公司运营的、因当前特殊局势而具有应急性质的私人无线电装置，而是那些据称正在接受或准备接受以商业基础传输信息的私人无线电装置。当被要求提供具体公司的详情时，波尔森先生表示他手头没有任何确凿事实，但他有充分理由相信，位于九江路190号和220号、从事工程、电气专业及通讯业务的A.R.圣路易斯（A.R. St. Louis）上尉，正在完成安排，以承担向马尼拉及可能其他地方大规模传输信息的工作。

In this connection he mentioned that the Globe Wireless
Co., Manila, Philippine Islands, would in all probability
act as receiving agent in the latter city. The Globe
Wireless Co. is regarded as a "pirate" wireless service
having connections in U.S.A. Several attempts have been
made from time to time to have it suppressed but all
legal steps taken in this direction proved unsuccessful.

Concerning other private stations, Mr. Poulsen
stated that he had no definite information but that a
suspicion is gaining strength in the minds of cable
company executives locally, that certain local firms are
extending the use of their private installations beyond
what might be regarded as the necessary requirements of
the prevailing conditions, e.g. the Robert Dollar Steamship
Co. is suspected of using their private installation
to transmit ordinary messages to Hongkong and Manila
which normally should go by one of the cable routes.
Other firms are similarly suspected, but it is questionable
if any legal objection could be raised as long as such
firms confine the use of their private installations
strictly to their own messages and do not accept messages
for transmission on a commercial basis.

However, there is reason to believe that certain
firms accept and transmit messages on a commission basis,
but such traffic is light and mostly to places where cable
facilities do not exist or have become temporarily
unavailable.

在此方面，他提到菲律宾群岛马尼拉的环球无线公司（Globe Wireless Co.）极有可能在该市充当接收代理。环球无线公司被视为一家与美国有联系的“海盗”无线服务机构。不时有人试图予以取缔，但为此采取的所有法律步骤均证明无效。

关于其他私人电台，波尔森先生表示他没有确切信息，但当地电缆公司高管心中的怀疑日益增强，即某些本地公司将其私人装置的使用范围扩展到了超出当前局势下必要需求的程度，例如，罗伯特·多尔轮船公司（Robert Dollar Steamship Co.）被怀疑利用其私人装置向香港和马尼拉发送普通信息，而这些信息通常应通过某条电缆线路传输。其他公司也受到类似怀疑，但只要这些公司将其私人装置的使用严格限制在自有信息范围内，且不接收以商业基础传输的信息，是否还能提出任何法律异议则存疑。

然而，有理由相信某些公司以佣金为基础接收和传输信息，但此类业务量不大，且主要发往没有电缆设施或电缆设施暂时无法使用的地方。

Enquiries at French Police Headquarters elicited
the information that Capt. A.R. St. Louis unofficially
approached the French Authorities recently and sounded
them on the possibility of his being permitted to
install a radio broadcasting and receiving station in
the French Concession for the purpose of undertaking
the transmission of commercial messages and also press
information on behalf of United Press Association and
certain other news agencies which are believed to have been
approached by Capt. St. Louis. The French Authorities
refused permission.
In the course of an interview with D.S.I. Logan
at 11.30 a.m. May 2, 1938, Capt. A.R. St. Louis, who
has a desk in the office of Frost, Bland & Co., Ltd.,
Engineers & Merchants, 190 Kiukiang Road, frankly
admitted that he is endeavouring to complete arrangements
for the establishing of a commercial wireless transmitting
station which will be operated at 220 Kiukiang Road.
The name of the service will be British Radio Company
and the trade name, "Bradco". Capt. St. Louis stated
that all the necessary equipment has been installed
and successful tests carried out between Shanghai and
Manila. The transmission of messages will be undertaken
as soon as contracts and arrangements are made with the
Globe Wireless, Manila, after which it is proposed to
extend the service to Batavia and if permission can be
obtained from the proper authorities, to Hongkong and

Our Companies strongly feel that if this state of
affairs is allowed to continue, or if the number of privately
operated radio installations is even allowed to increase, the
inevitable result will be a state of chaos in the communications
of Shanghai that will be ruinous to the regular communication
concerns, and detrimental, and in the long run disastrous, to the
public and to the Community. In this connection we would like to
point out that the regular and legitimate communication enterprises
are Public Utility concerns paying terminal charges etc. to the
concessionary Governments and operating a general and recognized
service with all parts of the world, including many unremunerative
circuits, and that private and irregular enterprises paying no such
charges and rendering only a limited service in a limited area are
consequently competing upon an unfair basis. Also we would like to
mention that in allowing private concerns to operate radio installa-
tions for their own use a special favour is granted to certain large
telegraph users as compared to general users of the telegraph ser-
vices in Shanghai.

In placing the above views before you we beg to express
our sincere hope, therefore, that, in the interest of the legitimate
telegraph enterprises, and of the general public and the community
such steps as are considered necessary and available will be taken
to prevent the continuation, enlargement or extension of the prac-
tice of operating private radio installations in the International
Settlement of Shanghai.

A similar letter has been forwarded to the Consul General
for France in Shanghai.

敝公司强烈认为，如果允许这种状况持续下去，或者甚至允许私人运营的无线电装置数量增加，不可避免的结果将是上海通讯陷入混乱，这将摧毁正规通讯企业，并对公众和社区造成损害，从长远来看更是灾难性的。在此方面，我们要指出，正规合法的通讯企业是公用事业机构，向租界当局支付终端费等费用，并向世界各地（包括许多无利可图的线路）提供普遍且公认的服务，而私人和不规范的企业不支付此类费用，仅在有限区域内提供有限服务，因此是在不公平的基础上进行竞争。此外，我们要提及，允许私人企业为其自身使用运营无线电装置，相较于上海电报服务的一般用户而言，是对某些大型电报用户的特殊优待。

在向阁下陈述上述观点之际，我们谨表达诚挚的希望，为了合法电报企业以及广大公众和社区的利益，将采取被认为必要且可行的措施，以防止在上海公共租界内运营私人无线电装置的做法继续、扩大或延伸。
