（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / Shanghai, April 27th 1938 / No. F 5402 / Date 28 / 4 / 38）

Dear Sir,

From time to time our Companies have received rumours
and information of private radio transmission stations being
put up and operated in the French Concession and the International
Settlement of Shanghai, and it appears that the present Sino-
Japanese hostilities have acted as an extra stimulant in this
respect, probably because it is generally believed by the public
that the enforcement of the international rules prohibiting the
establishment and working of such stations by individual persons,
or by any enterprise, without special licences issued by the
Government to which the stations in question are subject, is left
in suspense for the time being.

Whilst prior to the conflict only certain newspaper
agencies and firms appeared to operate private radio stations
for receiving and/or sending their own telegrams, it appears
from reliable information received by us that a number of firms
and individuals have established, or are making arrangements for
establishing, private radio installations and work them in com-
petition with the regular and legitimate communication channels.
Furthermore we have learned recently that at least one firm has
put up an installation capable of exchanging international tele-
grams on a large scale with such stations abroad, i.e. in Manila,
as are in a position to co-operate with a view to handling tele-
graphic messages to and from the general public in competition
with the legitimate communication enterprises.

TO THE CHAIRMAN
OF THE SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL,
SHANGHAI.

敬启者：

敝公司不时收到有关在法租界及上海公共租界内设立并运营私人无线电台的传闻和信息，且似乎当前的中日敌对行动在此方面起到了额外的刺激作用，这可能是因为公众普遍认为，禁止个人或任何企业在未获得相关政府颁发特别许可证的情况下设立和运作此类电台的国际规则的执行目前处于搁置状态。

虽然在冲突发生前，似乎只有某些新闻通讯社和公司运营私人无线电台以接收和/或发送其自身的电报，但根据我们收到的可靠信息，许多公司和个体已经建立或正在安排建立私人无线电设施，并与正规合法的通信渠道竞争进行运营。此外，我们最近获悉，至少有一家公司已安装了一套能够与国外（如马尼拉）的此类电台大规模交换国际电报的设施，这些国外电台有能力与之合作，以便处理往来于普通公众的电报业务，从而与合法的通信企业进行竞争。

致
上海公共租界工部局董事会主席，
上海。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
OFFICE REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 6813/141
Date 21 / 7 / 41
Shanghai, China.

TO OUR PATRONS

Dear Sirs,

We beg to inform you that we have been notified by the Ministry of Communications of Japan that, as from July 22, 1941, the following restrictions will be in force on telegrams to or from Japan written in foreign language:-

1 Telegrams are accepted only at the sender's risk.
2 Telegrams are subject to censorship and the senders are not to be notified of any delay or stoppage in case it occurs.
3 Private telegrams must be written in plain Japanese (Romanized), German, or English; but telegrams to or from Tokyo, Yokohama, Osaka, and Kobe may also be written in any of the following codes, the name of which, however, must appear in the preamble in its abbreviated form as given below in parenthesis:-

Oriental Improved Code (ORI)
Oriental Three-Letter Code (ORITH)
Schofield Three-Letter Code (SCHO)
Bentley's Second Phrase Code (BENSEC)
Bentley's Complete Phrase Code (BENCOM)
Acme Commodity and Phrase Code (ACME)

4 The signature of the sender is necessary.
5 The use of an abbreviated or code address is not allowed either in the address or in the signature.
6 Telegrams with reply prepaid are not allowed.
7 Except telegrams concerning important affairs exchanged between the captain of the vessel and the shipowner, all private messages to or from ships may be stopped at the censor's discretion.
8 Telegrams to or from foreign countries relayed at Japan are not subject to the restrictions mentioned in the preceding paragraphs.

Yours faithfully,

SHANGHAI INTERNATIONAL RADIO OFFICE

4 必须有发报人签名。
5 地址或签名中均不得使用缩写或代码地址。
6 不允许使用预付回电费电报。
7 除船长与船东之间交换的重要事务电报外，所有往来船舶的私人信息均可由审查员酌情扣留。
8 经日本转发的往来外国的电报不受前述段落所述限制的约束。

Shanghai, China

TO OUR PATRONS

Dear Sirs,

Re: Restrictions on Telegrams written in foreign language to or from Japan

Further to our previous circular concerning the same subject, we beg to inform you of the following additional restrictions to be enforced on and after July 25, 1941:-

1 The following telegrams are not accepted:—
(A) Telegrams solely expressing congratulation or condolence over any matters whatsoever.
(B) Telegrams of which the contents are considered by the telegraph office as not necessarily requiring telegraphic dispatching.

2 Press telegrams must not contain more than one hundred words in the text of each message.

3 The following special services are not allowed:-
RP Telegrams with reply paid
PC Telegraphic notification of delivery
FS Telegrams to follow
RF Telegrams redirected to any other address
TM Multiple telegrams (Telegrams to five or less than five addressees are, however, admitted)

4 Paid service advices for correction or stoppage of telegrams duly sent are not allowed.

5 The above restrictions are applicable to telegrams exchanged between Japan and Central China as well as telegrams to or from Manchoukuo.

It is understood that the above restrictions are enforced only to cope with the congested condition of the radio and telegraph communications at present in Japan, and Manchoukuo, and your kind co-operation in this connection will be greatly appreciated.

Yours faithfully,

SHANGHAI INTERNATIONAL RADIO OFFICE

继我们就同一主题发出的前一份通告之后，兹通知各位，自1941年7月25日起将执行以下附加限制：-

1 以下电报不予接受：—
(A) 仅就任何事项表达祝贺或哀悼的电报。
(B) 电报局认为内容不一定需要通过电报发送的电报。

2 新闻电报每条信息的正文不得超过一百个字。

5 上述限制适用于日本与华中之间交换的电报，以及往来满洲国的电报。

据悉，上述限制的实施仅是为了应对目前日本和满洲国无线电及电报通信的拥堵状况，对此若能获得阁下的 kindly co-operation，我们将不胜感激。

station was notified by Special Branch and Sinza Station

the certificate was made and is attached hereto with
translation.

Resort was also financially interested in the
venture, while one Zau Yao Yien (趙效賢),
formerly connected with the National Electric Co.
Broadcasting Station (closed) and the Liang Yue
Broadcasting Station, AQCT, 454 Nanking Road, was
the operator and nominal proprietor.

A visit was thereafter paid to the Station
which was found to be housed in two small rooms
recently constructed on the roof of the Resort for
the purpose. The roof of the New World is flat
and open and there are no theatres or other forms of
amusement thereon.

Hotel, 560 Avenue Edward VII, over the right to use K.C. 780.

Broadcasting Superintendence Office, this station changed

With regard to the Tien Sung (天声) Broadcasting

which was referred to in Special Branch report dated January
17, 1939, this station commenced broadcasting on January 5
or 6, 1939, without first obtaining permission from the
Municipal Police. The station is regarded as being Chinese
owned and not British owned as stated in attached letter
from Major Asano. The misapprehension concerning the
nationality of the owner is due to the fact that the Chinese
owner attempted to persuade Mr. ARNOVICK (British) to lend
his name to the venture and has attempted to spread the
impression that the Station is British owned.

Subject Tien Sung (天声) Broadcasting Station (X.H.B.C.) K.C.680
(Chinese owned) - established without permission.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Gimson

Information was recently obtained to the effect
that a new commercial broadcasting station known as the
Tien Sung (天聲 ) (XHBC) K.C.680 was established at
Lane 540, House 10, Avenue Foch and is at present broadcasting
commercial advertising matter. No application or official
information concerning this station was received by the
Police from the owners.

In order to ascertain the identity of the owners
of the Station, Special Branch detectives visited the above
address at 10 a.m. January 16, 1939 and interviewed the
manager, namely, Ma Chia Tsung (馬家珍 ) who admitted
that he is the owner of the station, but stated that the
station has been established in the name of one G. Arnovick
(British) employed by Metropolitan Motors, Ltd., 1 Avenue
du Roi Albert, who was paid over $100.00 by Ma Chia Tsung
in consideration of permitting his name to be used.

It was also learned from Ma Chia Tsung that
application was made by Mr. Arnovick to the Japanese
Broadcasting Superintendence Office for registration about
the beginning of January, 1939, and that the latter had
indicated that there was no objection to K.C.680 being
adopted by the station. In this connection it is noteworthy
that this wavelength was adopted by Mr. Bosustow (British)
for his station on November 25, 1938, though his station
has not yet begun to broadcast. Mr. Beare, H.B.M. Vice-
Consul, when interviewed on January 14, 1939, stated that
there was nothing on record concerning Station XHBC at the
British Consulate-General.

H. HARVEY dated 15-10-38.
Made by D.S. Henchman Forwarded by C. Crawford.

Mr. H. Harvey, British Eurasian, residing at 153 Route
de Soeurs, employee of Messrs. Canadian Pacific Railway Co.,
when interviewed in connection with his proposal to operate
the Hwa Ying (華英) Radio Broadcasting Station (Call
sign: XHAR, 1420 kilocycles, 282 metres), stated that it
was not his intention to take any part, active, financial
or otherwise, in the operation of the proposed station but
merely to lend his name and nationality so as to enable his
Chinese friend, Mr. Chen Yao Ting (陳耀庭), to secure
British registration for the project.

It was then pointed out to Mr. Harvey, who appears to
be very simple, that if the station was registered in his
name he would be held responsible for its operation.

Having had this fact made clear to him Mr. Harvey
intimated that he wished to take no further action in the
matter and that he was not desirous of registering the
station in his name. He said, however, that he would tell
his friend, Mr. Chen, to call at Police Headquarters with
a view to making his own arrangements.

On the morning of 24-10-38 Mr. Chen visited Police
Headquarters and explained that he was an ex-employee of
the Tuh Kee (德記) Woollen Goods Co. and an ex-member of
the Chapei Fire Brigade. He stated that he intended to
operate the station at Room 316, No.749 Bubbling Well Road
and that its purpose would be solely commercial. He requested
that permission be given him to commence operations as soon
as possible.

英籍欧亚混血人士 H. Harvey 先生，居住于姐妹路（Route de Soeurs）153号，系加拿大太平洋铁路公司职员，就其运营“华英”（Hwa Ying）广播电台（呼号：XHAR，1420千周，282米）的提议接受问询时称，他无意在该拟议电台的运营中承担任何主动、财务或其他方面的角色，而仅仅是出借其姓名和国籍身份，以便使其中国朋友陈耀庭（Chen Yao Ting）先生能为该项目取得英方注册。

Mr. Pan Ching-sung (潘金生), Manager of the Tsing
Mei Broadcasting Station, X.H.T.M., 1160 K.C., 130 Avenue
Road, called at the Special Branch at 2.30 p.m. October 6
and stated that a special programme will be broadcast between
12 noon and 12 m.n. October 7, 1938 from his station, by
comedians such as Liu Tsung-san, Tsu Ziang-fee, etc. for
the purpose of advertising for the Wu Foh Duan (五福團)
Comedians' Group, so that the public and managers of
amusement resorts may have an opportunity to hear them and
thereby be persuaded to engage them.
He submitted a letter containing the names of the
comedians, numbering 17, who will participate in the
broadcast. He stated that humourous songs and dialogue,
which have no written script and which have been staged or
broadcasted before, will be included and emphasized that
nothing of a political nature will be introduced.
Mr. Pan Ching Sung was informed that a reply would
be sent to him before 12 noon, October 7, 1938.
As the manager of the Tsing Mei station is aware
that he will be held responsible for any infringement of
the guarantee given to the Police by the Station there does
not appear to be any objection to the proposed special
programme.

由副督察长洛根呈报，经 C. Gastao J.J. 转递。

精美广播电台（呼号 X.H.T.M.，频率 1160 千周，地址爱文义路130号）经理潘金生（Pan Ching-sung）先生于10月6日下午2时30分造访特别调查科，并称该台将于1938年10月7日中午12时至午夜12时之间播出特别节目，由刘宗三（Liu Tsung-san）、朱祥飞（Tsu Ziang-fee）等滑稽演员表演，旨在为五福团（Wu Foh Duan）滑稽剧团做广告，以便公众及娱乐场所经理有机会聆听他们的表演，从而被说服聘用他们。
他提交了一封信，其中列出了将参与广播的17名滑稽演员的姓名。他表示，节目中将包含以前曾上演或广播过的、无书面剧本的幽默歌曲和对白，并强调不会引入任何政治性质的内容。
已告知潘金生先生，将在1938年10月7日中午12点前给予答复。
鉴于精美电台经理知晓他将对电台违反向警方作出的任何保证的行为承担责任，目前看来对该拟议的特别节目并无异议。

With reference to the attached letter from the
Tsing Mei Broadcasting Station, XHTM, K.C. 1160, 130A
Avenue Road, Mr. Pan Ching-sung (潘淦生), responsible
representative of the Station was interviewed at Special
Branch, Headquarters, on the afternoon of September 20,
when he was given two blank copies of the usual pledge
form, with the request that he should complete one and
return it to the Police, while retaining the other for
reference. At the same time, he was warned to observe
the conditions set forth in the pledge form, it being
emphasized that any breach of the conditions might entail
the closure of his station. Mr. Pan replied that he
would abide strictly by the conditions laid down by the
S.M.C.

A copy of the pledge form, duly signed and chopped,
was returned to Special Branch the same afternoon and is
forwarded herewith.

The original permit issued by the Japanese
Broadcasting Superintendence Office, which was attached
to the letter received by the Municipal Police from this
station, was returned to Mr. Pan during the interview.
A copy of the permit was made and is attached hereto
together with translation.

1939年1月25日上午10时，日本分区副督察 (D.C.) 通过“A”分区巡官 (D.O.) 向本站发送了两封恐吓信，这些信件是由位于南京路哈同大楼316室的日本广播管制办公室寄给他的，信中包含对投诉人的威胁。

经黑 (Black)、小林 (Kobayashi) 两位侦探长 (D.S.I.) 及刑事侦缉股316室 (C.D.S. 316) 查询显示，投诉人是广东路93号 X.H.H.Z. 电台的经理（他声称该电台由于亚清 (Yu Ya Ching) 先生赞助），同时也是南京路370号426室 X.H.H.A. 电台的所有者，以及《上海无线电刊》(Shanghai Radio Review) 的发行人，这是一份专门报道无线电新闻的刊物。

《上海无线电刊》于1938年4月开始出版，名义价格为2分，刊登无线电爱好者感兴趣的内容，并列出在上海注册的电台及其节目单，该列表也包括 X.O.J.B. 电台的节目，该电台由大上海广播电台 (Greater Shanghai Broadcasting Company) 指导，该电台受日军控制，位于南京路哈同大楼316室。

1939年1月12日，投诉人通过邮政收到一封信，内容如下：

According to information received from the investigating section (Nanking Road Branch) of this body, we have learnt that you are a traitor, and we are pointing out your guilt as follows:-

(2) Touting for Programmes in favour of the Japanese Broadcasting Station, the "Greater Shanghai", for the purpose of defrauding the public.
(3) Publishing the "Shanghai Radio Weekly" as wide propaganda in Shanghai.
The above three items have been definitely corroborated through investigations.
Therefore this letter of warning is written you, in the hope that you will earnestly change your present attitude within one week upon the receipt of this letter. Also you are requested to contribute a sum of $50.00 for the refugees, failing which "printed matters" showing the above three items will be distributed to the public and certain "free action" followed against you.
Please note that your movements have been kept under observation by the members of this body (Nanking Road Branch).
When you have contributed the above sum of money to refugees, please have the receipt for same printed in the press.

The Blood Body for the riddance of Traitors.

Complainant ignored these letters but on
the 19-1-39 received another letter through the
post which reads:-

To the Editor Yang,
Suspecting that you haven't received my pre-
vious letter addressed to you at the "Shanghai
Radio Weekly", I having obtained your address from
the Investigating Section of this Body, am again
sending you this letter of warning.
The editing of the "Shanghai Radio Weekly" is
a traitorous act. Upon receipt of this letter, I
hope that you cease publishing this paper immediately
or change your attitude in compiling it.
Also you are requested to tell Mr. Lung that this
Body is preparing to proclaim his guilt by distributing
Printed matters, should he continue what he is doing
now.

Copied: The Blood Body for the
Riddance of Traitors.

The receipt of this third letter alarmed complain-
ant and he therefore took all three to a Japanese off-
icial of the Japanese Broadcasting Control Office, one
Yoshio Ban, who is the "chief official of the Broad-
casting Superintendence office", room 316, Hardoon
Building, Nanking Road, and the latter in turn handed
them over to D.C. (J.).

The complainant was called to the station and
interrogated as to any information he could give
detectives as to the possible writer of these letters
but was unable to do so, stating he had never pre-
viously been threatened and that his associations
with fellow business men had always been cordial.

收到这第三封信使投诉人感到惊慌，因此他将这三封信全部交给日本广播管制办公室的一名日本官员坂芳雄 (Yoshio Ban)，他是“广播监理所首席官员”，办公地点在南京路哈同大楼316室，后者随即将信件转交给日本分区副督察 (D.C. (J.))。

投诉人被召至警局，并就其能否向侦探提供关于这些信件可能作者的信息接受讯问，但他未能提供，称他以前从未受到过威胁，且与商界同行的关系一直融洽。

Subject Li Shu Teh Tang Broadcasting Station - change of name and wavelength.

Made by D. S. I. Logan Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

The Li Shu Teh Tang (李樹德堂) Broadcasting Station, Room 316, Shanghai New Hotel, 579 Kiukiang Road, K.C. 940, call sign XHHE, has recently changed its name to Dah Hwa (大華) Broadcasting Station, K.C. 980, call sign XHHE. The change was made with permission from the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendent's Office but no report was made to the Shanghai Municipal Police.

It has been confidentially learned that K.C. 940, vacated by the Li Shu Teh Tang Station, will be taken up by a new Japanese sponsored broadcasting station, AKLE, but full particulars are not available at present.

With reference to the attached application
from Lord Robertson Lee of X.H.H.E. Broadcasting
Association, Sun Hotel, Chekiang Road, residing
at 150 Edinburgh Road, for a special curfew pass,
enquiries have been made in the Western District
with little success.

Eventually, enquiries made at the X.H.H.E.
Broadcasting Association, which is known as the
Lee Shu Teh Tang Broadcasting Station, Room 316, 579
Kiukiang Road, met with a refusal by the employees
to disclose anything appertaining to Lee, neither
would they divulge his Chinese name nor his actual
residence, the only information obtainable being
that he was connected with the station. House 150
Edinburgh Road, according to Tsu Foh Chun (朱福鈞),
Manager of the Radio Station, is his residence, but
he very seldom lives there, and it is impossible
to gain an interview. All his affairs are dealt
with by Tsu of the radio station.

Discreet enquiries have also been made at
House 150 Edinburgh Road, and according to the
inmates there, the resident is named Lee Zeu Kiu
(李瑾九) who owns the Lee Shu Teh Tang Broadcasting
Station. It is however not known whether Lee Zeu
Kiu and Robertson Lee are one and the same person.

With reference to the attached letter from Young's
Broadcasting Station (楊氏廣播電台), House 23, Lane 145
Kuling Road, Mr. Y.C. Young (楊貽慶), manager and owner

been taken up by the Dah Loh Broadcasting Station (XHHK)

Subject Chen Tseng Tsang (陳正章), manager of Hong Nyih (航業)
Broadcasting Station, stated to be agent of Broadcasting
Superintendence Office.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.S.

Information has been received to the effect that Chen
Tseng Tsang, manager of the Hong Nyih Broadcasting Station,
93 Canton Road, call sign XHH2, frequency K.C. 1180, is in
secret collusion with the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence
Office. It is stated that he is a member of the committee
of that organ and is in receipt of a monthly salary of $300.
He is held responsible for the watching of the activities
of the Shanghai Municipal Council in their handling of the
control of broadcasting problem.

It will be recalled that the Hong Nyih Broadcasting
Station was among the five stations marked with red circles
mentioned on the list of broadcasting stations supplied to
the Shanghai Municipal Police by the Broadcasting Superinten-
dence office as having effected registration with the Japanese
controlled organ. Information has been received that a
few days before the list mentioned was handed to the Shanghai
Municipal Police, three of the five stations referred to,
were approached by Chen Tseng Tsang and advised to register
with the Japanese without further delay in order to avoid
trouble, Chen at the same time intimating that he could arrange
negotiations for them. The remaining station, the Li Shu
Tun Tang (李樹德堂 ) station being located O.C.L. (Western
District) was not approached.

In support of the foregoing it will be noted that Chen
Tseng Tsang was instrumental in securing for Liu Tseng San
(刘春山), a comedian notoriously active in national
salvation propaganda prior to the withdrawal of the Chinese

制作人：副督察长洛根 转呈人：C. Crawford. D.S.

收到情报称，航业广播电台经理陈正章，位于广东路93号，呼号XHH2，频率千周1180，与日本广播监理所秘密勾结。据说他是该机构委员会成员，每月领取薪金300元。他负责监视上海公共租界工部局在处理广播管制问题上的活动。

回想起来，航业广播电台是广播监理所向上海公共租界工部局警务处提供的已向日方控制机构注册的广播电台名单中，用红圈标记的五家电台之一。收到情报称，在上述名单交给上海公共租界工部局警务处前几天，陈正章接触了所述五家电台中的三家，劝告它们立即向日方注册以避免麻烦，陈同时暗示他可以为他们安排谈判。剩下的一家电台，李树德堂（Li Shu Tun Tang，李樹德堂）电台，位于西区（O.C.L.），未受接触。

为支持上述情况，值得注意的是，陈正章曾协助刘春山（Liu Tseng San，刘春山）获得免受日本特务机关骚扰的豁免权，刘是一名喜剧演员，在中国军队撤离上海地区之前，以积极参与救国宣传而闻名，参见1938年5月13日的特务科报告。

Section I, Special Branch.
December 6, 1939.

Great China Broadcasting Station -
ordered to suspend functioning by Japanese.
------------------------------------------

The Great China Broadcasting Station, XHHH,
K.C.1040, 313 Foochow Road, has been ordered by the
Japanese Radio Broadcasting Superintendent's Office,
Hardoon Building, to suspend operations for co-operating
with non-registered radio stations by giving publicity
to the Moral Rearmament Movement.

The Moral Rearmament Movement was sponsored by
persons of Christian faith abroad, calling upon every
individual of the world, irrespective of nationality,
to embark upon a new life, a life ruled by God and
guided by the four principles of the movement, namely,
Absolute Honesty, Absolute Purity, Unselfishness and
Fraternity. Local Christian circles, both foreign and
Chinese, have responded to the movement and broadcast
programmes from the Tung Fang (東方) a British owned
station located at 120 Yu Ya Ching Road and the Poh
Ying (柏音) Broadcasting Station operated by the
Shanghai Christian Broadcasting Association, 128 Museum
Road, between December 1 and 3. As the Tung Fang and
Poh Ying stations are not registered with the Japanese
Radio Broadcasting Superintendent's Office, and the
Great China Dispensary, the owner of the Great China
Radio Station, has contributed space in the Chinese
Press to give publicity to the broadcasts connected with
the Moral Rearmament Movement, the Great China Station

大中华广播电台，呼号XHHH，
频率1040千周，福州路313号，已被日本广播监理处（设于哈同大楼）下令暂停运作，原因是通过与非注册广播电台合作，为“道德重整运动”进行宣传。

“道德重整运动”由海外基督教人士发起，呼吁世界上每个人，不分国籍，开始新生活，一种由上帝统治并受该运动四项原则指导的生活，即绝对诚实、绝对纯洁、无私和博爱。本地中外基督教界响应了这一运动，并于12月1日至3日期间，通过位于亚尔培路120号的英资东方（Tung Fang）广播电台，以及由上海基督教广播协会运营、位于博物馆路128号的柏音（Poh Ying）广播电台，播出了相关节目。由于东方电台和柏音电台未在日本广播监理处注册，且大中华广播电台的所有者大中华药房在中文报刊上提供版面，宣传与“道德重整运动”相关的广播，因此大中华电台

December 5, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

National Herald :-

LOCAL BROADCASTING STATION ORDERED TO SUSPEND

The Great China Radio Broadcasting Station
which is operated by the Great China Dispensary on Foochow
Road was ordered by the Shanghai Radio Broadcasting
Stations Control Office on December 2 to suspend operations.
As the station was registered with the Control Office, it
had to comply with the order for the suspension. Nothing,
however, is known as to the cause of this forced suspension.

（批：C.T. 12/5）

1939年12月5日。下午译文。

《国民新闻报》：

本地广播电台被令停播

由大中华药房在福州路运营的大中华广播电台于12月2日被上海广播电台管理处下令停止运作。由于该电台已在管理处注册，故必须遵守停播命令。然而，对于此次强制停播的原因，目前尚不知情。

（批注：C.T. 12/5）

page_data.en:
Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Ta Mei Pao, Chinese-American Daily
News, National Herald and Hwa Pao :- 2.12.29 (H/Y)

SPECIAL BROADCAST PROGRAMME MARKS PROGRESS OF UNIVERSAL
MORAL REARMAMENT MOVEMENT

Commencing from yesterday, the local
supporters of the Universal Moral Rearmament Movement
started to propagate the movement from local broadcasting
stations. Broadcasting programmes have been fixed and
will be carried out between 12.30 p.m. and 1.50 p.m. at
the Eastern Broadcasting Station and between 7 p.m. and
8 p.m. at the Fuh Ying Broadcasting Station every day.
Wang Yuan-pai (王元白), a doctor by profession,
broadcasted his experience in pushing the movement from
the Eastern Broadcasting Station yesterday. At night
Dr. Chin Wu-chow (金武周), professor of the University
of Shanghai, delivered a lecture giving important points
of the movement at Fuh Ying Station and the local student
representatives also made speeches in support of the
movement.

C. Tsoong

特别广播节目标志普世道德重整运动的进展

从昨天起，本地普世道德重整运动的支持者开始通过本地广播电台宣传该运动。广播节目已安排妥当，每天中午12:30至下午1:50在东方广播电台播出，晚上7点至8点在福音广播电台播出。王元白医生昨日在东方广播电台广播了他推动该运动的经验。晚间，沪江大学教授金武周博士在福音电台发表演讲，阐述该运动的要点，本地学生代表也发表演讲支持该运动。

C. Tsoong

Subject Broadcasting Superintendence Office: alleged to have attempted

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford. S.I.

Mr. Li Sih-tang (李錫棠), manager of the Fuh Ying
Broadcasting Station, 418 Hart Road, XHEB, called at the Police
Headquarters at 2.30 p.m. May 25, and made a report to the
following effect :-

He was told by one named Chen, an engineer of the Hwa
Tung Broadcasting Station, when the latter was making repairs
at the Fuh Ying Broadcasting Station, this morning, May 25,
that the Dah Kwong Ming Broadcasting Station, Burkill Road,
has registered with the Broadcasting Superintendence Office.
According to Mr. Chen, the management of the Dah Kwong Ming S......
had been told by the S.M.C. authorities to approach and
register with the Broadcasting Superintendence Office, if it
wished to reopen the station.

At 10.30 a.m. May 25, he received a telephone message
from one Chow Kan-foo (周幹甫), son-in-law of Mrs. Hardoon
and accountant of Hardoon & Company, advising him to register
his station with the Broadcasting Superintendence Office, and
urging him to be present at his office in the Hardoon Building,
Nanking Road, to discuss the matter. Li Sih-tang proceeded to
the Hardoon & Company Building at about noon, 25-5-38, and
interviewed Mr. Chow Kan-foo who accompanied him to an adjoin-
ing room to interview one named Chang, believed to be a
Japanese. Chang stated that the Broadcasting Superintendence
Office was under the direct control of the Japanese Military
authorities, and that he should register his station with the
Office, otherwise his station would be closed. Mr. Li Sih-tang
replied that he had already submitted a guarantee to the
Shanghai Municipal Police Headquarters that nothing of a

political nature would be broadcast from his station, and that
his station had resumed operations, following mediation by the
S.M.C. authorities in the dispute over the question of registra-
tion. Mr. Chang insisted that he must register with Broadcasting
Superintendence Office, and doubted whether the Municipal Police
could afford him the necessary protection.

After the interview, Mr. Chow Kan-foo, in an effort to
induce Mr. Li to register, told him that the Broadcasting
Superintendence Office has decided to close down six stations,
namely the Dah Loh, Great China, Foh Ying, Tung Loh, Tung Fang
and his own station, because of their failure to register, and
that as Mrs. Hardoon was very much in favour of the Buddhist
programmes broadcast over his station, he had asked him to
register accordingly. Mr. Chow also told him that the Dah
Kwong Ming Broadcasting Station has now completed its
registration with the office.

Note Reference Sinza Misc. file No. 201/38, dated 21-5-38,
and letter dated 23-5-38, addressed by the Dah Kwong Ming
Broadcasting Station to the Commissioner Of Police, the Dah
Kwong Ming Station equipment has been dismantled and removed
from 548 Burkill Road.

It is possible that, if the foregoing report is true,
the Dah Kwong Ming Station may endeavour to establish a secret
station in defiance of the S.M.P. ban and resume broadcasting.
With this possibility in mind, enquiries are being continued
in order to ascertain whether this station has resumed
broadcasting.

SUBJECT: Sun Sun Broadcasting Station - change of

On March 26, 1941, a letter was received
from the Sun Sun Company reporting that Mr. Chen
Chia Chu (鄭家駒) has been appointed the
responsible representative of the Sun Sun Broad-
casting Station, call sign X.L.H.A., K.C.800, in

Huang Zui Doo (黃燧圖). This station is
owned by the Sun Sun Company and situated on the
5th floor of the Company's Building on Nanking
Road. The letter is attached hereto together
with translation.

on the afternoon of March 27 when he was informed
that nothing of a political or objectionable
nature could be broadcasted from his station.

would be complied with, and at the same time he
endorsed the pledge form which was signed by his
predecessor, Mr. Huang Ying Chu to the same effect.

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C Crawford i/c S

Enquiries show that the Chinese radio broadcasting
stations in the International Settlement have not been
interfered with by the Japanese authorities, except that
at about 6 p.m. on February 21 or 22, a Japanese subject
approached the Sun Sun Radio Station (XHA), Sun Sun
Company Building, Nanking Road, and requested them to
accept a programme for broadcasting. On being informed
that his request could not be acceded to because their
broadcasting programme was fully taken up, the visitor
withdrew.

There are altogether 19 Chinese radio broadcasting
stations in the Settlement, but only 17 are at present
in operation. The remaining two suspended operations
because of the lack of business (Vide Special Branch
reports dated December 1 and 2, 1937.)

Subject (in full) Kien Hwa Broadcasting Station, XHHB, K.C. 720, frequency
wavelength changed to K.C. 740.

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C Gowen

On 26.11.38, it was learned that the Kien Hwa Broad-
casting Station, XHHB, K.C. 720, which is registered with
the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office, recently
changed its frequency wavelength to K.C. 740. No report
concerning the change was made to the Shanghai Municipal
Police by the owners of the Station.

An official of the Station, when questioned, denied
that the change was effected at the request of the Japanese
Broadcasting Superintendence Office and stated that the
change was carried out in order to make the frequency wave-
length conform to that stated in the original permit issued
by the National Government of China.

In view of the fact that this Station is registered
with the Japanese, it appears hardly probable that the change
would be made without the permission of the latter authority.

D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)
(Sp. Br.)

（印：POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 8 JUNE）

Further to Special Branch report dated May 28,
1938 entitled "Letter from Messrs. Allman, Davis & Kops
- Complaint of MacKay Radio Circuit" Mr. Ford, Acting
Consul in charge of Chinese Affairs, British Consulate-
General, requested D.S.I. Logan to call at his office
in connection with the Dollar Radio Station, 156 Peking
Road (Room 201). When interviewed at 10 a.m., June 2,
1938, Mr. Ford stated that as a result of enquiries having
been made by the Special Branch at the British Consulate-
General regarding the Dollar Radio Station which is owned
by Mr. Lee Berk Chun who is in possession of a Canadian
Passport, the matter of this Station was reviewed by
Mr. Ogden. Mr. Ogden instructed Mr. Ford to inform the
Special Branch that technically Mr. Lee Berk Chun enjoys
dual nationality, i.e. while in Canada he is recognized
as a British subject but while in China, he is not
recognized as British on account of the fact that he is
a member of the Chinese race and is domiciled in China.
Therefore he is not entitled to the privileges enjoyed
by a British subject. Mr. Ford stated that a letter
confirming the above is being prepared and will be
forwarded to the Commissioner of Police in due course.

In view of the foregoing the letter, dated May 28,
1938, sent to Messrs. Allman, Davies & Kops is somewhat
misleading.

Reference the instructions of D.C. (Special
Branch) on the attached letter dated May 25, 1938, from
Messrs. Allman, Davies & Kops, Attorneys at Law, Room 208,
Hamilton House, to D.C. (Special Branch) asking to be
informed as to whether the Dollar Radio Station (British),
Room 201, 156 Peking Road, has applied for or has been
granted a permit by the Shanghai Municipal Council to
operate a circuit from Shanghai and, if so, to what point
or points, also, the name and nationality of the person
or firm operating this station, the station in question is
owned by a Canadian born Chinese (British registered
subject) named Lee Berk Chun (李北钦) who is also owner
of Canada Greenhouse, Lane 189, House 42, Kinneer Road.
This person addressed a letter dated May 12, 1938, to the
Shanghai Municipal Police enquiring about the formalities
to be complied with in effecting registration of his
station with the Shanghai Municipal Police and was
informed by a member of the Special Branch that while
the Shanghai Municipal Police would not issue permission
to him to operate, his operation of the station would not
be prevented by the Shanghai Municipal Police provided
he registered with and obtained permission from the
British Consulate-General.

Mr. S.G. Beare, Consul and Deputy Registrar
of Companies, Land Office, British Consulate-General,
when interviewed on May 27, 1938, stated that as the
Dollar Radio Station is a private concern it is not
necessary to register it under the Companies Ordinances.

参照副警司（特务科）对随附的1938年5月25日来自奥尔曼、戴维斯和科普斯律师事务所（地址：汉密尔顿大厦208室）致副警司（特务科）信函的指示，该律所询问是否已申请或已获上海公共租界工部局颁发许可，允许美元广播电台（英资），位于北京路156号201室，运营从上海出发的无线电电路，如有，终点为何处；此外，还询问运营该电台的个人或商号的名称及国籍。经查，该电台由一名加拿大出生的华人（英国注册臣民）李北钦（Lee Berk Chun）所有，他也是奇尼尔路（Kinneer Road）189弄42号加拿大温室（Canada Greenhouse）的所有者。此人曾于1938年5月12日致函上海公共租界工部局警务处，咨询在其电台向上海公共租界工部局警务处办理登记手续时需履行的手续，特务科成员告知他，虽然上海公共租界工部局警务处不会向他颁发运营许可，但只要他在英国总领事馆登记并获得许可，上海公共租界工部局警务处将不阻止其运营该电台。

英国驻上海总领事馆领事兼土地局公司注册处副处长 S.G. Beare 先生在1938年5月27日接受问询时表示，由于美元广播电台属于私人机构，无需根据《公司条例》进行注册。

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford

Reference the attached letter, dated 12/5/38, addressed
by the Dollar Radio Station (British), 156 Peking Road,
to the S.M.C. requesting permission to operate in the Settle-
ment, and with reference to the instructions of D.C. (Special
Branch) on memo dated 14/5/38, Mr. Lee Berk Chun (李北銓),
the writer of aforesaid letter, was interviewed at Special
Branch, Headquarters, on 14/5/38, when he was informed that
permission to operate any new stations in the Settlement
would not be granted for the time being. Mr. Lee then
produced Canadian Passport No.58629, issued on 16/6/33 in
his favour (registered at the local British Consulate-
General) and claimed that his proposed station was entitled
to the same treatment as other foreign owned stations now
operating, whereupon, in accordance with the verbal
instructions of D.C. (Special Branch), he was informed that
while the S.M.P. did not in any way issue permission to him
to operate, provided he registered with, and obtained per-
mission from the British Consulate-General, the S.M.C. would
not prevent his operating.

and not by the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office,

参阅所附日期为1938年6月16日、由住在天津路293号凯泰饭店三楼的白维良 (Bah Chee Liang) 致特务科的信件，申请获准在上述地址建立一家广播电台，命名为三阳广播无线电台，呼号 XnLC，频率 1060千周 (K.C.)，用于商业广告目的。白维良先生于1938年6月16日在特务科总部接受问询，当时他出示了一份文件（附于此及译文），他称这是日本当局为其拟设电台签发的许可证。据白维良先生称，上述许可证是通过一位名叫武宣停 (Wu I-ting) 的朋友从日本当局获得的，此人与日本人有某种联系。注：武宣停在1938年6月15日的特务科报告中被提及为“世界和平运动”的主要发起人，而申请人白维良的父亲白玉山 (Bah Ngoh San)，又名白云山 (Bah Luin San)，被提及积极协助武宣停。

值得注意的是，该日本许可证是由上海特务机关总务部签发的，而不是由位于南京路哈同大楼、受浅野少佐 (Major Asano) 控制的日本广播监理所签发的。

Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office is well
aware that the Tung Fang Station has been using frequency

Subject Yung Sung Broadcasting Station - application for registration.
Proposed adoption of same frequency as Tung Fang Station.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford

Reference D.C. (Special Branch's) instructions on
margin of Special Branch report dated 21.6.38 on above
subject, Mr. Ho Kia Tsing(何家駿), Manager of the Yung
Sung (永生) Radio Station, was interviewed at Police
Headquarters on June 23, when he was informed that in the
case of a new station, besides the permit from the Japanese
Broadcasting Superintendence Office, a written guarantee
is required by the Police before it be permitted to operate.
Two blank guarantee bonds were given to him with the request
that he should complete one and return it to the Police
while retaining the other for reference. At the same
time his attention was drawn to the first condition of the
guarantee form which reads:- "Not to obtrude on other
established wave lengths.", and the fact that wave length
K.C. 1080 has been used by the Tung Fang Radio Station
(call sign XHHG, 120 Yu Ya Ching Road) for a long time.
In reply Mr. Ho stated that he would refer the matter to the
owner of the station, named, Chung Wei Ling (宗惠麟) and
intimated that he would suggest to Mr. Chung Wei Ling that
the wave length should be changed as the adoption of the
same frequency by two stations would only result in con-
fusion and be detrimental to the business of both parties.
Mr. Ho stated that he would communicate further
on the matter to the Special Branch at an early date.

Logan
D.S.I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

Subject... Tong Loh Broadcasting Station (XLHG) K.C. 860 - broadcasted a national salvation song entitled "Song of Peace".
Made by D.C.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Campbell

At 9.45 a.m. November 8, Mr. Chang Ching-pah (張錦伯), staff member of the Tung Loh Broadcasting Station, Tung Fang Hotel, corner of Hankow and Chekiang Roads, representing Mr. Loh Sang-ngo (陸省吾), the manager, who is stated to be sick at present, called at Special Branch, and was questioned regarding the broadcast of a song entitled "Song of Peace". He admitted that this song had been broadcast over his station from a gramophone record at 1.40 p.m. November 5 through the carelessness of the announcer. He was unable to produce a copy of the words of the song but upon a copy of the song which was on file in this office being shown to him he identified it as being the same as that broadcasted. He stated that the record in question had been taken away by a coolie from the Broadcasting Superintendence Office, who called at the broadcasting station at 4 p.m. November 7, and demanded it in the name of his Japanese superiors.

A statement made by Mr. Chang Ching-pah regarding the incident is attached hereto, together with a copy of the song in question.

D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

at S.I., S.P. on the 8/11/38 and interpreted by Clerk Wong Chia-tsing

My name is Chang Ching-pah (張錦伯). I am a
staff member of the Tung Loh Broadcasting Station, Tung
Fang Hotel, Hankow Road.

At 1.40 p.m. November 5, 1938, the song entitled
"Peace" was broadcasted over the Tung Loh Station from a
gramophone record. This record was put on to the air in-
advertently by Ho Feng-nyi (何鳳儀), sister of the female
announcer of the station Ho Feng-tsien (何鳳倩), while the
latter went to the lavatory, she having failed to note the
contents of the record.

At about three o'clock on the afternoon of November
7, a telephone message was received from the Broadcasting
Superintendence Office, instructing that the record containing
the "Song of Peace" should be sent to the superintendence
Office. This message was received by the female announcer;
who being afraid to disclose the matter, did not inform me
till the matter was brought to my notice by the S.M.P.

About an hour later, a Chinese of the coolie type,
claiming to have been detailed by the Broadcasting
Superintendence Office, called at the Tung Loh Station and
demanded the record in question. This was given to him
by the announcer without my knowledge, and no report was
made to the Police regarding the incident.

I had no knowledge of the above matter until 6 p.m.
when informed by a member of the S.M.P. Special Branch.

At 9 a.m. this morning, November 8, I called at the
Broadcasting Superintendence Office in the Hardoon Building,

我叫张锦伯（張錦伯）。我是汉口路东方饭店同乐广播电台的职员。

1938年11月5日下午1时40分，一首名为《和平》的歌曲通过留声机唱片在同乐电台播出。这张唱片是由该台女播音员何凤倩（Ho Feng-tsien）的妹妹何凤仪（Ho Feng-nyi）无意中放上广播的，当时后者去洗手间，她未能注意到唱片的内容。

11月7日下午三点左右，接到广播监理局的电话通知，指示将包含《和平歌》的唱片送往监理局。该消息由女播音员接收；因害怕披露此事，直到上海公共租界工部局警务处引起我注意之前，她并未告知我。

大约一小时后，一名苦力模样的中国人声称受广播监理局派遣，来到同乐电台，索要相关唱片。播音员在我不知情的情况下将其交出，且未就此事件向警方报告。

直到下午6点，经上海公共租界工部局警务处特务科成员告知，我才知晓上述事宜。

今天上午，即11月8日上午9时，我前往哈同大楼的广播监理局，

Let us rise.

We young men must sing songs against war.

The imperialists will struggle among themselves

Our semi-colony will become their battle field.

Translation of a despatch from Da Lai Broadcasting Station.

Owing to the fact that the present location
of our station and its surrounding areas are unsuitable
for a broadcasting station, and that the power of our
transmitter is smaller than other stations in Shanghai,
our broadcasts cannot be received by the public in all
circumstances, with the result that our business has been
poor and a big loss has been sustained. In the hope
of improving our business, we have secured a place on the
7th floor of the Yangtse Hotel, 287 Yunnan Road, for our
station. At the same time, we will increase the power
of our transmitter to 100 watts. Apart from applying
for permission from the Broadcasting Superintendence
Office, we forward you this letter for your approval.

Ma Siang Ching (馬襄卿),
Manager of Da Lai Broadcasting
Station. September, 1938.

To Special Branch,
S. M. P.

Mr. Ma Siang-ching (馬襄卿 ), Manager of the Da Lai
Broadcasting Station, call sign XMHJ, 7 Ning Chung Fong, Hupeh
Road, called at Police Headquarters on the morning of June 27
and explained that in consequence of his repeated requests,
the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office had agreed
to assign K.C. 1120 instead of 1080 to his station. In proof
of this new arrangement, Mr. Ma produced a new type-written
certificate issued by the Superintendence Office. A written
copy of the certificate together with translation is attached
to this report.

The K.C. 1120 was formerly adopted by the Yuen Chong
Radio Station, located on Rue du Marche in the French
Concession, which was closed down indefinitely about 2 months
ago by the French Authorities for having broadcasted certain
songs of a political nature.

Blank registration forms (in duplicate) were then given
to Mr. Ma to be filled in. The original duly signed by Mr. Ma,
is attached to this report.

Broadcasting Station, call sign KMHJ, 7 Ning Chung Fong,

Broadcasting Station located at Room 633, Wu Kung Lodging House,

despite the fact that this frequency has been used by the Tung
Fang Broadcasting Station, call sign XHHG, 120 Yu Ya Ching

Ma that, not taking into consideration the Tung Fang Radio
Station, it was impossible for both the new stations - the
Da Lai Station and Yung Sung Station - to operate on the same
frequency without confusion.
In reply Mr. Ma stated that he realized this fact and
had brought this state of affairs to the notice of the
Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office, but in reply
had been told to use this frequency, as the Yung Sung
Station would be told to change their kilocycles, while

大来广播电台经理马襄卿先生（呼号 KMHJ，湖北路宁忠坊7号）曾于1938年5月18日向警察总局特务科申请运营该台（见1938年5月18日特务科报告），他于1938年6月24日下午来到警察总局。他带来了一份由日本广播监理所签发、浅野先生签署的打字证书。该证书的抄本及译文附于本报告后。
根据该证书，监理所也分配给这家新电台 K.C.1080 的频率。值得注意的是，尽管福建路152号武功旅社633室的永声广播电台（见1938年6月24日特务科报告）也被同一机构分配了该频率，但该频率长期以来一直由呼号为 XHHG、位于虞洽卿路120号的东方广播电台使用。因此，已向马先生指出，若不考虑东方广播电台，大来电台和永声电台这两家新电台不可能在同一频率上运行而不造成混乱。
马先生回答说，他意识到这一事实，并已将此情况通知日本广播监理所，但得到的答复是使用该频率，因为永声

Consequently, Mr. Ma added, he has no alternative but
to proceed with the original arrangement.
He desires to furnish the requisite guarantee to the
S.M.P. but in the light of the attitude of the Broadcasting
Superintendence Office in insisting that he broadcast over
a frequency of K.C.1080, is in a quandary where the matter
of complying with the condition of the Police guarantee
is concerned, i.e. "Not to obtrude on any established wave-
lengths."
The action of the Japanese is apparently designed to bring
pressure to bear on those old established stations which have
so far refused to register with the Broadcasting Superintendence
Office (See D.C.(Japanese)* memo to Commissioner of Police
dated June 16, 1938 attached) by bringing about confusion of
wavelengths and, if persisted in, will lead to chaotic condition
as far as the Chinese stations affected are concerned.
Instructions are therefore solicited as to what action
should be taken in the matter.

东方电台（Tung Fang Station）因未向广播监理处登记，将不被允许继续使用 K.C.1080 这一频率。
因此，马先生补充说，他别无选择，只能按原计划行事。
他希望向上海公共租界工部局警务处提供所需的担保，但鉴于广播监理处坚持要求他在 K.C.1080 频率上广播的态度，他在遵守警方担保条件即“不干扰任何既定波长”一事上陷入了困境。
日本人的行动显然是旨在通过造成波长混乱，向那些迄今拒绝向广播监理处登记的老旧既定电台施加压力（参见附后的 1938 年 6 月 16 日日本副警务总监致警务总监的备忘录），如果 persisted in（持续下去），将导致受影响的中国电台陷入混乱局面。
因此，请示在此事上应采取何种行动。

Headquarters, on June 16, 1938, when he was informed that

to operate in the Settlement and that for that reason his
application could not be entertained in the meantime.
He was, however, informed unofficially that should his
client of his own accord succeed in registering his station
with the local Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office
and thereafter commence operating, the S.M.P. would not
prevent his doing so provided the usual guarantee form
required from all Chinese broadcasting stations is completed
and supplied to the Special Branch.

In reply, Mr. Chien Chen stated that he would
inform his client in terms of above and mentioned that
rather than approach the Japanese Authorities his client
would prefer to endeavour to find a foreigner in possession
of Extraterritoriality rights and establish the station under
his protection.

tisement, and no politics, nor news of a
military nature, will be broadcasted.
In view of the fact that the station was
authorised by the Government, I trust
permission for broadcasting will also
be given by the Settlement Authorities.
As the station is now under the juris-
diction of a police station in the Settle-
ment, I hereby authorise you to report
the matter to the authorities concerned
on my behalf."

Date Dec. 8. 19 38.

Subject Application by Yeu Lien (Union) Broadcasting Station
(XHHV) for permission to re-commence broadcasting.

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford

The attached application by the Yeu Lien (Union)
Broadcasting Station, dated 8.12.38, was delivered to the
Special Branch at 9.30 a.m. December 8, 1938, by Mr. Chen
Yeu Foo (陳懋甫) representing the said station, together
with a permit issued by the Japanese Broadcasting
Superintendence Office, authorising the Yeu Lien Station,
call sign XHHV, which was formerly located at Lane 930,
House 5, Avenue Foch, but closed down on April 27, 1938,
to recommence broadcasting at new premises located on the
4th floor of the Chung Nan Hotel, 560 Avenue Edward VII.

Prior to April 27, 1938, when the station closed
down, it broadcasted over a frequency wavelength of K.C. 880
on permit No.23 issued by Mr. Wen Yueh-ching (温毓慶),
Chief of the Bureau of International Telegraphs of the
National Government, dated 18.7.33. On October 3, 1938,
an application was received from this station requesting
permission to re-open the station but owing to the fact
that the applicant had not received the sanction of the
Broadcasting Superintendence Office and, in fact, refused
to recognize that organ, permission was refused. It
would appear, however, that in the meantime the Yeu Lien
Station approached the Japanese and arrived at an arrangement
whereby it has now obtained the requisite permission (vide
copy of permit hereto attached).

The Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office,
however, allocated to the Yeu Lien Station a frequency
wavelength of K.C.780, which wavelength has been reserved
by the American Commercial Broadcasting Station (XMHE),
an American owned station belonging to Mr. P.H. Vanmeter

主题 友联广播电台（XHHV）申请重新开播。

由副督察长洛根呈报 转呈 C. Crawford

友联广播电台于1938年12月8日提交的附件申请书，由该台代表陈懋甫先生于1938年12月8日上午9时30分送达特务科，随附日本广播监理所颁发的一份许可证，授权原址位于福煦路930弄5号、已于1938年4月27日停播的友联电台（呼号XHHV），在爱多亚路560号中南酒店四楼的新址重新开播。

在1938年4月27日该台停播之前，它依据国民政府国际电信局局长温毓庆先生于1933年7月18日签发的第23号许可证，在880千周（K.C. 880）的频率波长上进行广播。1938年10月3日，收到该台请求重新开台的申请，但由于申请人未获得广播监理所的批准，且事实上拒绝承认该机构，故予以拒绝。然而，看来在此期间，友联电台已与日方接触并达成安排，从而获得了必要的许可（参见随附的许可证副本）。

然而，日本广播监理所为友联电台分配的频率波长为780千周（K.C.780），该波长已由美商广播电台（XMHE）预留，这是一家属于 P.H. Vanmeter 先生的美资电台

(vide Special Branch report dated 6.12.38). In view of
the information contained in the report on Mr.* Vanmeter's
station and that contained in the foregoing report, as well
as information supplied by Mr. Saunier of the Swiss owned
Liang Yue (XQCT) Station, it would appear that the Japanese
Broadcasting Superintendence Office is making every possible
effort to force foreign owned stations and Chinese owned
stations which have, up to date, abstained from registering
with the Japanese organ, to close down through confusion
of wavelengths, or to come within the sphere of Japanese
control.
It will be remembered that when a new station
(Chinese owned) applied for permission to operate, one of
the conditions that must be complied with is the supplying
to the S.M.P. of a guarantee undertaking not to obtrude on
an established wavelength. Instructions are therefore
solicited as to what reply should be given to the Yeu Lien

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Dawson

Reference the memo. by D.C. (Special Branch)
attached hereto, Mr. Chen Meu-foo (陳懋甫), representative
of the Yue Lien Broadcasting Station, was interviewed at the
Special Branch on October 6, 1938, when he was advised to
secure a registration certificate from the Japanese
Broadcasting Superintendence Office and informed that as
soon as he did so and submitted the usual guarantee to
the S.M.P., he would be permitted to operate his station.
In reply, Mr. Chen Meu-foo stated that he would
refer the matter to the Board of Directors and communicate
their decision later.
On October 10, 1938, Mr. Chen again visited the
Special Branch and, stating that the owners of the station
did not wish to have anything to do with the Japanese,
asked to be informed whether the Police would permit the
station to function without the sanction of the Japanese,
provided the station owners held themselves responsible
for whatever consequences might follow any measures the
Japanese should take against them.

D.S.I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

Sir, Chen Meu-foo was again
informed of the original decision
on 11.10.38 when he made no comment.
Logan

With reference to the attached application from the
Yue Lien Broadcasting Station for permission to resume
operations, Mr. Chen Meu-foo (陳懋甫 ), responsible
representative of the station, was interviewed at Police
Headquarters on the forenoon of October 5, 1938, when the
following particulars were obtained :-

The Yue Lien Station was first established in
July, 1933, by the Yue Lien Electric Radio Service Co. at
No.419 Avenue Dubail near Avenue Joffre, and removed to
Lane 930, 5 Avenue Foch about three years ago. The station
is in possession of permit No.23 dated 18/7/35 issued by
Mr. Wen Yueh-ching, Chief of the Bureau of International
Telegraphs of the National Government.

In April, 1938, the Yue Lien Station suspended
functioning, together with other Chinese owned stations,
when the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office
commenced to register broadcasting stations. Later, when
the majority of Chinese owned stations resumed functioning
following mediation by the Municipal Council, this station
failed to do so and the Board of Directors of the Yue Lien
Company decided to close temporarily pending developments
in the situation. Recently, the Board of Directors decided
to re-open and to remove the station to the Chung Nan Hotel,
560 Avenue Edward VII, which place is stated to be more
convenient.

During the interview, Mr. Chen intimated that he
has no intention to approach the Radio Broadcasting Superin-
tendence Office in view of the fact that there are several

友联电台最初由友联电气无线电服务公司于1933年7月在靠近霞飞路的杜拜尔路419号设立，约三年前迁至福煦路5号930弄。该台持有国民政府国际电信局局长温毓庆先生于1935年7月18日签发的第23号许可证。

1938年4月，当日本广播监理所开始注册广播电台时，友联电台与其他华资电台一起暂停运作。后来，当大多数华资电台在市议会调解后恢复运作时，该台未能如此，友联公司董事会决定暂时关闭，以待局势发展。最近，董事会决定重新开台，并将电台迁至爱多亚路560号的中南酒店，据称该处更为便利。

With reference to the application from the East Asia Broadcasting Station, (formerly located at Lane 185, 5 Rue Gaston Kahn, at present in the Wing On Roof Garden) for permission to operate, Mr. Yui Koh Tseng (俞國楨), Manager of the Station, was interviewed at Special Branch, Headquarters, at 11 a.m. May 12, when he was informed he would be required to observe the following conditions in accordance with the instructions of D.C. (Special Branch) :-
a) do not obtrude on other established wave lengths.
b) obtain authority from Chinese Government as soon as possible.
c) obtain authority from local authority if and when such is recognized by the S.M.C.
d) obey police instructions in the Settlement if a dispute arises.

He promised to observe strictly the foregoing instructions, and when questioned regarding the reason for the removal of the station (Vide Commissioner of Police query on report dated 11.5.38) he stated that as Rue Gaston Kahn is far away from the business centre and is inconvenient, it would affect the business of the station. Therefore, with this idea in view, he decided to remove to the Wing On Roof Garden.

He claimed that a station operating in the French Concession would incur a larger expenditure than one operating in the Settlement. He further claimed that a station like his would be required to pay a business "licence" fee of about $600 each year, to be paid in two instalments. In addition,

c) 如果且当地方当局得到工部局承认时，须获得该地方当局的授权。
d) 若租界内发生纠纷，须服从警方指令。

他承诺严格遵守上述指示，当被问及搬迁电台的原因时（参见警务处处长在1938年5月11日报告中的查询），他表示，由于盖司康路远离商业中心且交通不便，会影响电台业务。因此，出于此考虑，他决定迁至永安公司屋顶花园。

他声称，在法租界运营的电台比在公共租界运营的电台开支更大。他还声称，像他这样的电台每年需缴纳约600元的商业“执照”费，分两期支付。此外，

Translation of letter from East Asia Broadcasting
Station, Wing On Roof Garden, Nanking Road
------

May 10, 1938.

D.C. (Special Branch)

Our station was formerly located at Lane
185, 5 Rue Gaston Kahn. We applied to you for permission
to remove our station to the Wing On Roof Garden on
April 27, and on April 29, we submitted to you particulars
of the organization of the station, in which it was stated
our purpose is to undertake commercial broadcasting
and to assist in charitable enterprises. Now, we beg to
submit the following guarantee :-
1. Matters and news items touching on politics, or
considered objectionable by the Police will not be
broadcast.
2. Programmes will be submitted for your censorship
before they are broadcast.
3. When the "Broadcasting Stations Control Office" is
established in Shanghai, we will duly register with
it, if so required.
4. We will conduct our business in accordance with the
regulations of the Police.

Please approve and grant us permission for the
removal of our station. The frequency will be 780 k.c.

Chopped: Yui Koh Tseng (俞國楨)
East Asia Broadcasting Station
XLHJ.

1938年5月10日。

致：副总巡捕（特科）

本台原址位于盖司康路5号185弄。我们曾于4月27日向贵处申请将本台迁至永安公司屋顶花园，并于4月29日向贵处提交了本台组织详情，其中声明我们的目的是从事商业广播并协助慈善事业。现谨提交以下保证书：-
1. 凡涉及政治或被认为警方不宜的事项及新闻稿件，不予广播。
2. 节目在广播前将提交贵处审查。
3. 若上海成立“广播电台管理处”，我们将按要求 duly 向其注册。
4. 我们将依照警方规章开展业务。

恳请批准并准许本台搬迁。频率将为780千周。

Translation of letter received from the Yah Tung
Broadcasting Station.
----------

April 27, 1938.

To the Officer i/c Special Branch.

The Yah Tung Broadcasting Station was established
on January 21, 1933 when Permit No. 28 was issued to us
by the Telegraph Office of the Ministry of Communications
of the National Government. The Station was at first
located at 625 Avenue Edward VII, later removed to 47
Kong Loh Tsung, Avenue Foch where business was carried
out for approximately two years. The Station was later
again removed to No.5, Lane 185, Rue Gaston Kahn but owing
to this place being too far away no business was done.
Now we have found a suitable place on the roof garden of
Wing On Company and wish to resume our broadcasting
business there. Our former wave length, 760 KC has been
adopted by the Foh Ying Station and we propose to take
780 KC formerly used by Sun Sun Station whose present wave
length is 800 KC. We therefore write to request your
permission for removal and the adoption of the new wave
length and also to issue a broadcasting permit for our
station.

Yui Koh Tsung 俞國楨
Yah Tung Broadcasting Station.
(亚东电气)

1938年4月27日。

致特别处主管警官。

亚东广播电台（Yah Tung Broadcasting Station）成立于1933年1月21日，当时国民政府交通部电政司向我台颁发了第28号许可证。电台最初位于爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）625号，后迁至福煦路（Avenue Foch）公乐总汇47号，在此经营约两年。随后电台又迁至盖斯康路（Rue Gaston Kahn）185弄5号，但因该地过于偏远，未能开展业务。现我们在永安公司屋顶花园找到一处合适地点，希望在此恢复广播业务。我台原波长760千周（KC）已被佛音电台采用，我们拟采用新声电台目前未使用的原波长780千周（该台现用波长为800千周）。因此，特致函请求批准迁移及采用新波长，并为我台颁发广播许可证。

Subject......King Ying Broadcasting Station - change of ownership.

Made by...D.S.I...Logan................Forwarded by.........D. I. Crawford

Further to Special Branch report dated
June 11, 1940, on the above subject, Mr. Sung
Mong Lai (孫夢雷) called at the Special
Branch on the afternoon of June 15, 1940, and
reported that he has purchased the station from
Mr. Huang Kuo Bing (黃國屏).
Mr. Sung stated that he was formerly a
partner in the King Ying Station and now becomes
the sole owner. The licence issued by the
Japanese Broadcasting Superintendent's Office,
Hardoon Building, Nanking Road, to the King Ying
Station expired on May 29, 1940 and renewal was
refused. The station suspended broadcasting on
May 30, 1940.
He is aware that permission to use wavelength
K.C. 1360 has been given by the Japanese
Broadcasting Superintendent's Office to the
Kwang Ming Broadcasting Station, call sign A.H.H.A.,
now in course of installation on the 3rd floor of
the New World Amusement Resort, 4 Bubbling Well
Road. However, he will endeavour to secure
permission from the Japanese to operate under
a new name and on a new wavelength, but these
have not yet been decided upon. He was requested
to inform the Special Branch by letter when
permission to operate is obtained and he agreed
to do so.

dated 12/6/40
by D.S.I. MacAdie).

Date October 28, 1938.

Subject Report on Station X.Q.H.K.

Made by O.A. R.J. Broadley Forwarded by [Signature]
O/C.

Sir:-
Regarding the work carried out this morning on checking
the King Ying Broadcasting Station X.Q.H.K. 1380 Kc., a Precision
Wavemeter was used and the frequency of the station was found
to be correct. From 11.30 to 11.45 A.M. this station was put
on the air for a test and in the Radio Room at C.C.R. this
station was tuned-in on two receivers and both registered 1380
Kc., for X.Q.H.K. We also found a signal from X.Q.H.K. on 1400
Kc., This latter signal may be caused by another Broadcast
station operating on a frequency close to 1380 Kc. A suggestion
that we may put forward is that the X.Q.H.K. Broadcast station
which operates on 1380 Kc., go on the air when the Broadcast
station X.Z.H.D. which operates on 1360 Kc., is off the air
and see if it is possible to hear his own signal on 1400 Kc.,
as well as on his standard frequency of 1380.
If his own signal cannot be heard on 1400 Kc., when the
other Broadcast station is not operating then the cause of
his second signal being on 1400 Kc., is through a Radio fault
which is picked up by the Broadcast station operating on 1360
Kc., and re-radiating the signal of 1380 Kc., on 1400 Kc, but
the above statement has to be tested as mentioned above.

I am,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
[Signature: R J Broadley]
O. A.

先生:-
关于今早检查金鹰广播电台 X.Q.H.K. 1380 Kc. 所做的工作，使用了精密波长计，发现该电台频率正确。上午11:30至11:45，该电台开机测试，在中央无线电台站的无线电室内，两台接收机均调谐到该电台，且均显示为 X.Q.H.K. 的1380 Kc.。我们还在1400 Kc.上发现了来自 X.Q.H.K. 的信号。后一信号可能是由另一家在接近1380 Kc.频率上运营的广播电台造成的。我们可以提出的建议是，让在1380 Kc.运营的 X.Q.H.K. 广播电台，当在1360 Kc.运营的 X.Z.H.D. 广播电台停机时开机，看看是否能在1400 Kc.以及其标准频率1380上听到其自身信号。
如果当另一家广播电台不运营时，在1400 Kc.上听不到其自身信号，那么其在1400 Kc.出现第二个信号的原因是通过无线电故障，该故障被在1360 Kc.运营的广播电台接收，并将1380 Kc.的信号在1400 Kc.上重新辐射，但上述说法必须如上所述进行测试。

我是，
先生，
您顺从的仆人，
[签名: R J Broadley]

Subject King Ying Broadcasting Station (XQHK) K.C. 1300, given

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C Crawford

Reference Special Branch report dated 23/10/38 on
the subject of the suspending of the King Ying Broadcasting
Station in order to compel it to effect adjustment of its
wavelength control and the attached letter dated 22/10/38,
addressed to the Police Department, S.M.C. by Major Asano
of the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office, complaining
of the action of the Police in suspending the King Ying
Station, tests were carried out by the personnel of C.C.R.
during the forenoon and evening of October 25 and early
morning of October 26 when it was found that the King Ying
Station broadcast was not obtruding on the Alliance Francaise
Station (K.C.1400) and appeared to be within the prescribed
limit. It was found, however, that some other Station, at
present unidentified, was obtruding to some extent on K.C.
1400. Efforts are being continued by the staff of C.C.R. to
identify the offending station but these are rendered
difficult by the fact that the offending station does not
broadcast its call sign every half hour as is customary.

Mr. Huang Kuo-bing (黄國屏), Manager of the King
Ying Station, was informed at 9.40 a.m. October 26 that the
Station might resume broadcasting forthwith, and the Sub-
Inspector on Duty, Louza, requested to withdraw the C.P.C.
posted on duty in the radio station.

Mr. Perie of the Section Politique, French Police,
was also informed of the result of the tests and also that
the King Ying Station had been granted permission to resume
broadcasting.

A report on the tests carried out will be submitted

参考1938年10月23日关于暂停金鹰广播电台以迫使其调整波长控制的特别处报告，以及附上的1938年10月22日日本广播监理处浅野少校致上海公共租界工部局警务处的信函，信中投诉警方暂停金鹰电台的行动。中央无线电台站人员于10月25日上午和晚上以及10月26日凌晨进行了测试，发现金鹰电台的广播未干扰法兰西联盟电台（1400千周），且似乎在规定限度内。然而，发现另有某家电台（目前身份不明）在一定程度上干扰了1400千周。中央无线电台站工作人员正继续努力识别违规电台，但由于违规电台未按惯例每半小时播报一次呼号，使得识别工作困难重重。

金鹰电台经理黄国屏先生于10月26日上午9:40获知，该电台可立即恢复广播，并要求卢家湾值班副督察撤出部署在广播电台的值勤警员（C.P.C.）。

法国警察政治科 Perie 先生也获知了测试结果，以及金鹰电台已获准恢复广播的消息。

Radio Broadcast Control Office
October 23, 1938. No. S. B. D.
Date

Police Department,
S. M. C.

Re: Ching Ying Radio Station

Dear Sirs,

It has come to our notice that at about 11 a.m.
to-day a party of S.M.C. officers, comprising two plain
clothes Foreign Constables, a Chinese Detective, an
interpreter and a C.P.C. 200, accompanied by a Frenchman,
presumably a representative of the local French Radio
Station, visited Room 511, 5th Floor, Shun Chow Hotel,
136 Nanking Road, and closed down the Ching Ying Radio
Station (金鷹電台) located at this address. The
reason given for the order of suspension by the Police
Officers concerned is that the Ching Ying Station broad-
casting over carrier frequency of 1,480 kc. disturbs the
operations of the French Central Radio Station with
frequency of 1,400 kc due to the proximity of the frequency.

Before leaving the premises after closing down the
station, the officers posted C.P.C. 200 to maintain
guard at this place.

As you are already aware, the authority for the
control of radio stations has come into our hands since
1.3.38 and should any question crop up regarding wave
length, the proper procedure would be to notify us in the
first place and await our rulings after investigation.
In the present case quoted above it would appear that
action was taken by you on the complaint of the French
Radio Station without any reference to us and accepting
the complaint blindly without taking the trouble to enquire
into the matter. Apart from the irregularities in the
procedure adopted by you in ordering the suspension
of the station concerned, we must point out the great
being
inconvenience and financial loss suffered by the station

日期

警务处，
上海公共租界工部局。

事由：金鹰广播电台

敬启者：

我方获悉，今日上午11时许，一队上海公共租界工部局官员，包括两名便衣外籍巡捕、一名华籍侦探、一名翻译和一名200号驻派警员，在一位法国人（推测为当地法国广播电台代表）的陪同下，前往南京路136号新昌酒店五楼511室，关闭了位于此地址的金鹰广播电台（金鷹電台）。有关警官下达停播令的理由是，金鹰电台以1,480千周载波频率广播，因频率相近，干扰了频率为1,400千周的法国中央广播电台的运作。

在关闭电台离开现场前，官员们部署了200号驻派警员在此地维持警戒。

正如贵方所知，自1938年3月1日起，广播电台的管制权已移交我方，若出现任何关于波长的问题，适当程序应是首先通知我方，并在调查后等待我方裁决。在上述案例中，贵方似乎是在法国广播电台投诉后采取行动，未与我方协商，且未费心调查此事便盲目接受投诉。除了贵方下令暂停相关电台的程序存在违规之处外，我们必须指出该电台遭受的巨大不便和经济损失

page_data.en:
(2)
due to irrational suspension of business.
In this connection we would like to add also that
since 13.8.43, the Main Tokyo Radio Station has adopted
crystall point stabilizer system and for this reason the
broadcasting has become very accurate. Therefore, if the
French Station concerned complain of disturbance there
must be some defect in mechanism of the French Station.
In the circumstances, we should appreciate if you
would be good enough to withdraw the order for suspension
forthwith and at the same time inform the French Station
that the question of complaint be referred to us for
settlement.
Yours faithfully,
(Sgd.) KAZUO ASANO,
President.

因无理暂停营业。
在此方面，我们要补充说明，
自1943年8月13日起，东京中央广播电台已采用

有关法国电台抱怨受到干扰，那一定是法国电台的
机械装置存在某些缺陷。
鉴于上述情况，如蒙贵方
立即撤回停业令，并同时告知法国电台
将投诉事宜转交我方处理，
我们将不胜感激。
此致，

page_data.zh:
正如阁下所知，自本年八月二十日起，无线电波的管制及其他一切与电信有关的事务，均由本监督处负责执行。若发生涉及无线电波的问题，恳请首先向本处提出，经详细调查后予以解决。据称，法国电报公司（Compagnie Française des Télégraphes）已提出上述请求。然而，本处若仅凭法方断言，盲目听从其一面之词，立即命令停止广播，不仅在学术上存在错误，而且会对正当经营者造成非法的巨大困扰和损害。此外，前述金厅电台自去年九月十八日以来一直采用晶体控制振荡方式，其发射电波稳定可靠。因此，如果确实存在电波干扰的事实，那只能是法国电报公司一方存在缺陷，别无其他原因。

鉴于上述情况，恳请贵处对金厅电台立即解除广播禁令，同时请向法国电报公司传达：此类问题应首先向本处提出，并等待本处的处理结果。

此致

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford.

At 10 a.m. October 22, 1938, Mr. Perie of the
French Police Political Section came to the Special Branch
and stated that for some time the King Ying Broadcasting
Station (XQHK) K.C.1380, located at Room 516 of 150
Chelkiang Road was obtruding on the wavelength of K.C.1400
of the Alliance Francaise Station, 193 Avenue Joffre and
requested that the management of the King Ying Station
should be compelled to adjust their wave length.

Reference Special Branch report dated 24/6/38, it
will be noted that on June 23 this station was warned for
obtruding on K.C. 1400 and informed that a further
infraction of the condition of his guarantee pledge might
result in the closure of his station.

Acting upon the instructions of D.C. (Special
Branch) assistance was obtained from D.S.I. Black (Louza),
and Mr. Wong Zao-chi (王肇基 ), accountant of the King
Ying Station, was required to close the station and refrain
from broadcasting until such time as the necessary
adjustment is effected. A C.P.C. was posted in the
broadcasting studio to see that the station remains closed
(D.O. "A" informed).

C.A. Moss and O.A. Broadley attached to C.C.R.
accompanied the party of detectives and examined the
equipment of the station which was found to be of inferior
material and in a dilapidated condition.

Mr. Wong Zao-chi, aforesaid, was instructed to
inform the Special Branch as soon as the necessary

Alliance Francaise Station, French Concession.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford
At 10 a.m. 23-6-38, Mr. Perie, of the Political Section,
French Police, visited Special Branch Headquarters, and stated
that for some time the King Ying Broadcasting Station, 159
Chekiang Road, call sign XQHK, frequency K.C.1380 has been
obtruding on the wave length K.C.1400 of the Alliance Francaise
Station, 193 Avenue Joffre and requested that the management
of the King Ying Station should be requested to adjust their
wave length.
Mr. Huang Kuo Ping (黃國屏), manager of the King Ying
Station, was interviewed at Special Branch, Headquarters,
at 4 p.m. 23-6-38, when he promised to adjust his wave length
forthwith. He was warned that in the event of a further
complaint being received the Police might consider closing
his station and at the same time reminded of the condition
contained in the guarantee supplied by him to the Police
whereby he bound himself not to obtrude on any other wave
length.
D.C.(Special Branch)

The attached letter (translation attached)

Reference attached file on this station, it
will be recalled that before installing the broadcasting
equipment at 159 Chekiang Road (4th floor), the King
Ying Broadcasting Station obtained permission from the
Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office to do so,
but such permission was not regarded as the effecting
of registration.

In view of the fact that several recent
applications for permission to establish broadcasting
stations have been refused for the time being, it is
suggested that the King Ying Station be likewise refused
permission to commence operating pending a settlement
of the question of registration and supervision of radio
broadcasting stations in the Settlement.

Should permission be granted to this station,
which of its own volition applied direct to the Japanese
and was granted permission to install its equipment,
such action would tend to influence those stations which
were refused permission by the S.M.P. to deal direct with
the Japanese, as they might be led to believe that the

May 16, 1938.

To Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police Hdqrs.

This station will commence broadcasting from
April 19. The purpose of the station is to broadcast
on a purely commercial basis. We will strictly abide
by the following rules :-
1. We will not broadcast anything of a political nature
or any items or news that the police may regard as
objectionable.
2. We will submit for censorship programmes prior to
broadcasting.
3. We will apply for registration when an office for the
control of broadcasting stations has been established
in Shanghai.
4. We will abide by all Police regulations in all business
dealings of this station.

We submit herewith for your censorship the
programmes for the last three days.

(Chopped) Wong Kuo Bing (黃國屏)

1938年5月16日。

致：
上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别部门（Special Branch）

本台将于4月19日开始广播。本台宗旨为纯商业性广播。我们将严格遵守以下规则：-
1. 我们不广播任何具有政治性质的内容，或警方可能视为不当的任何项目或新闻。
2. 我们将在广播前提交节目以供审查。
3. 当上海设立广播电台管理机构时，我们将申请注册。
4. 在本台的所有业务往来中，我们将遵守所有警务规章。

现随函附上过去三天的节目单，供贵处审查。

（盖章）黄国屏 (Wong Kuo Bing)
“金鹰广播电台”

Subject King Ying Broadcasting Station (XQHK) - application
for registration.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford

In accordance with the instructions of
D.C. (Special Branch) on attached letter, dated April 28,
1938, from the King Ying Broadcasting Station (XQHK),
159 Chekiang Road, to the Special Branch, applying for
registration, Mr. Wong Kuo Bing (黄國屏) proprietor,
manager and engineer of the said station, was interviewed
at Special Branch Headquarters on April 29, 1938, when
he was advised to make application to the Japanese
Broadcasting Superintendence Office either direct or
through the Special Branch. In reply, he stated that
he had approached the Japanese before installing the
Station and produced a document endorsed by the Broadcasting
Superintendence Office granting him permission to proceed
with the installation (translation attached). As the
document mentioned did not appear to be in the nature of
a certificate of registration, he was given a copy of
Japanese Notification No.2 and requested to complete the
questionaire and thereafter forward same to the Special
Branch or direct to the Japanese. On the afternoon of
April 29, 1938, he handed a letter to the Special Branch
containing the required particulars (translation attached)
which is forwarded herewith for transmission to the
Broadcasting Superintendence Office.

(批：Include with others in due course)

D. S. I.

Date May 2nd, 1938.
Subject Dah Kwong Ming Broadcasting Station - to commence operation.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.S.

On May 2nd, 1938, Messrs. Chao Ching Foong and Miao
Chi Tsih of the Dah Kwong Ming Broadcasting Station, 584
Burkill Road, called at Police Headquarters and reported
that the station would commence operating on May 5, 1938.
During the visit they submitted a draft of the programme
to be adopted by the station. Perusal of the draft,
which is attached herewith, shows that it contains singing,
drama, comedy, story-telling items and nothing of an
objectionable nature.

They were reminded that the introduction of anything
relating to politics or articles objectionable to the
police would entail immediate action, which instructions
they stated they fully understood.

Application for registration with the Japanese
Broadcasting Superintendence Office has already been forwarded.

Logan
D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

Subject Application from Dah Kwong Ming Broadcasting Station
for permission.
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C. Crawford D.I.

In connection with the attached application for
permission to establish a radio station, Messrs. Chao
Ching Foong (趙景峰) and Miao Chi Tsih (繆治捷),
accompanied by Mr. T. L. Chang (張登瀛), ex-General
Secretary of the P.M.A.A., called at the Police Headquarters
on the morning of April 18, 1938, when they were informed
that they would be required to submit to the Police a
guarantee to refrain from broadcasting any political
propaganda and that furthermore, they would be required
to observe the following conditions in accordance with
the instruction of D.C. (Special Branch) :
a) do not obtrude on other established wave lengths.
b) obtain authority from Chinese Government as soon as
possible.
c) obtain authority from local authority if and when
such is recognized by the S.M.C.
d) obey police instructions in the Settlement if a dispute
arises.

In addition to a verbal promise to observe
strictly the foregoing instructions, a letter of guarantee
was received by Special Branch on April 19. The letter
is attached herewith together with translation.

With reference to the programme, the promoters
of the station promise to send the Police a copy as soon
as the Station is ready to operate.

Sih Tse liang

:D 68:3/4/Fv
With reference to Special Branch report dated May 12, 1938 regarding the closing on May 12 of the Dah Yah Broadcasting Station by the Municipal Police at the request of the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence Office, a telephone message was received by the Special Branch, on the afternoon of 24.6.38, from the Sub Inspector on duty, Louza, to the effect that several Japanese had visited the Dah Yah Broadcasting Station on that date. Subsequent enquiries ascertained that the Dah Yah Station submitted on May 17, an application to the Broadcasting Superintendence Office for permission to resume operations. Consequently, several officials of the Broadcasting Superintendence Office visited the station located at 545 Kiukiang Road during the afternoon of June 24 and carried out an inspection of the equipment of the station. According to the Broadcasting Superintendence Office, should the application of the Dah Yah Station be approved, a certificate will be issued to them, in which event the station will resume operations on June 27 or 28, and the Municipal Police will be informed in due course.
The application submitted by the Dah Yah Broadcasting Station gives the name of Mr. Soong Chi (宋杰), otherwise known as Mr. Soong Sze-siang (宋士), a lawyer, living at Lane 351 No. 4 Elgin Road, as manager instead of Mr. Koo Sung-shiang (顧沈香), who was in the position prior to the closure of the station.
D.S. Kamashita reported on 25.6.38 that Major Asano of the Broadcasting Superintendence Office, in course of a conversation with the D.C. (Japanese) some days ago, informed the latter of the foregoing information and stated that as soon as permission

Date April 6, 19 38
Subject Dah Yah Broadcasting Station - application for permission.
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C. Crawford D.I.

With reference to the attached application from
大亚
the Dah Yah Broadcasting Station, 545 Kiukiang Road, for
permission to operate, Mr. Koo Sung Shang(顧沈香), the
applicant, was interviewed at Police Headquarters on the
afternoon of April 5, when he stated that his programme would
consist of drama, songs, and advertisements of the usual
nature. He was informed that he should submit to the Police
a guarantee to refrain from broadcasting any political
propaganda. In addition the instructions of D.C. (Special
Branch) regarding the operation of a new station, contained
in the memo dated February 25, 1938 were conveyed to him viz.
a) do not obtrude on other established wave lengths.
b) obtain authority from Chinese Government as soon as possible.
c) obtain authority from the local authority if and when such
becomes necessary.
d) obey police instructions in the Settlement if a dispute
arises.

With regard to (a), it was pointed out to him that
the wave length 1,020 k.c. as mentioned in his letter had
already been taken by the Hwa Tai(華泰)(XLHB) Broadcasting
Station (Vide letter received by the Municipal Police on
April 1, 1938). Mr. Koo agreed to change the wave length to
1,160 k.c.

In addition to his verbal promise to observe strictly
the foregoing instructions, the letter of guarantee was also
delivered to the Special Branch the same afternoon. The
letter is attached herewith together with translation.

（左侧批注：M.B. / 1020 / only / m(b) / S.I. / D.R. / 6/4 / C.）

关于附件中来自九江路545号大亚广播电台的运营许可申请，申请人顾沈香先生（Koo Sung Shang）于4月5日下午在警察总局接受问询，当时他表示其节目将由戏剧、歌曲和常规性质的广告组成。被告知他应向警方提交一份保证书，承诺不广播任何政治宣传。此外，还向他传达了1938年2月25日备忘录中关于新电台运营的D.C. (特别处) 指令，即：
a) 不得干扰其他既定波长。
b) 尽快获得中国政府授权。
c) 如有必要，获得地方当局授权。
d) 若租界内发生纠纷，服从警方指令。

关于(a)项，向他指出，其信中提到的1,020千周波长已被华泰（華泰）(XLHB) 广播电台占用（参见工部局警务处于1938年4月1日收到的信件）。顾先生同意将波长更改为1,160千周。

除了口头承诺严格遵守上述指令外，保证书也于当日下午送达特别处。该信随附于此，并附译文。

page_data.en:
Appendix "B"

The following is an urgent notice inserted by
LIU TSHUNG SAN (劉春山) in the advertisement columns
of the Sin Wen Pao of August 27, 1941 :-

I wish to express my appreciation for the kind
patronage extended to me by the public since I, a man wanting
in ability and knowledge, have taken up the profession of
a singer. Last year my health failed and as a result I
was secluded from outside circles, thus giving rise to
certain unfavourable impressions. However, during this
period I have never been slow behind others in participating
in the raising of contributions sponsored by either public
or private bodies.

Nevertheless, certain unscrupulous elements,
perceiving the susceptibility of philanthropists in Shanghai
to deception, have of late fabricated rumours which are
absolutely unfounded. It is feared that in the near
future these persons will openly solicit for contributions.

In order to safeguard my integrity as well as to
prevent the public from being swindled, I am firmly refusing
to take part in the radio broadcasts as requested by these
"money-grabbing gangsters," and I shall disown my name should
it appear in the list of participants.

I publish this notice for the information of the
public lest they should not be aware of the real circumstances.
page_data.zh:
附件 “B”

以下是刘春山 (LIU TSHUNG SAN / 劉春山) 于1941年8月27日在《新闻报》广告栏刊登的紧急声明：-

本人才疏学浅，投身歌者行业以来，承蒙公众厚爱，不胜感激。去年因健康欠佳，遂深居简出，不与外界接触，因而引起某些不良印象。然而，在此期间，本人在参与公私团体发起的捐款活动时，从未落后于人。

尽管如此，某些不法之徒利用上海慈善家易受欺骗的心理，近期捏造了毫无根据的谣言。恐怕这些人在不久的将来会公开募捐。

为了维护本人的名誉，也为了防止公众受骗，本人坚决拒绝参加这些“敛财匪徒”要求的无线电广播，如果本人的名字出现在参与者名单中，本人概不承认。

特此登报，以告公众，以免不知实情。

page_data.en:
劉春山緊要啓事
啟者春山不才胸無存竹自流入賣唱承蒙各界賜顧相邀不勝感激之至自去歲身遭病困以來當然
與外界隔絕而引起不良影響不過春山在過度時期中無論社會地方或公私團體每逢舉行籌募捐
春山無不奮勇參加向不後人盡力而爲此乃已往之事實無用再述近有不肖無恥之徒見上海善
士好騙故胆敢巧立名目全無稽考恐怕不久即將公開向各募捐春山爲保全人格及不使諸君受騙
故對這班「撈血黨」之要求公演與播音完全拒絕如再發現春山之微名按次例入刊載春山庶不任
認深恐各界不明眞相特此登報聲請高名賢士明察秋毫此乃春山之爲人一貫正氣是也

Subject Broadcast of attacks on members of rice trade.

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

* File DS8039A/...
(30-10-...)

Copy sent
to Mr. T. Beeley
4/11/40

With reference to that part of the Price
Investigation Committee report (attached) and the
remarks of the D.C. (Crime & Special Branches),
regarding the broadcasting of attacks over local
radio stations on members of rice trade, enquiries
show that songs denouncing speculators and hoarders
in the rice and coal trades are occasionally
broadcast by certain Pootung songsters and comedians.
Mr. Chen Shien Tsoong (陳顯宗), a committee
member of the Radio Broadcasting Stations' Association,
71 Chihli Road, was interviewed at headquarters on
the forenoon of November 2, when he was informed of
the undesirable nature of such broadcasts and
requested to have these broadcasts stopped. It was
explained to him that if not stopped there was a
likelihood of such incitement being taken seriously
with attacks against the person concerned in the
trades mentioned, with which view Mr. Chen agreed,
and stated he would put the matter before the
responsible members of the Association and with a
view to issuing a circular notice to the radio
station owners.

C. Crawford
D. I.

D.C. (Crime & Special Branches)
