Subject Shanghai Municipality Private Broadcasting Stations'
Guild - office established in Settlement.

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

The Shanghai Municipality Private Broadcasting
Stations' Guild, which is sponsored by the Japanese
Radio Broadcasting Control Office, established an
office in Room A6, 1st floor, 119 Nanking Road on
August 1, 1939. The association previously occupied
an office in the Astor House, Hongkew.

The Chinese person responsible have been
notified to register with the Shanghai Municipal Police
before they can be allowed to function. This is a
purely Chinese concern backed by the Japanese and as
such should be compelled to register. The detective
informing them was told there was no need to register
with the Shanghai Municipal Police as the Japanese were
behind them and refused to disclose the personnel of
the guild; this it is respectfully suggested is a
flagrant case of interference with the power of the
Police.

C Crawford

Regulations of the Shanghai Municipality Private
Broadcasting Stations' Guild
(上海市民營廣播電台同業公會)

PART I - General Rules

Art. 1 - This body is known as the Shanghai Municipality
Private Broadcasting Stations' Guild, which has
been formed by radio stations in Shanghai,
privately owned and registered with the chief
controlling organ.

Art. 2 - The object of this guild is to promote the welfare
and mutual friendship of radio station owners.

Art. 3 - The office of the guild is established at ........

PART II - Membership

Art. 4 - All radio stations in the Shanghai area which are
registered with the chief controlling organ will
be allowed to become members of the guild provided
they observe the regulations, discipline and
decisions of the body. The procedure of joining
is as follows :-

(a) complete a membership pledge form.

(b) Pay the entrance fee.

Art. 5 - Privileges of a member :-

(a) The right of being elected or electing others.

(b) The right of submitting and deciding upon
proposals.

(c) Entitled to enjoy the benefits enumerated in
these regulations.

Art. 6 - Duties of a member :-

(a) To obey the regulations and decisions of the
guild.

(b) To take charge of duties assigned.

(c) To answer enquiries and investigations by
the guild.

(d) To pay membership fees at the right time.

(e) To attend meetings punctually.

(f) Not to encroach upon the business of others.

Art. 7 - In case a member violates one of the rules
mentioned in Article 6, the defaulter will be
warned in a minor case, and on the second occasion
will be deprived of all privileges. In a serious
case, the defaulter will be expelled from the
guild and will be referred to the controlling
organ to be dealt with.

上海市私营广播电台同业公会规章
(上海市民營廣播電台同業公會)

第一部分 - 总则

第一条 - 本团体名为上海市私营广播电台同业公会，由在上海私人拥有并向主要管制机关注册的广播电台组成。

第二条 - 本公会的宗旨是促进电台业主的福利和相互友谊。

第三条 - 公会办事处设于 ........

第二部分 - 会员

第四条 - 上海地区所有向主要管制机关注册的广播电台，只要遵守本团体的规章、纪律和决议，均允许成为公会会员。入会程序如下：

(a) 填写入会誓愿书。

(b) 缴纳入会费。

第五条 - 会员权利：

(a) 选举权和被选举权。

(b) 提案权和表决权。

(c) 享有本规章所列各项权益。

第六条 - 会员义务：

(a) 遵守公会的规章和决议。

(b) 承担指派的任务。

(c) 回答公会的询问和调查。

(d) 按时缴纳会费。

(e) 准时出席会议。

(f) 不侵犯他人的业务。

第七条 - 若会员违反第六条所述规则之一，情节轻微者予以警告，再犯者剥夺一切权利。情节严重者，将其开除出公会，并移交管制机关处理。

- 2 -

Art. 8 - Members are not allowed to leave the guild without reason.

Art. 9 - When a member is expelled from the guild, the money paid by the member will not be refunded.

Art.10 - When a dispute arising between members cannot be solved privately, the dispute will be referred to the chief controlling organ for decision. Members will not be allowed to raise any objection to the decision rendered.

PART III - Organization

Art.11-- The unit member of the guild is a radio station. Each station is entitled to appoint the manager or a responsible representative to the guild.

Art.12 - Representatives appointed by member stations should be provided with a letter of appointment and the guild should be informed of same. Similar steps should be followed when the representatives are changed.

Art.13 - This guild will be under the direction and supervision of the chief controlling organ in Shanghai.

PART IV - Staff employees

Art.14 - Five of the members of the guild will be elected to serve on the executive committee. The election will be held during a general representative meeting of members. One of the members of the executive committee will be elected as chairman. the standing committee to look after daily affairs.

Art.15 - The service period of an executive committee member will be ....... (year-s)

Art.16 - The executive committee will consist of the following departments, each of which will have a chief to be appointed by the executive committee who will be in charge of the affairs of the respective departments:-

(a) 1st Department To take charge of documents, despatching and receiving; accounting; general affairs; compilation of reports; as well as matters not coming under the other departments.

(b) 2nd Department To take charge of welfare matters of members.

(c) 3rd Department To take charge of publications, registration and organization of members.

Art.17 - Each department will be allowed to engage a number of staff members to assist in its affairs. They will be employed by the respective chiefs.

Art.18 - Duties of the Executive Committee :-

(a) To execute the affairs of the guild.

(b) To represent the guild in matters relating to outsiders.

(c) To convene meetings of members and execute decisions.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

第八条 - 会员不得无故退会。

第九条 - 会员被开除出会时，其所缴款项概不退还。

第十条 - 会员间发生纠纷且无法私下解决时，应将纠纷提交最高主管机关裁决。会员对所作裁决不得提出任何异议。

第三部分 - 组织

第十一条 -- 本会之基本会员单位为广播电台。各台有权委派经理或负责人作为代表加入本会。

第十二条 - 会员单位委派的代表应持有委任书，并通知本会。更换代表时，亦应遵循相同程序。

第十三条 - 本会受上海最高主管机关的指导与监督。

第四部分 - 职员

第十四条 - 从会员中选举五人组成执行委员会。选举在会员全体代表大会期间举行。执行委员会成员中选举一人为主席，并设立常务委员会处理日常事务。

第十五条 - 执行委员会委员的任期为……（年）

第十六条 - 执行委员会下设下列各部门，各部设主任一人，由执行委员会任命，负责各部事务：-

(a) 第一部 负责文件收发；会计；总务；报告编纂；以及不属于其他各部门管辖的事项。

(b) 第二部 负责会员福利事项。

(c) 第三部 负责出版物、会员登记及组织工作。

第十七条 - 各部可雇用若干职员协助处理事务。职员由 respective 主任雇用。

第十八条 - 执行委员会职责：-

(a) 执行本会事务。

(b) 在涉及外部人员的事项中代表本会。

(c) 召集会员会议并执行决议。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

(d) To receive and accept proposals of members.

PART V - Meetings

Art. 19 - General representative meetings of members will
be held half yearly, but such meetings may be
called at the request of more than two thirds of
the members, when it is considered necessary.

Art. 20 - Meetings of the Executive Committee will be held
every week (or every two weeks). During the
meetings, a report on guild affairs during the
past one or two weeks will be made by the standing
committee and discussions on future affairs will be
held.

Art. 21 - A meeting will only be opened when more than half
of the total number of members attend, and
decisions will be passed when more than half of
those present approve.

PART VI - Finance

Art. 22 - The funds of the guild will depend upon the
following :-

(a) Members' entrance fees.

(b) Members' monthly subscriptions and annual
subscriptions.

(c) Special subscriptions.

(d) Sinking fund.

Art. 23 - When special subscriptions are to be collected
to meet special requirements, the collection should
first be approved by a general representative
meeting and must also be approved by the chief
controlling organ before it can be put into force.

PART VII - Appendix

Art. 24 - Rules governing the holding of meetings will be
made separately.

Art. 25 - These regulations are subject to amendment
provided it is decided upon by the general
representative meeting and approved by the chief
controlling organ.

Art. 26 - These regulations will be forwarded to the chief
controlling organ for reference as well as for
enforcement.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

(d) 接收并受理会员提案。

第五部分 - 会议

第十九条 - 会员全体代表大会每半年举行一次，但在认为必要时，经三分之二以上会员请求，亦可召开此类会议。

第二十条 - 执行委员会会议每周（或每两周）举行一次。会上由常务委员会报告过去一两周的本会事务，并对未来事务进行讨论。

第二十一条 - 会议仅在超过半数会员出席时方可召开，决议须经出席者过半数同意方为通过。

第六部分 - 财务

第二十二条 - 本会经费来源如下：-

(a) 会员入会费。

(b) 会员月费及年费。

(c) 特别捐。

(d) 偿债基金。

第二十三条 - 为满足特殊需要而征收特别捐时，须先经会员全体代表大会批准，并须获最高主管机关批准后方可实施。

第七部分 - 附则

第二十四条 - 会议举行规则另行制定。

第二十五条 - 本章程经会员全体代表大会决定并经最高主管机关批准后，可进行修订。

第二十六条 - 本章程将呈送最高主管机关备案并予以执行。

Reference the attached translation of a letter dated
11.9.38, addressed by one Chang Ching Pah (張敬伯),
Tsung Chang (正章) Dry Cleaning Shop, 600 Avenue Joffre,
to the Special Branch, requesting advice as to whether it
is necessary to submit names of actors, details of programmes,
etc., to the Special Branch for approval, when special
programmes are being broadcast for purely commercial adverti-
sing purposes, it should be mentioned that the writing of
the letter mentioned was prompted by the fact that recently
the Yung Sung Station (XHHJ) refused to accept a special
commercial advertising programme from the writer unless the
latter could produce a letter from the Special Branch saying
that the programmes had been approved. In this connection
Chang Ching Pah called at the Special Branch and requested a
letter along the lines indicated. He was informed that
the management of the respective radio stations is held
responsible to ensure that political or other objectionable
matter is not broadcast and that it was not the practice of
the Police to censor purely commercial advertising, further,
that if the Yung Sung Station chose to refuse to accept his
programme, it was entitled to do so and purely a matter for
the station to decide. It should be mentioned that only in
such cases as special broadcasts for charitable purposes,
etc., does the Special Branch require details of programmes,
etc., when approval is given or withheld.

（批：Detached & put together with previous ones in envelope approved file）

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 24 MAY 1938）

The seventeen Chinese broadcasting stations which
are at present operating in the International Settlement
have all affixed their respective seals to the amended
pledge forms prepared by the Municipal Police, in which
the responsible representative of each station guarantees
to observe the instructions of the Police contained
therein. A list of these stations, together with the
pledge forms, is attached herewith.

The last mentioned station on the attached list,
namely, the Fuh Ying ( 佛音 ) Broadcasting Station,
418 Hart Road, call sign X.M.H.B., Frequency 980 K.C.,
which suspended functioning on April 15, 1938, over the
question of registration with the Broadcasting Superin-
tendence Office, resumed broadcasting on May 20. It
will be recalled that on May 8, 1938, when all managers
of stations were instructed to submit particulars relating
to their respective stations, the management of this
station refused to do so, and expressed determination to
suspend operations (Vide Special Branch report dated
10/5/38). During an interview at Special Branch,
Headquarters, on May 23, when he submitted the pledge
form, duly filled in, Mr. Li Sih Tang ( 李棠 ), the
responsible representative of this station, intimated
that although his station had resumed operations and
submitted the pledge, he was not prepared to sign and
fill in any forms issued in the name of the Broadcasting
Superintendence Office.

（批注：拆下并与之前文件一起放入信封，归入批准档案）

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别处 1938年5月24日）

目前在国际租界内运营的十七家中文广播电台，均已在工部局警务处拟定的修订版保证书表格上加盖各自印章，各电台负责人保证遵守其中所载的警务处指令。这些电台的名单连同保证书表格附后。

附件名单中最后一家电台，即位于哈特路418号、呼号X.M.H.B.、频率980千周的佛音（Fuh Ying）广播电台，曾因向广播监理处注册一事于1938年4月15日暂停运营，现已于5月20日恢复广播。需指出的是，1938年5月8日，当所有电台经理被指示提交各自电台的相关详情时，该电台管理层拒绝这样做，并表示决心停止运营（参见1938年5月10日的特别处报告）。5月23日，该电台负责人李棠（Li Sih Tang）先生在特别处总部接受问询并提交填写妥当的保证书时暗示，虽然其电台已恢复运营并提交了保证书，但他不准备签署和填写任何以广播监理处名义发出的表格。

13th May 1938.

P. A.
S. 1

New Broadcasting Stations

(a) No new Station will be established and allowed
to operate pending settlement of the present
discussions.

----------

(b) When agreement is reached Stations will not be
allowed to open until
(1) They have furnished usual guarantee re
politics as at present.
(2) They agree on two points and write a letter
accordingly:-
(A) Do not obtrude on established wave lengths.
(B) Obey Police instructions in the Settlement
if a dispute arises.

Other two points formerly included
re "Chinese Government authority" (for wave length)
"local authority if and when recognised" to be
omitted. In such cases as already exist terms will
be altered forthwith in accordance with (2) unless Stations
have been closed down.

Deputy Commissioner
(Special Branch)

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.1, Special Branch
REPORT
File No.
REC S
Shh 6813/14
Date: April 4, 1938. 38.

Subject Chinese Radio Broadcasting Stations in the Settlement.

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C. Garfao D.I

D 6813/

The number of Chinese radio broadcasting stations
in the International Settlement has increased from 19 to
20, as compared with that reported on November 30, 1937.
The Lee Lee Broadcasting Station (XHHY - 1,240 k.c.),
395 Bubbling Well Road, which closed in December, 1937,
at the request of the Japanese Military Authorities, has
resumed operations, and a new station entitled "Dah Mei"
(XHDM - 1,100 k.c.), 15 Bubbling Well Road, has recently
been established (Vide Special Branch reports 11/2/38 and
29/3/38).
The "Shanghai" Broadcasting Station (XHHS), 323
Kiangse Road, and the Hwa Mei Broadcasting Station (XHHI),
565 Nanking Road, which suspended operations in December,
1937 through lack of business, are still not functioning.
The Hwa Chiao (華僑) Broadcasting Station, Lane
1729, 5 Avenue Road (XMHC), which was a Chinese concern,
has now been registered with the U.S. Consulate.
With the exception of the Dah Mei, 15 Bubbling
Well Road, all the above mentioned stations are in receipt
of a letter from the "Supervisory Office of Radio
Broadcasting Stations," Room 316, Hardoon Building, 233
Nanking Road, informing them of the taking over of all
matters relating to supervision of radio broadcasting in
Shanghai which was formerly undertaken by the National
Government.

Sec D 6813/6

FILE
DBR.
4+

Sih Tse liang
C. D. I.
D. C. (Special Branch)

报告
档案号
REC S
Shh 6813/14
日期：1938年4月4日。38。

主题：租界内的中文广播电台。

由 特别调查员 Sih Tse-liang（音译） 制作 经由 督察长 C. Garfao 转呈

D 6813/

与国际租界内中文广播电台的数量相比，1937年11月30日报告的数字为19家，现已增至20家。位于静安寺路395号的“丽丽广播电台”（XHHY - 1,240千周），曾于1937年12月应日本军方当局要求关闭，现已恢复运营；一家名为“大美”（XHDM - 1,100千周）的新电台最近在静安寺路15号成立（参见特务科1938年2月11日和3月29日的报告）。
位于江西路323号的“上海”广播电台（XHHS）和位于南京路565号的“华美”广播电台（XHHI），因业务匮乏于1937年12月暂停运营，目前仍未恢复运作。
位于爱文义路5号1729弄的“华侨”广播电台（XMHC），原为华商机构，现已在美国领事馆注册。
除位于静安寺路15号的“大美”电台外，上述所有电台均收到一封来自“广播电台监理处”的信函，该处位于南京路233号哈同大楼316室，通知它们接管此前由国民政府负责的上海无线电广播监理的一切事宜。

Sec D 6813/6

Subject.........Chinese and semi-Chinese radio broadcasting stations
                operating in the International Settlement.
Made by D.S. Henchman           Forwarded by C Crawford. D.I

Forwarded herewith under headings "A" and "B"
respectively lists in tabulated form of radio broadcasting
stations, both government and otherwise, operating in the
International Settlement.

In connection with the Chinese Telegraph Office,
or telegraph administration as it was previously known,
it should be noted that this organ is at present not
accepting messages for inland transmission.

Letters in which an undertaking not to broadcast
anti-Japanese propaganda has been set forth, have been
obtained from the persons responsible for the operation of
the various radio stations, and are attached hereto.

D.S. Henchman

Copy will be included in tomorrow's
Intelligence Summary.
Thought S1 will continue experiments
in conjunction with C.C.R. to try & pick up
any other Stations now recorded. If successful
a further list can be published from time
to time.

D.S. Henchman
C/3.

page_data.en:
UU288
6813/14/II
13 8 37

Japanese Issue Five New
Radio Station Permits To
Increase Mix-Up On Ether

Licenses Revoked By Chinese Gov't For Poor
Equipment Are Re-Issued By Nipponese;
Congestion Again Prevails Here

Undoing the long and pains-
taking work undertaken by the
Ministry of Communications to
eliminate congestion in Shanghai's
broadcasting wave-band, the local
Japanese Radio Control Office has
recently allowed five additional
Chinese stations to go on the air,
THE CHINA PRESS learned yesterday.
The broadcasting of the five new
stations, all of which are said to be
Chinese-owned, has brought back
to Shanghai its old radio mix-up,
which the Chinese Government had
consistently tried, and to a large
extent, succeeded in remedying,
broadcasters here pointed out.

Licenses Once Revoked
Given permits by the Japanese
to broadcast were five Chinese
stations whose licenses were revoked
by the Ministry in February last
year because their equipment was
obsolete and their programs were
found to be below the required
standard.
The five broadcasters who had
applied for the Japanese permits
were said to have changed the
names and call signals of their
stations. Local broadcasting circles
stated that these stations, despite
their new names, are owned
by the same people whose licenses
were stricken off the Ministry's roll
last year.

Stations Named
The new stations registered with
the Japanese are: the Chin Ying
or the XQHK, the Yang Shih or the
XHHT, the Ta Mei or the XHHM,
the Dah Lai or the XMHJ and the
Ta Yah or the XHHC.
According to information obtained
by THE CHINA PRESS yesterday,
these five stations, together with
Station XHHE known as the Li Shu
Teh Tang, are the only local Chin-
ese broadcasters which have re-
gistered directly with the Japanese
Radio Control Office.

Stations Not Registered
Other local Chinese stations, it
was learned, have not complied with
the registration regulations pro-

mulgated by the Japanese some time
ago. These stations, however, have
submitted particulars regarding
ownership, name, wave length and
other relevant information to the
Shanghai Municipal Council.
The Japanese are believed to have
secured from the Council authori-
ties the information submitted by
the owners.
Local radio broadcasters recalled
yesterday that in January last
year, the Ministry of Communica-
tions through the Shanghai Tele-
graph Office announced that it
planned to revoke the licenses of
eight local stations.

To End Mix-Up
Ministry officials pointed out at
that time that the measure repre-
sented one of the steps the Govern-
ment was taking to end the radio
mix-up in the city.
The large number of commercial
stations in Shanghai, it was stated
at that time, was far above the re-
quirement of the city. As a result
of the congestion in the ether, the
officials stated, Shanghai radio
listeners were having a difficult
time in getting clear reception.
To pave the way toward better
broadcasting in Shanghai, eight
stations, which had failed to secure
modern equipment and to improve
their programs, were to be stricken
off the roll, the Ministry authorities
stated.

No New Permits Given
In addition, the Ministry had
consistently maintained the policy
of refusing to issue any new licenses
for broadcasting in Shanghai.
Stations, which closed down on
their own accord, were not replaced
by new stations.
Broadcasters in Shanghai pointed
out that this whole plan, aimed at
improving local broadcasting, had
been partially shattered by the
issuance of new licenses by the
Japanese.
Leading station operators believe
that as a result of the new permits
given by the Japanese, a new mush-
room growth of radio stations is
likely to appear in Shanghai.

（批：Lie
巴
S1.
R
12/8）
page_data.zh:
UU288
6813/14/II
1937年8月13日

日本颁发五张新电台执照
加剧空中电波混乱

因设备简陋被中国政府吊销的执照
由日方重新颁发；
本地再次出现拥堵状况

《字林西报》昨日获悉，当地日本无线电管理处最近允许另外五家中国电台开播，此举破坏了交通部为消除上海广播波段拥堵所进行的漫长而艰苦的工作。这里的广播界人士指出，这五家新电台据称均为中国人所有，它们的广播使上海恢复了旧的无线电混乱局面，而中国政府一直试图并在很大程度上成功 remedied（纠正）了这种局面。

执照曾被吊销
获准由日本方面广播的五家中国电台，其执照曾于去年二月被交通部吊销，原因是其设备陈旧，节目未达到规定标准。
据悉，申请日本执照的五家广播机构已更改了其电台名称和呼号。本地广播界表示，尽管这些电台使用了新名称，但其所有者与去年被从交通部名册中除名的所有者相同。

电台名称
向日方注册的新电台包括：Chin Ying (XQHK)、Yang Shih (XHHT)、Ta Mei (XHHM)、Dah Lai (XMHJ) 和 Ta Yah (XHHC)。
根据《字林西报》昨日获得的信息，这五家电台连同被称为“李树德堂”的 XHHE 电台，是唯一直接向日本无线电管理处注册的本地中国广播机构。

未注册电台
据了解，其他本地中国电台并未遵守日本方面不久前颁布的注册规定。然而，这些电台已向上海公共租界工部局提交了有关所有权、名称、波长及其他相关信息的详细资料。
据信，日本人已从工部局当局那里获得了业主提交的信息。
本地无线电广播从业者昨日回顾称，去年一月，交通部通过上海电报局宣布，计划吊销八家本地电台的执照。

旨在结束混乱
当时，交通部官员指出，该措施代表了政府为结束本市无线电混乱局面所采取的步骤之一。
当时指出，上海的商业电台数量远远超过城市需求。官员们表示，由于空中电波拥堵，上海无线电听众难以获得清晰的接收效果。
交通部当局表示，为了改善上海的广播状况，八家未能获得现代化设备并改进节目的电台将被从名册中除名。

未颁发新执照
此外，交通部一直坚持拒绝为上海的广播业务颁发任何新执照的政策。
自行关闭的电台没有由新电台取代。
上海广播界人士指出，日本人颁发新执照的行为，部分破坏了这一旨在改善本地广播的整体计划。
主要电台经营者认为，由于日本颁发了新执照，上海可能会出现电台如雨后春笋般涌现的新局面。

fwing to the suspension of operations by the
